prompt_hi: Socho, agar ek poore hafte tak gali saaf karne wale aur kooda uthane wale bhaiya na aayein, toh hamari gali ka kya haal hoga? Pehle apna guess batao.
answer: Garbage piles up, it smells, flies and mosquitoes breed and people can fall ill; their work is very important for everyone.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how people in a locality work and celebrate together
prompt: Why do people in a colony celebrate festivals like Diwali, Eid, Christmas, Gurpurab or Pongal together? What does it do for the community?
prompt_hi: Colony mein log Diwali, Eid, Christmas, Gurpurab ya Pongal saath milkar kyon manaate hain? Isse community ko kya fayda hota hai?
answer: Celebrating together helps people know and trust each other, share happiness and help each other when someone needs it.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how people in a locality work and celebrate together
prompt: Look at two pictures: (A) one family of five eating dinner at home; (B) families from a whole building meeting to fix their broken water tank. Which one shows a community working together, and what makes it different?
prompt_hi: Do picture dekho: (A) ek family ghar pe khana kha rahi hai; (B) poori building ki families milkar toota hua paani ka tank theek karwa rahi hain. Kaunsi picture community ka milkar kaam karna dikhati hai, aur kyon?
answer: B: many families who live in the same place join to solve a shared problem. A is one family; a family is only a small part of a community.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how people in a locality work and celebrate together
prompt: A school is also a kind of community. How do different people work together so your school runs every day? Give two examples.
prompt_hi: School bhi ek tarah ki community hai. Alag-alag log milkar kaise kaam karte hain taaki school roz chale? Do example batao.
answer: Each person does a different job that helps the school: teachers teach, support staff clean and ring the bell, the guard keeps the gate safe, the van or bus driver brings children, the principal plans.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how people in a locality work and celebrate together
prompt: During a heavy monsoon flood in a village, the roads are blocked for days. How could the people of the village help each other? Give two ideas.
prompt_hi: Ek gaon mein bahut baarish se baadh aa gayi aur raaste kai din band hain. Gaon ke log ek dusre ki madad kaise kar sakte hain? Do idea batao.
answer: Any two cooperative actions: share food and clean drinking water, give shelter in houses on higher ground, help elderly people and small children to safety, inform the panchayat or officials, clean drains together once the water goes down.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how people in a locality work and celebrate together
prompt: Draw a circle map: yourself in the middle, your family in the next ring, neighbours in the next, and the helpers of your locality in the outer ring. Tell me who you put in each ring.
prompt_hi: Ek circle map banao: beech mein tum, uske bahar family, phir padosi, aur sabse bahar mohalle ke helpers. Batao kis ring mein kisko rakha?
answer: Middle: me; next ring: family; then neighbours; outer ring: locality helpers such as the shopkeeper, sweeper, postman, guard, doctor and teacher. All the rings together are the community.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how people in a locality work and celebrate together
prompt: Golu says: 'Only doctors and teachers are important in a community. The sweeper and the vegetable seller don't matter.' What is wrong with what Golu said?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Community mein sirf doctor aur teacher important hain. Safai wale bhaiya aur sabzi wale uncle se koi farak nahi padta.' Golu ki baat mein galti kya hai?
answer: Every job matters: without sweepers the streets get dirty and people fall ill; without vegetable sellers it is hard to get food. People in a community depend on each other.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how people in a locality work and celebrate together
prompt: Two plans for a colony cleaning day. Plan A: all 20 people only sweep and nobody collects the garbage. Plan B: some sweep, some fill garbage bags, some carry the bags to the big dustbin. Which plan works better, and why?
prompt_hi: Colony ki safai ke do plan. Plan A: saare 20 log sirf jhaadu lagaate hain, kooda koi nahi uthata. Plan B: kuch jhaadu lagaate hain, kuch kooda bori mein bharte hain, kuch bori bade dustbin tak le jaate hain. Kaunsa plan behtar hai aur kyon?
answer: Plan B, because splitting different jobs gets the whole task done; in Plan A the swept garbage is left lying around.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how people in a locality work and celebrate together
prompt: Your little cousin Golu thinks 'community' just means 'my family'. Explain to him what a community really is, with one example from your street.
prompt_hi: Tumhara chhota cousin Golu sochta hai ki 'community' matlab bas 'meri family'. Use samjhao ki community asal mein kya hoti hai, apni gali ka ek example dekar.
answer: A community is all the people who live in a place and help and depend on each other (family, neighbours, shopkeepers, helpers), e.g. the colony planting trees or cleaning the park together.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how people in a locality work and celebrate together
prompt: Last time we talked about communities. Without looking back: what is a community, and what is one thing people do together in it?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar humne community ki baat ki thi. Bina dekhe batao: community kya hoti hai, aur log usme saath milkar kya karte hain?
answer: A group of people living in the same place who share and help each other; for example celebrating festivals, cleaning drives or planting trees together.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: Name five different ways people send a message to each other.
prompt_hi: Paanch alag-alag tareeke batao jinse log ek dusre tak message pahunchaate hain.
answer: Any five, such as talking, writing a letter, a phone call, a text message, email, gestures or hand signals, facial expressions, sign language, pictures or signboards, Braille.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: What message does each one give: a red traffic light, a finger on the lips, a thumbs-up?
prompt_hi: Batao, inka kya matlab hai: laal traffic light, hothon pe ungli, aur thumbs-up?
answer: Red light: stop. Finger on lips: be quiet. Thumbs-up: good, well done or okay.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: Your nani lives in another city. Predict which will reach her faster, a letter posted today or a phone call, and roughly how long each will take.
prompt_hi: Tumhari nani doosre shehar mein rehti hain. Guess karo: aaj post ki gayi chitthi jaldi pahunchegi ya phone call? Dono mein kitna time lagega?
answer: The phone call reaches her at once; a letter takes a few days to travel by post.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: Imagine you visit a village where nobody speaks your language and you are thirsty. Predict: can you ask for water without speaking? How?
prompt_hi: Socho tum ek aise gaon mein ho jahan koi tumhari bhasha nahi samajhta, aur tumhe pyaas lagi hai. Guess karo: kya bina bole paani maang sakte ho? Kaise?
answer: Yes, with gestures: pretend to drink from a cupped hand or a glass, or point at water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: Why do railway stations use announcements, display boards AND picture signs all together?
prompt_hi: Railway station pe announcement, display board aur picture wale sign, teeno saath kyon lagaate hain?
answer: Different people need different ways: some cannot hear well or it is too noisy, some cannot read or don't know the language. Using many ways makes sure everyone gets the message.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: Compare a letter and a phone call: give one thing a letter can do that a call can't, and one thing a call can do that a letter can't.
prompt_hi: Chitthi aur phone call ki tulna karo: ek cheez jo chitthi kar sakti hai par call nahi, aur ek jo call kar sakti hai par chitthi nahi.
answer: Letter: can be kept and read again, can carry a drawing or photo, needs no phone. Call: reaches instantly, you hear the voice and can answer back straight away.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: A friend in your class cannot hear. How could you tell them 'Let's play cricket after school'?
prompt_hi: Tumhari class mein ek dost sun nahi sakta. Use 'school ke baad cricket khelein?' kaise bataoge?
answer: Without sound: write it down, show it with gestures (batting action, point to the clock or outside), use the sign if you know it, or show a picture.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: Long ago, before phones, how could people in one village quickly warn the next village about danger? Think of things that can be seen or heard from far away.
prompt_hi: Bahut pehle, jab phone nahi the, ek gaon wale paas ke gaon ko jaldi se khatre ki khabar kaise dete honge? Socho, aisi cheezein jo door se dikhein ya sunaai dein.
answer: By loud sounds or signs seen from far: beating drums, blowing a conch or horn, ringing bells, smoke signals, or sending a fast runner or rider.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: Look at three road signs on the screen: a triangle with a walking person, a red circle with a horn crossed out, a triangle with two children carrying school bags. Tell me in words what each sign says.
prompt_hi: Screen pe teen road sign dekho: triangle mein chalta hua aadmi, laal gol ghere mein kata hua horn, aur triangle mein bag liye do bachche. Har sign kya keh raha hai, shabdon mein batao.
answer: Walking person: people crossing ahead (pedestrian crossing). Horn crossed out: no honking. Children with bags: school ahead, drive slowly.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: Golu says: 'Sign language is just people waving their hands. Anyone can understand it, and it's the same in every country.' Find the mistakes.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Sign language toh bas haath hilaana hai. Koi bhi samajh sakta hai, aur har desh mein same hoti hai.' Galtiyan pakdo.
answer: Sign language is a real language with fixed signs and rules that have to be learnt; different countries have different sign languages, such as Indian Sign Language.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: Two situations: telling your friend across a very noisy platform to come to you, and telling your aunt in Chennai that you passed your exam. Pick a good way for each. Why are they different?
prompt_hi: Do situation: shor wale platform ke us paar dost ko bulana, aur Chennai wali mausi ko batana ki tum pass ho gaye. Dono ke liye achha tareeka chuno. Dono alag kyon hain?
answer: Noisy platform: wave or point, because your friend can see you but not hear you. Chennai: phone call or message, because she is far away. The best way depends on the situation.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu how we can talk to someone without using any words. Give two examples.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin Golu ko samjhao ki bina shabdon ke kisi se baat kaise kar sakte hain. Do example do.
answer: Messages can be shared with gestures, facial expressions, signs and pictures, sign language or touch (Braille); e.g. waving goodbye, a red light meaning stop.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
prompt: Remember our talk about ways of communicating? Name two ways that use words and two ways that don't.
prompt_hi: Yaad hai communication wali baat? Do tareeke batao jinme shabd hote hain, aur do jinme nahi.
answer: With words: talking, letters, phone calls, text messages. Without words: gestures, signs or pictures, sign language, facial expressions.

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: Name four public places in or near your neighbourhood.
prompt_hi: Apne mohalle mein ya paas ki chaar public jagahon ke naam batao.
answer: Any four, such as a post office, bank, hospital or health centre, police station, school, park, market, library or ration shop.

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: Where would you go to: post a rakhi to your cousin in another city? See a doctor for fever? Report a lost bicycle?
prompt_hi: Kahan jaoge: doosre shehar mein cousin ko rakhi bhejne? Bukhaar mein doctor ko dikhane? Khoyi hui cycle ki report karne?
answer: Post office; hospital, clinic or health centre; police station.

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: A farmer needs money to buy seeds, but his crop will only be ready months later. Predict: which neighbourhood place can help him, and how?
prompt_hi: Ek kisaan ko beej khareedne ke liye paise chahiye, par fasal toh mahino baad aayegi. Guess karo: mohalle ki kaunsi jagah uski madad karegi, aur kaise?
answer: A bank: it can give him a loan now, which he pays back later with a little extra called interest.

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: Predict what the colony park will look like after a month if everyone throws wrappers there and nobody cleans it.
prompt_hi: Guess karo, agar sab log park mein wrapper phenkein aur koi saaf na kare, toh ek mahine baad park kaisa dikhega?
answer: Dirty and smelly, with flies and mosquitoes; children cannot play there and it can become unsafe. Everyone has to help keep it clean.

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: Why are places like parks, hospitals and post offices called 'public' places?
prompt_hi: Park, hospital aur post office jaisi jagahon ko 'public' jagah kyon kehte hain?
answer: Because they are for everyone to use and are not owned by one person; they are run for all the people (often by the government), so everyone must take care of them.

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: Compare a chemist shop and a hospital. What can each do for you?
prompt_hi: Chemist ki dukaan aur hospital mein kya farak hai? Dono tumhare liye kya kar sakte hain?
answer: The chemist sells medicines (the ones a doctor has written); the hospital has doctors and nurses who check you, treat you and can keep you there if you are very sick.

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: Your family has moved to a new town. Name three places you would want to find first, and say why.
prompt_hi: Tumhari family naye shehar mein shift hui hai. Teen jagah batao jo tum sabse pehle dhoondhoge, aur kyon.
answer: Any three with sensible reasons, e.g. hospital (health), school (studies), market or kirana (food), bank or ATM (money), police station (safety).

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: In a small village there is no big hospital nearby. Where might people go for health help, and what number can anyone in India call in an emergency?
prompt_hi: Ek chhote gaon mein paas mein bada hospital nahi hai. Wahan log ilaaj ke liye kahan jaate honge, aur India mein emergency mein kaunsa number milaate hain?
answer: A primary health centre (PHC) or the village health worker (ASHA didi); 112 is India's emergency number (many states also use 108 for an ambulance).

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: I'll describe a tiny map in words. Top row: school on the left, post office on the right. Bottom row: kirana on the left, park on the right. Draw it, then tell me which place is just above the park and which is just to the left of the park.
prompt_hi: Suno, ek chhota sa map shabdon mein. Upar wali line: left mein school, right mein post office. Neeche wali line: left mein kirana, right mein park. Ise banao, phir batao park ke theek upar kya hai aur park ke left mein kya hai?
answer: The post office is just above the park; the kirana is just to the left of the park.

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: Golu says: 'A bank just keeps your money locked in a big safe. That's all it does.' What did Golu miss?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Bank bas tumhare paise ek badi tijori mein band rakhta hai. Bas itna hi kaam hai.' Golu kya bhool gaya?
answer: A bank also lends money (loans) to people who need it, pays interest to savers and helps people send money; it does not just lock money away.

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu what three public places in your neighbourhood do for people.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki tumhare mohalle ki teen public jagahein logon ke liye kya karti hain.
answer: Three public places with a correct service each, e.g. the post office sends letters and parcels and keeps savings; the hospital treats sick people; the police station helps keep people safe.

subject: evs
topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
prompt: From our last talk: what can you do at a post office, other than sending a letter?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baat se: post office mein chitthi bhejne ke alawa aur kya kar sakte hain?
answer: Send parcels, keep money in a savings account, send money (money order).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: Give two reasons why people save money.
prompt_hi: Log paise kyon bachaate hain? Do kaaran batao.
answer: Any two: to buy something bigger later, for emergencies such as illness, for the future such as studies, for festivals or trips.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: You want a cricket bat that costs ₹300. If you save ₹50 every week, how many weeks will it take?
prompt_hi: Tumhe ₹300 ka cricket bat chahiye. Agar har hafte ₹50 bachao, toh kitne hafte lagenge?
answer: 6 weeks.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: You keep ₹1000 in a gullak and your brother keeps ₹1000 in a bank savings account for one year. Predict: after a year, who will have more, and why?
prompt_hi: Tum ₹1000 gullak mein rakhte ho aur tumhara bhai ₹1000 bank ke savings account mein, ek saal ke liye. Guess karo: saal ke baad kiske paas zyada honge, aur kyon?
answer: The brother: the bank adds a little interest, so he will have a bit more than ₹1000; the gullak still has exactly ₹1000.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: You deposit five ₹100 notes in a bank. A month later you withdraw ₹500. Predict: will you get the same five notes back?
prompt_hi: Tumne bank mein ₹100 ke paanch note jama kiye. Ek mahine baad ₹500 nikaale. Guess karo: kya wahi paanch note wapas milenge?
answer: Almost certainly not the same notes, but the same amount: the bank keeps a record of how much is yours, not your exact notes.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: Why might a family prefer a bank account to keeping a lot of cash in a gullak at home?
prompt_hi: Ek family ghar pe gullak mein bahut saara cash rakhne ki jagah bank account kyon pasand karegi?
answer: The money is safer from theft, loss or damage, it is recorded in their name, and it earns a little interest.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: Gullak versus savings account: tell me one good thing about each.
prompt_hi: Gullak aur savings account: dono ki ek-ek achhi baat batao.
answer: Gullak: easy, at home, good for small coins, you can see it fill up. Savings account: safe, earns interest, recorded in your name.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: Meera saves ₹20 every week. Her birthday is in 8 weeks. Will she have enough for a ₹150 book?
prompt_hi: Meera har hafte ₹20 bachaati hai. Uska birthday 8 hafte baad hai. Kya ₹150 ki kitaab ke liye paise ho jayenge?
answer: Yes: 8 × ₹20 = ₹160, which is more than ₹150, with ₹10 left over.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: A shopkeeper wants to make his shop bigger but doesn't have enough money. How can a bank help him, and how is that connected to people who save?
prompt_hi: Ek dukaandaar apni dukaan badi karna chahta hai par paise kam hain. Bank uski madad kaise karega, aur iska bachat karne walon se kya rishta hai?
answer: The bank gives him a loan from the money that savers have deposited; he pays it back over time with interest, and part of that interest is paid to savers.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: Someone phones your mother and says, 'I'm calling from your bank. Tell me your ATM PIN and the OTP.' What should your family do?
prompt_hi: Koi mummy ko phone karke kehta hai: 'Main bank se bol raha hoon, apna ATM PIN aur OTP batao.' Family ko kya karna chahiye?
answer: Never share the PIN or OTP; real banks never ask for them. Hang up, and tell a trusted adult or contact the bank on its official number.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: Here is Ravi's saving chart: Week 1 ₹10, Week 2 ₹20, Week 3 ₹10, Week 4 ₹30. Tell me in words what happened, and how much he saved in all.
prompt_hi: Ye Ravi ka saving chart hai: Hafta 1 ₹10, Hafta 2 ₹20, Hafta 3 ₹10, Hafta 4 ₹30. Shabdon mein batao kya hua, aur kul kitna bachaya?
answer: He saved a different amount each week, the most in week 4; the total is ₹70.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: Golu says: 'I have nine ₹1 coins and you have only two ₹5 coins, so I'm richer because I have more coins!' Check Golu.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Mere paas ₹1 ke nau sikke hain aur tumhare paas sirf ₹5 ke do. Mere paas zyada sikke hain, toh main ameer hoon!' Golu ko check karo.
answer: Golu has ₹9; two ₹5 coins make ₹10, so the two coins are more money. Count the value, not the number of coins.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: Two children each get ₹50 a week. Asha spends ₹30 and saves ₹20. Bunty spends all ₹50. After 5 weeks, how much has each saved? Does saving mean not spending at all?
prompt_hi: Do bachchon ko har hafte ₹50 milte hain. Asha ₹30 kharch karke ₹20 bachaati hai. Bunty poore ₹50 kharch kar deta hai. 5 hafte baad kisne kitna bachaya? Kya saving ka matlab bilkul kharch na karna hai?
answer: Asha has saved ₹100 and Bunty ₹0. Asha still spent money, so saving means keeping some aside regularly, not never spending.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu what happens to money when we put it in a bank, and why it is safe even though the bank doesn't keep our exact notes.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki bank mein paise jama karne pe unka kya hota hai, aur bank humare wahi note nahi rakhta phir bhi paise safe kyon hain.
answer: The bank writes how much is ours in our account, uses the pooled money to give loans, pays us interest, and we can take out our amount whenever we need it.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
prompt: Without looking back: name two places where we can save money, and one reason to save.
prompt_hi: Bina dekhe batao: paise bachaane ki do jagah, aur bachat ka ek kaaran.
answer: Places: a gullak (piggy bank), a bank savings account, a post office savings account. Reasons: the future, emergencies, buying something bigger.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: A parrot has a strong, curved, hooked beak. What kind of food is it good for?
prompt_hi: Tote ki chonch mazboot, mudi hui aur hook jaisi hoti hai. Ye kis tarah ka khaana khaane ke liye achhi hai?
answer: Cracking nuts and hard seeds and biting into fruits.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: Match each beak to its food. Kingfisher: long and pointed. Sparrow: short and cone-shaped. Eagle: sharp and hooked. Foods: seeds, fish, meat.
prompt_hi: Chonch ko khaane se milao. Kingfisher: lambi aur nukeeli. Gauraiya: chhoti aur cone jaisi. Cheel/baaz: tez aur mudi hui. Khaana: beej, machhli, maans.
answer: Kingfisher: fish. Sparrow: seeds. Eagle: meat (it tears flesh with its hooked beak).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: Here's a bird you may not know. It has very long thin legs and a long pointed beak, and it stands still in shallow water. Predict: what does it eat, and how does it get its food?
prompt_hi: Ek aisi chidiya dekho jo shayad tumne na dekhi ho. Uski taangein lambi-patli hain, chonch lambi aur nukeeli, aur woh kam gehre paani mein chupchaap khadi rehti hai. Guess karo: woh kya khaati hai aur kaise pakadti hai?
answer: Fish, frogs or small water animals; it stands in the water and quickly stabs or grabs them with its long beak (like a heron or egret).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: A cactus lives in a hot, dry desert. Before I show you, predict: will its leaves be big and thin like a banana leaf, or something else? Why?
prompt_hi: Cactus garam aur sookhe registaan mein rehta hai. Dikhane se pehle guess karo: kya uske patte kele ke patte jaise bade aur patle honge, ya kuch aur? Kyon?
answer: Not big thin leaves: its leaves are sharp spines and its stem is thick and fleshy, which stores water and loses very little water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: Put your hand in a bucket of water and push the water, first with your fingers spread wide apart, then with your fingers pressed together like a paddle. Predict first: which way will push more water?
prompt_hi: Paani ki baalti mein haath daalo aur paani ko dhakelo: pehle ungliyan door-door phaila ke, phir ungliyan chipka ke chappu jaisa banake. Pehle guess karo: kis tarah zyada paani dhakelega?
answer: Fingers pressed together like a paddle push more water; this is how a duck's webbed feet help it swim.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: Why does a woodpecker have a strong, chisel-like beak, and toes with two pointing forward and two backward?
prompt_hi: Kathfodwa (woodpecker) ki chonch chheni jaisi mazboot kyon hoti hai, aur uske do panje aage aur do peeche kyon hote hain?
answer: Its beak drills holes in tree bark to find insects; its toes grip the tree trunk so it can cling and climb.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: Compare a duck's feet and a hen's feet. What is different, and why?
prompt_hi: Batakh ke pair aur murgi ke pair mein kya farak hai, aur kyon?
answer: A duck has webbed feet for swimming; a hen has separate toes with claws for walking and scratching the ground for food.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: A lotus grows in ponds. Its leaves are big, round and flat, with a waxy top where water drops roll off. How does this help the lotus?
prompt_hi: Kamal talaab mein ugta hai. Uske patte bade, gol aur chapte hote hain, aur upar se mome jaise, jahan se paani ki boondein lud jaati hain. Isse kamal ko kya fayda hai?
answer: The broad flat leaves rest on or above the water and catch lots of sunlight; the waxy coat keeps water from soaking or sitting on them.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: Pine trees grow in cold, snowy mountains like those in Himachal. Their leaves are thin and needle-like. Why might needle leaves help in heavy snow?
prompt_hi: Cheed (pine) ke ped Himachal jaise thande, barfeele pahadon mein ugte hain. Unke patte patle, sui jaise hote hain. Bhaari barf mein sui jaise patte kaise madad karte honge?
answer: Snow slides off thin needles easily, so branches don't get loaded and break; needle leaves also lose less water in cold, dry winds.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: Draw (or describe) a bird that lives on water and eats fish. What beak and what feet will you give it?
prompt_hi: Ek aisi chidiya banao (ya batao) jo paani pe rehti hai aur machhli khaati hai. Usko kaisi chonch aur kaise pair doge?
answer: A beak suited to catching fish (long and pointed, or hooked at the tip) and webbed feet for swimming.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: Golu says: 'A neem tree is not a living thing. It can't walk and it doesn't eat.' Find the mistake.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Neem ka ped jeevit nahi hai. Woh chal nahi sakta aur khaata bhi nahi.' Galti pakdo.
answer: Trees are living: they grow, take in water and air, make their own food and make seeds and new plants. Living things don't have to walk.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu why a parrot and a kingfisher have different beaks.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki tote aur kingfisher ki chonch alag-alag kyon hoti hai.
answer: Beak shape matches food: the parrot's strong hooked beak cracks nuts and seeds and bites fruit; the kingfisher's long pointed beak catches fish.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
prompt: Quick memory check: what is special about a duck's feet, and what do they help it do?
prompt_hi: Chhota sa yaad karo: batakh ke pair mein kya khaas hai, aur usse kya madad milti hai?
answer: Webbed feet, which push water like paddles and help it swim.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: Sort these into plant-eaters and meat-eaters: cow, tiger, goat, eagle, rabbit, frog.
prompt_hi: Inhe ghaas-paat khaane wale aur maans khaane wale mein baanto: gaay, sher, bakri, cheel, khargosh, mendhak.
answer: Plant-eaters: cow, goat, rabbit. Meat-eaters: tiger, eagle, frog (it eats insects).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: Put these in a food chain with arrows: frog, grass, snake, grasshopper.
prompt_hi: Inko teer (arrow) laga ke food chain mein lagao: mendhak, ghaas, saanp, tidda.
answer: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: On a farm: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake. Predict: if most of the frogs disappear, what happens to the grasshoppers and to the snakes?
prompt_hi: Ek khet mein: ghaas → tidda → mendhak → saanp. Guess karo: agar zyadatar mendhak gayab ho jaayein, toh tiddon ka kya hoga, aur saanpon ka?
answer: Grasshoppers increase because fewer frogs eat them (and they may eat more grass and crops); snakes decrease or go hungry because they have less food.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: Two pots of the same sprouting moong seeds: one kept on a sunny windowsill, one inside a dark cupboard, both watered. Predict how each will look after a week.
prompt_hi: Moong ke ek jaise ankurit beej do gamle mein: ek dhoop wali khidki pe, ek andhere almari ke andar, dono ko paani milta hai. Guess karo, ek hafte baad dono kaise dikhenge?
answer: The one in the dark will be pale yellow, thin and weak (often long and floppy); the sunny one will be green and healthy. Plants need sunlight to make their food.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: Farmers kill all the snakes near their fields. Predict what might happen to the rats, and to the farmers' grain.
prompt_hi: Kisaan apne kheton ke paas saare saanp maar dete hain. Guess karo, chuhon ka kya hoga aur kisaan ke anaaj ka?
answer: Rats increase because no snakes are eating them, and they eat more of the grain; so snakes actually help farmers.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: Every food chain starts with a plant. Why?
prompt_hi: Har food chain paudhe se hi kyon shuru hoti hai?
answer: Plants make their own food from sunlight, water and air; animals cannot make food, so they eat plants or animals that ate plants.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: Compare a cow's teeth and a tiger's teeth. How does each match what the animal eats?
prompt_hi: Gaay ke daant aur sher ke daant ki tulna karo. Dono ke daant unke khaane se kaise milte hain?
answer: A cow has broad flat teeth for grinding grass; a tiger has sharp pointed teeth for gripping and tearing meat.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: Make a food chain from a pond using: small fish, kingfisher, tiny water plants (algae), mosquito larvae.
prompt_hi: Talaab ki food chain banao: chhoti machhli, kingfisher, paani ke chhote paudhe (kaai), machhar ke laarva.
answer: tiny water plants (algae) → mosquito larvae → small fish → kingfisher

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: Bees seem small, and some people only think of them as insects that sting. What would happen to fruit trees and vegetable plants, and to us, if all the bees disappeared?
prompt_hi: Madhumakkhi chhoti si lagti hai, aur kuch log bas sochte hain ki woh kaat-ti hai. Agar saari madhumakkhiyan gayab ho jaayein, toh phal ke pedon, sabziyon aur humare saath kya hoga?
answer: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower (pollination), so without them many flowers would not turn into fruits and seeds; we would get fewer fruits and vegetables. Small animals matter.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: Say this food chain in words using 'is eaten by': grass → deer → tiger.
prompt_hi: Is food chain ko 'ko ... khaata hai' ya 'is eaten by' lagakar shabdon mein bolo: ghaas → hiran → sher.
answer: Grass is eaten by the deer, and the deer is eaten by the tiger.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: Golu drew: snake → frog → grasshopper → grass, and says 'the arrow means eats'. Fix Golu's chain.
prompt_hi: Golu ne banaya: saanp → mendhak → tidda → ghaas, aur kehta hai 'teer ka matlab hai khaata hai'. Golu ki chain theek karo.
answer: Arrows go from the food to the eater: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake. The arrow means 'is eaten by'.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu why a farm needs plants, insects, frogs AND snakes, and where the plants get their food.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki khet ko paudhe, keede, mendhak AUR saanp, sabki zaroorat kyon hai, aur paudhon ko khaana kahan se milta hai.
answer: Plants make their own food using sunlight, water and air; insects eat plants, frogs eat insects, snakes eat frogs and rats; each keeps the others in balance, so removing one upsets the chain.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
prompt: From last time, finish this chain: grass → grasshopper → ___ → snake.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar wali chain poori karo: ghaas → tidda → ___ → saanp.
answer: frog

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: Name one community or movement in India known for protecting trees.
prompt_hi: India ki koi ek community ya andolan batao jo pedon ko bachaane ke liye jaana jaata hai.
answer: The Bishnoi community of Rajasthan, the Chipko movement of Uttarakhand, or villages that keep sacred groves.

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: What is a sacred grove?
prompt_hi: Sacred grove (pavitra van) kya hota hai?
answer: A patch of forest that a village protects and does not cut, often linked to a local deity; the plants and animals there are left safe.

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: A hill has two sides: one side has a thick sacred grove, the other side's trees were all cut. Predict: after heavy rain, which side loses more soil, and near which side will a spring keep flowing longer into the dry months?
prompt_hi: Ek pahaadi ke do taraf hain: ek taraf ghana sacred grove, doosri taraf saare ped kaat diye gaye. Guess karo: bhaari baarish ke baad kis taraf zyada mitti bahegi, aur kis taraf ka jharna sookhe mahino tak zyada der chalega?
answer: The bare side loses more soil because nothing holds it; the spring near the grove keeps flowing longer because roots hold the soil and help rainwater soak into the ground slowly.

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: Two jars of stored wheat are kept for a few months: one with dry neem leaves mixed in, one without. Predict which jar will have fewer insects.
prompt_hi: Gehun ke do dibbe kuch mahino ke liye rakhe hain: ek mein sookhe neem ke patte mile hain, ek mein nahi. Guess karo kis dibbe mein keede kam honge?
answer: The jar with neem leaves; neem helps keep insects away.

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: Why did the people in the Chipko movement hug trees?
prompt_hi: Chipko andolan mein log pedon se kyon chipak gaye the?
answer: To stop the trees from being cut: by holding the trees they stood between the axe and the tree, because the forest gave them fuel, fodder and water and held the soil.

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: Compare what a village gets from one mango tree that stands for 20 years with what it gets if the tree is cut down once for wood.
prompt_hi: Ek aam ka ped jo 20 saal khada rahe, aur wahi ped ek baar lakdi ke liye kaat diya jaaye: gaon ko dono mein kya-kya milta hai?
answer: Standing: fruit every year, shade, homes for birds and insects, soil held in place, cleaner air. Cut: wood only once. A standing tree usually gives far more.

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: Bishnoi people protect blackbuck and khejri trees. Think of one thing your family or colony could do in the same spirit.
prompt_hi: Bishnoi log kaale hiran aur khejri ke pedon ki raksha karte hain. Isi soch se tumhari family ya colony kya kar sakti hai? Ek cheez batao.
answer: Any sensible protective action, e.g. not cutting trees, planting and caring for saplings, keeping water bowls for birds in summer, not plucking flowers in parks, saving water.

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: In many old towns of Rajasthan people built stepwells (baoris) and stored rainwater. Why was that smart in a dry place, and how is it like rainwater harvesting today?
prompt_hi: Rajasthan ke kai purane shehron mein log baori (stepwell) banate the aur baarish ka paani jama karte the. Sookhi jagah mein ye samajhdaari kyon thi, aur aaj ke rainwater harvesting se ye kaise milta hai?
answer: Rain falls rarely there, so storing it gives water for the long dry months; today's rainwater harvesting also collects rain from roofs into tanks or into the ground for later.

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: Look at this timeline picture: about 300 years ago, Khejarli villagers stand up to save khejri trees; 1973, Chipko people hug trees; today, villages still protect sacred groves. Tell the story in your own words, in order.
prompt_hi: Ye timeline picture dekho: lagbhag 300 saal pehle Khejarli ke gaon wale khejri ke pedon ko bachaane khade hue; 1973 mein Chipko ke log pedon se chipke; aaj bhi gaon sacred grove bachaate hain. Apne shabdon mein kram se kahani sunao.
answer: Long ago the Bishnoi villagers of Khejarli stood up to protect khejri trees; in 1973 the Chipko people hugged trees to stop cutting; today villages still protect sacred groves. People have protected forests for a very long time.

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: Golu says: 'Old ways like keeping neem in grain or storing rainwater are just superstitions. Science has nothing to learn from them.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Anaaj mein neem rakhna ya baarish ka paani jama karna, ye sab purane andhvishwas hain. Science inse kuch nahi seekh sakta.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Many traditional practices work for real reasons that science can explain (neem keeps insects away; stored rainwater gives water in dry months); we can learn from them and test them.

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu what a sacred grove is and how it helps animals, plants and water.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki sacred grove kya hota hai aur woh jaanwaron, paudhon aur paani ki madad kaise karta hai.
answer: A sacred grove is forest a village protects and never cuts; animals and birds live there safely, many plants survive, roots hold the soil and water soaks in to keep springs flowing.

subject: evs
topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
prompt: From last time: what did the people in the Chipko movement do, and why?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Chipko andolan mein logon ne kya kiya tha, aur kyon?
answer: They hugged trees to stop them from being cut down.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: Name one plant part we eat that is a root, one that is a stem, and one that is a leaf.
prompt_hi: Ek aisi cheez batao jo hum jad (root) ke roop mein khaate hain, ek tana (stem), aur ek patta.
answer: Root: carrot, radish or beetroot. Stem: sugarcane or potato (an underground stem). Leaf: spinach, methi or cabbage.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: Name a plant used for each: making rope, making a roof, making a basket.
prompt_hi: Har kaam ke liye ek paudha batao: rassi banane ke liye, chhat banane ke liye, tokri banane ke liye.
answer: Rope: jute or coconut coir. Roof: bamboo, palm leaves, thatch grass or wood. Basket: bamboo or cane.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: Bury a piece of banana leaf and a piece of plastic plate in a pot of moist soil. Predict what each will look like after a month.
prompt_hi: Ek gamle ki geeli mitti mein kele ke patte ka tukda aur plastic plate ka tukda daba do. Guess karo, ek mahine baad dono kaise dikhenge?
answer: The banana leaf will have started to rot and break into the soil; the plastic will look almost the same.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: Before we look around: predict how many things in your room came from plants, a few or lots? Now find three and tell me which plant each came from.
prompt_hi: Idhar-udhar dekhne se pehle guess karo: tumhare kamre mein kitni cheezein paudhon se aayi hain, thodi ya bahut saari? Ab teen dhoondho aur batao kis paudhe se aayi.
answer: Usually lots: e.g. a wooden table or door (trees), cotton bedsheet or clothes (cotton plant), paper books (wood pulp), a jute mat (jute plant).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: Why do many people in India use a neem twig (datun) to clean their teeth?
prompt_hi: India mein bahut log daant saaf karne ke liye neem ki datun kyon use karte hain?
answer: Chewing the twig makes a soft brush that scrubs the teeth, and neem has bitter substances that people have long used to help keep the mouth clean and fight germs.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: Compare a banana-leaf plate and a plastic plate after a wedding feast. What happens to each after it is thrown away?
prompt_hi: Shaadi ki daawat ke baad kele ke patte ki plate aur plastic ki plate ki tulna karo. Phenkne ke baad dono ka kya hota hai?
answer: The banana leaf rots and mixes into the soil (or is eaten by cattle); the plastic plate stays for hundreds of years and pollutes soil and water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: Look at your lunch thali: name each item and the plant or plant part it came from.
prompt_hi: Apni lunch ki thali dekho: har cheez ka naam batao aur woh kis paudhe ya paudhe ke kis hisse se aayi.
answer: e.g. roti: wheat seeds (grains); rice: rice seeds; dal: pulse seeds; aloo: potato, an underground stem; salt: not from a plant.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: Think about a cricket match. Which things in it come from plants?
prompt_hi: Ek cricket match ke baare mein socho. Usme kaun-kaun si cheezein paudhon se aati hain?
answer: The bat (willow wood), the wooden stumps and bails, cotton clothes, the grass of the field, and the cork inside the ball (from cork tree bark).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: Here is a picture of a plant with labels: root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit. For each part, name one food we eat from that part.
prompt_hi: Ek paudhe ki picture hai jisme likha hai: jad, tana, patta, phool, phal. Har hisse ke liye ek khaane ki cheez batao jo hum us hisse se khaate hain.
answer: Root: carrot. Stem: sugarcane. Leaf: spinach. Flower: cauliflower. Fruit: mango or tomato.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: Golu says: 'All plants are natural, so any berry or leaf in the park is safe to eat.' What is the mistake, and what is the safe rule?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Saare paudhe natural hain, toh park ka koi bhi ber ya patta khaana safe hai.' Galti kya hai, aur safe rule kya hai?
answer: Some plants and berries are poisonous; 'natural' does not mean 'safe'. Never taste an unknown plant; always ask an adult first.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu four different ways we use plants, with one example each.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki hum paudhon ka chaar alag tareekon se kaise use karte hain, har ek ka ek example dekar.
answer: Food (wheat, dal, fruits), medicine (tulsi or neem in home remedies; quinine from cinchona), shelter (bamboo, wood, thatch) and craft or clothes (jute, cotton, cane).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
prompt: From last time: name one plant used for medicine and one used to build a house.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek paudha jo dawai mein kaam aata hai, aur ek jo ghar banane mein.
answer: Medicine: tulsi, neem, haldi or cinchona. House: bamboo, wood or thatch grass.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: Sort into energy-giving, body-building and protective: rice, dal, spinach, paneer, guava, roti.
prompt_hi: Inhe energy dene wale, body banane wale aur bachaane wale (protective) khaane mein baanto: chawal, dal, palak, paneer, amrood, roti.
answer: Energy-giving: rice, roti. Body-building: dal, paneer. Protective: spinach, guava.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: Your thali has roti, aloo sabzi and rice. Which food groups are missing or too small, and what could you add?
prompt_hi: Tumhari thali mein roti, aloo ki sabzi aur chawal hai. Kaunse food group missing ya kam hain, aur kya jod sakte ho?
answer: It is almost all energy food; body-building food is missing (add dal, curd or paneer) and protective food is too little (add a green vegetable, salad or fruit).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: Chew a small piece of plain roti slowly for about a minute without swallowing. Predict first: will the taste change?
prompt_hi: Saadi roti ka chhota tukda bina nigle lagbhag ek minute dheere-dheere chabao. Pehle guess karo: kya swaad badlega?
answer: Yes, it starts to taste slightly sweet: saliva begins changing the starch in roti (an energy food) into sugar.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: Predict: if a child eats only rice and potatoes every day for months, with no dal, milk, fruits or vegetables, will they stay healthy? What might happen?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar koi bachcha mahino tak roz sirf chawal aur aloo khaaye, dal, doodh, phal ya sabzi bilkul nahi, toh kya woh healthy rahega? Kya ho sakta hai?
answer: No: they would get energy but not enough body-building and protective food, so they may grow slowly, feel weak and fall sick more often.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: Why do we need protective foods like fruits and vegetables, even though they don't give much energy?
prompt_hi: Phal aur sabziyan zyada energy nahi deti, phir bhi hume inki zaroorat kyon hai?
answer: They have vitamins and minerals that keep body parts working and help fight illness, and fibre that helps digestion.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: Compare two snacks: a bowl of roasted chana with an apple, and a packet of chips with a cold drink. Both taste good. Which helps your body more, and why?
prompt_hi: Do snack ki tulna karo: bhune chane ki katori ke saath ek seb, aur chips ka packet ke saath cold drink. Dono swaadisht hain. Body ki zyada madad kaun karta hai, aur kyon?
answer: Roasted chana and an apple: body-building food, fibre and vitamins. Chips and a cold drink: lots of salt, fat and sugar with little else.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: Plan a balanced breakfast for the morning of a cricket match, using foods from your home.
prompt_hi: Cricket match wali subah ke liye ghar ki cheezon se ek balanced naashta plan karo.
answer: Any breakfast with energy food (poha, paratha, roti, idli, upma), body-building food (milk, curd, egg, sprouts, dal) and protective food (fruit or vegetables), plus water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: A family on the Kerala coast eats rice, fish curry and a vegetable thoran. A family in Punjab eats roti, rajma and saag with lassi. Are both meals balanced? Explain.
prompt_hi: Kerala ke samandar kinare ek family chawal, machhli ki curry aur sabzi ka thoran khaati hai. Punjab mein ek family roti, rajma, saag aur lassi khaati hai. Kya dono meal balanced hain? Samjhao.
answer: Yes, both: rice or roti give energy; fish, rajma and lassi build the body; the vegetable thoran and saag protect. Balanced meals can look different in different places.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: Here is a plate picture: half is vegetables and fruits, a quarter is roti or rice, a quarter is dal or paneer, with a glass of water. Describe in words what this plate tells us to eat.
prompt_hi: Ek plate ki picture hai: aadhi plate mein sabziyan aur phal, ek chauthai mein roti ya chawal, ek chauthai mein dal ya paneer, aur ek glass paani. Shabdon mein batao ye plate humein kya khaane ko kehti hai.
answer: Eat lots of vegetables and fruits (half the plate), some grains for energy (a quarter), some body-building food (a quarter), and drink water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: Golu says: 'Ghee and nuts have fat, so they are poison. Never eat them.' Fix Golu's idea.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Ghee aur nuts mein fat hota hai, toh ye zeher hain. Kabhi mat khao.' Golu ki soch theek karo.
answer: The body needs a small amount of fat for energy and growth; the problem is eating too much, like lots of fried food.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu the three jobs food does in our body, with one food for each.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki khaana humare body mein teen kaam karta hai, har kaam ke liye ek khaane ka example dekar.
answer: Energy-giving (roti or rice) gives energy; body-building (dal, milk or paneer) helps us grow and repair; protective (fruits and vegetables) keeps us healthy and fights illness.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
prompt: From last time: name two body-building foods a vegetarian child can eat.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: do body-building khaane batao jo shakahari bachcha kha sakta hai.
answer: Any two of: dal, paneer, milk, curd, chana, soybean, rajma.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: Which of these are junk food: chips, roasted chana, cold drink, banana, instant noodles, sprouts chaat?
prompt_hi: Inmein se junk food kaunse hain: chips, bhune chane, cold drink, kela, instant noodles, sprouts chaat?
answer: Junk: chips, cold drink, instant noodles. Healthy: roasted chana, banana, sprouts chaat.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: Give one food for each taste: sweet, salty, sour, bitter.
prompt_hi: Har swaad ke liye ek khaana batao: meetha, namkeen, khatta, kadwa.
answer: Sweet: gur or mango. Salty: namkeen or salted peanuts. Sour: lemon, imli or curd. Bitter: karela or methi seeds.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: Press a potato chip on a piece of plain paper for a minute, and do the same with a slice of raw cucumber. Predict: what will you see on the paper after you lift each one and wait a while?
prompt_hi: Saade kaagaz pe ek chips ko ek minute dabao, aur phir kheere ke ek tukde ko. Guess karo: dono hata ke thodi der baad kaagaz pe kya dikhega?
answer: The chip leaves an oily, see-through spot that does not dry away; the cucumber leaves a wet spot that dries. The chips have a lot of fat (oil).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: Put a few grains of sugar on the side of your tongue, not the tip. Predict first: will you taste sweet there?
prompt_hi: Cheeni ke kuch daane zubaan ke side pe rakho, tip pe nahi. Pehle guess karo: kya wahan meetha lagega?
answer: Yes: the sides of the tongue can taste sweet too; all parts of the tongue can sense all tastes.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: Shake a sealed packet of chips without opening it. Predict: is the packet full of chips? What fills the rest?
prompt_hi: Chips ka band packet bina khole hilao. Guess karo: kya packet chips se bhara hai? Baaki jagah mein kya hai?
answer: No: a lot of the space is gas (nitrogen) that is put in to keep the chips fresh and stop them from breaking, so there are fewer chips than the packet size suggests.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: Why is it okay to eat junk food only once in a while, not every day?
prompt_hi: Junk food kabhi-kabhi theek hai, par roz nahi. Aisa kyon?
answer: It has too much salt, sugar and fat and very little body-building or protective food; eaten often it can cause weight gain, tooth decay, tiredness and illness, and leaves less room for healthy food.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: Compare a whole orange and a glass of packaged orange drink. Which keeps you full longer, and which has fibre?
prompt_hi: Ek poora santra aur ek glass packet wali orange drink ki tulna karo. Kaun zyada der tak pet bhara rakhta hai, aur kismein fibre hai?
answer: The whole orange: it has fibre, which fills you up and helps digestion; the drink has little fibre and often added sugar.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: A juice pack's ingredients say: 'Water, sugar, mango pulp (10%), ...'. What is in it the most, and is it mostly fruit?
prompt_hi: Ek juice pack pe ingredients likhe hain: 'Paani, cheeni, aam ka pulp (10%), ...'. Isme sabse zyada kya hai, aur kya ye zyadatar phal hai?
answer: Mostly water, then sugar; only 10% is mango. It is mostly sugary water, not fruit.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: Your class is planning snacks for a school trip. Suggest tasty swaps for chips, cold drinks and cream biscuits.
prompt_hi: Tumhari class school trip ke liye snacks plan kar rahi hai. Chips, cold drink aur cream biscuit ki jagah kuch swaadisht swap batao.
answer: e.g. roasted chana, makhana or peanuts instead of chips; nimbu paani, chaas or water instead of cold drinks; fruit or a homemade laddoo instead of cream biscuits.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: This bar chart shows teaspoons of ADDED sugar: a 300 ml can of cold drink about 8, a glass of plain milk 0, a fresh orange 0. Tell me in words what the chart shows.
prompt_hi: Ye bar chart ADDED cheeni ke chammach dikhata hai: 300 ml ki ek can cold drink mein lagbhag 8, ek glass saade doodh mein 0, ek taaze santre mein 0. Shabdon mein batao chart kya keh raha hai.
answer: The cold drink has about 8 teaspoons of added sugar; plain milk and a fresh orange have no added sugar, so the cold drink adds a lot of sugar.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: Golu says: 'This biscuit packet shows fresh milk and wheat fields, so it must be healthy.' Fix his thinking.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Is biscuit ke packet pe taaza doodh aur gehun ke khet ki photo hai, toh ye healthy hi hoga.' Uski soch theek karo.
answer: Pictures prove nothing; read the label and check the first ingredients and how much sugar, salt and fat it has.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu how to tell whether a packet food is junk food.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki kaise pata karein ki packet wala khaana junk food hai ya nahi.
answer: Read the label: if sugar, salt or fat is high and near the top of the ingredients, with little fibre or real food, it is junk; eat it only rarely and choose fresh food more.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
prompt: From last time: why is a fresh fruit better than packaged juice?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: taaza phal packet wale juice se behtar kyon hai?
answer: Fresh fruit has fibre and no added sugar; packaged juice often has added sugar and little fibre.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: About how many hours of sleep does a child of your age need each night?
prompt_hi: Tumhari umar ke bachche ko har raat lagbhag kitne ghante sona chahiye?
answer: About 9 to 12 hours.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: Name four feelings people can have.
prompt_hi: Chaar feelings ke naam batao jo log mehsoos karte hain.
answer: Any four, such as happy, sad, angry, scared, worried, excited, surprised, shy, proud.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: Sit still and put your hand on your chest to feel your heartbeat. Then do 20 jumping jacks on a clear, open floor. Predict first: will your heartbeat be faster, slower or the same after jumping?
prompt_hi: Chupchaap baith ke seene pe haath rakho aur dhadkan mehsoos karo. Phir khuli, saaf jagah pe 20 jumping jacks karo. Pehle guess karo: jumping ke baad dhadkan tez hogi, dheemi, ya waisi hi?
answer: Faster: exercise makes the heart pump faster to send more blood and air to the working muscles.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: Two children have a test the next morning. One sleeps at 9:30 pm; the other watches a phone till midnight. Predict who will remember answers better and feel fresher.
prompt_hi: Do bachchon ka agle din test hai. Ek raat 9:30 baje so jaata hai, doosra aadhi raat tak phone dekhta hai. Guess karo, kise jawab zyada yaad rahenge aur kaun fresh mehsoos karega?
answer: The one who slept at 9:30: good sleep helps the brain store what was learnt and keeps you alert.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: Predict: if you watch a bright phone screen right before bed, will you fall asleep faster or slower?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: sone se theek pehle chamakti phone screen dekhoge, toh neend jaldi aayegi ya der se?
answer: Slower: bright screens and exciting videos keep the brain awake.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: Why does playing outside every day help both your body and your mind?
prompt_hi: Roz bahar khelna body aur mann dono ke liye achha kyon hai?
answer: Body: muscles and bones get stronger and the heart and lungs work well. Mind: you feel happier and calmer, sleep better and make friends.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: Compare how you feel in the morning after a full night's sleep and after sleeping very late. What is different?
prompt_hi: Poori neend lene ke baad subah kaisa lagta hai, aur bahut der se sone ke baad kaisa? Kya farak hai?
answer: After full sleep: fresh, energetic, able to focus. After a late night: sleepy, cranky, hard to focus, forgetful.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: Your best friend didn't get picked for the cricket team and is very upset. What could you say or do to help?
prompt_hi: Tumhare best friend ka cricket team mein selection nahi hua aur woh bahut udaas hai. Tum kya keh ya kar sakte ho jisse madad ho?
answer: Listen, tell them it's okay to feel sad, stay with them or play together, remind them they can practise and try again, and suggest talking to a parent or coach.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: Your dadaji says he feels stiff and tired after sitting all day. Using what you know about exercise, what would you suggest, and why?
prompt_hi: Dadaji kehte hain ki din bhar baithne se unka sharir akad jaata hai aur thakaan lagti hai. Exercise ke baare mein jo jaante ho, uske hisaab se kya suggest karoge, aur kyon?
answer: Gentle daily movement, like a walk or light yoga that his doctor says is fine, keeps the muscles and joints moving and the heart healthy, so he feels less stiff and fresher.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: Here is Riya's sleep chart: Monday 10 hours, Tuesday 7, Wednesday 10, Thursday 6, Friday 10. Which days did she probably feel tired, and why?
prompt_hi: Ye Riya ka sleep chart hai: Somvaar 10 ghante, Mangalvaar 7, Budhvaar 10, Guruvaar 6, Shukravaar 10. Kis din use shayad thakaan lagi hogi, aur kyon?
answer: Tuesday and Thursday, because she slept much less than the 9 to 12 hours a child needs.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: Golu says: 'If you feel sad, it means something is wrong with you. Good children are always happy.' What's wrong with that?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Agar tum udaas ho, toh tumme kuch gadbad hai. Achhe bachche hamesha khush rehte hain.' Isme kya galat hai?
answer: Everyone feels sad sometimes; it is normal and it passes. Talking to someone you trust helps.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu why he should go to bed on time. Give two reasons.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki use time pe kyon sona chahiye. Do kaaran do.
answer: While we sleep the body grows and repairs and the brain stores what we learnt; with enough sleep we feel fresh and can play and learn better.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
prompt: From last time: when you feel worried, who are two people you could talk to?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jab tumhe chinta ho, toh kin do logon se baat kar sakte ho?
answer: Any two trusted people, such as a parent, a grandparent, an older brother or sister, a class teacher or a good friend.

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: Put these steps in order: grinding into atta, harvesting, sowing seeds, making roti, threshing.
prompt_hi: In steps ko sahi kram mein lagao: atta peesna, fasal kaatna, beej bona, roti banana, gehun ke daane alag karna (thresher).
answer: sowing seeds → harvesting → threshing → grinding into atta → making roti

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: Name three people whose work helps a roti reach your plate.
prompt_hi: Teen logon ke naam batao jinki mehnat se roti tumhari thali tak pahunchti hai.
answer: Any three: farmer, farm labourer, truck driver, shopkeeper, chakki-wala (miller), the person who cooks.

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: A wheat field needs a lot of water to grow. Predict: if we throw away one roti, what else gets wasted besides the roti?
prompt_hi: Gehun ke khet ko ugne mein bahut paani lagta hai. Guess karo: agar hum ek roti phenk dein, toh roti ke alawa aur kya-kya bekaar jaata hai?
answer: The water, soil and seeds used to grow the wheat, the farmer's work, the fuel used to transport and grind it, and the gas and effort used to cook it.

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: Mix a handful of wheat or rice grains with some tiny dry bits of paper on a plate. Gently blow across the plate. Predict first: what will fly off and what will stay?
prompt_hi: Ek plate mein mutthi bhar gehun ya chawal ke daane aur kaagaz ke bahut chhote sookhe tukde mila do. Plate ke upar se dheere se phoonko. Pehle guess karo: kya ud jayega aur kya rahega?
answer: The light paper bits fly off and the heavier grains stay; farmers separate light husk from grain with wind in the same way (winnowing).

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: Why do farmers thresh and winnow wheat after harvesting it?
prompt_hi: Fasal kaatne ke baad kisaan gehun ko thresh aur winnow (phatakna) kyon karte hain?
answer: Threshing separates the grains from the stalks and ears; winnowing uses wind to blow away the light husk so only clean grain is left.

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: Two leftovers: (A) rice cooked last night, cooled and kept covered in the fridge; (B) dal left on the kitchen counter for two hot days that smells sour. Which can be used, and why?
prompt_hi: Do bache hue khaane: (A) kal raat ka chawal, thanda karke dhak ke fridge mein rakha; (B) do garam din tak counter pe padi dal jisme khatti badboo hai. Kaunsa use kar sakte hain, aur kyon?
answer: A can be used soon (stored safely; heat it well). B has spoiled and must not be eaten.

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: Rice also travels from field to plate. Fill in the missing step: paddy is grown → harvested → threshed → ___ (husk removed) → packed → cooked.
prompt_hi: Chawal bhi khet se thali tak aata hai. Khaali step bharo: dhaan ugaaya → kaata → daane alag kiye → ___ (chhilka hataaya) → pack kiya → pakaaya.
answer: Milling at a rice mill, where the husk is removed.

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: At a big wedding feast lots of food gets left over. Suggest two good ways to stop it going to waste.
prompt_hi: Badi shaadi ki daawat mein bahut khaana bach jaata hai. Ise bekaar hone se bachaane ke do achhe tareeke batao.
answer: Any two: serve smaller helpings and let people take only what they can eat; with adults, safely share good untouched food with others (food-sharing groups); compost peels and scraps.

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: Look at this picture strip of six boxes: seeds in soil, green plants, golden plants being cut, grains being separated, a chakki, a roti on a tawa. Tell the story of the roti in words.
prompt_hi: Ye chhe dabbon wali picture strip dekho: mitti mein beej, hare paudhe, sunehri fasal ki katai, daane alag hote hue, chakki, tawe pe roti. Roti ki kahani shabdon mein sunao.
answer: Seeds were sown, they grew into wheat plants, the ripe wheat was harvested, the grains were separated by threshing, ground into atta at the chakki, and the atta was made into roti.

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: Golu says: 'The kirana shop makes atta in the back of the shop. Farmers have nothing to do with it.' Fix Golu.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Kirana wale dukaan ke peeche atta banate hain. Kisaan ka isse koi lena-dena nahi.' Golu ko theek karo.
answer: Farmers grow the wheat; it is harvested, threshed, cleaned and ground at a mill or chakki; the shop only sells the atta.

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu why we shouldn't waste food, and give two safe ways to use leftovers.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki khaana kyon bekaar nahi karna chahiye, aur bache khaane ko use karne ke do safe tareeke batao.
answer: Food carries the work of many people plus water, land and fuel; take only what you can eat; turn safely stored leftovers into new dishes (lemon rice, roti upma, dal paratha); never eat spoiled food.

subject: evs
topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
prompt: From last time: what happens at the chakki?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: chakki mein kya hota hai?
answer: Wheat grains are ground into flour (atta).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: Which of these float in water and which sink: a steel spoon, a plastic bottle cap, a coin, a dry leaf, a stone, a piece of wood?
prompt_hi: Inmein se kya paani pe tairega aur kya doobega: steel ka chammach, plastic ki bottle ka dhakkan, sikka, sookha patta, patthar, lakdi ka tukda?
answer: Float: plastic bottle cap, dry leaf, wood. Sink: steel spoon, coin, stone.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: A big watermelon is much heavier than a small coin. Predict: which one will float in a big tub of water?
prompt_hi: Bada tarbooz chhote sikke se kahin zyada bhaari hai. Guess karo: paani ke bade tub mein kaun tairega?
answer: The watermelon floats; the coin sinks.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: Roll some modelling clay into a tight ball and put it in water: it sinks. Predict: if you press the same clay into a thin bowl or boat shape and place it gently on the water, will it float?
prompt_hi: Modelling clay ki kas ke goli banao aur paani mein daalo: woh doob jaati hai. Guess karo: agar usi clay ko daba ke patli katori ya naav bana do aur dheere se paani pe rakho, toh kya tairegi?
answer: Yes, it can float: the boat shape pushes aside more water, so the water's upward push is enough to hold it up.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: Put an orange with its peel on into water, then the same orange after peeling it. Predict which one floats.
prompt_hi: Chhilke wala santra paani mein daalo, phir wahi santra chheel ke daalo. Guess karo kaun tairega.
answer: The orange with its peel floats; the peeled orange sinks. The peel is full of tiny air pockets that help it float.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: A potato sinks in a glass of tap water. Predict: if we stir lots and lots of salt (many spoons) into the water, what will happen to the potato?
prompt_hi: Aloo saade paani ke glass mein doob jaata hai. Guess karo: agar us paani mein bahut saara namak (kai chammach) ghol dein, toh aloo ka kya hoga?
answer: It can float: very salty water pushes up harder than plain water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: Why does a huge iron ship float while a tiny iron nail sinks?
prompt_hi: Bahut bada lohe ka jahaaz tairta hai, par chhoti si lohe ki keel doob jaati hai. Aisa kyon?
answer: The ship is hollow, shaped like a giant bowl and full of air, so it pushes aside a huge amount of water and the water's upward push holds it up; the nail is solid and pushes aside only a little water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: A steel katori placed upright floats on water, but a steel spoon sinks. Both are steel. What is different?
prompt_hi: Steel ki katori seedhi rakhne pe paani pe tairti hai, par steel ka chammach doob jaata hai. Dono steel ke hain. Farak kya hai?
answer: The katori's hollow bowl shape pushes aside lots of water and holds air; the spoon is thin and solid and pushes aside very little water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: Fishing boats in Kerala are often made of wood, but big cargo ships are made of steel. How can a steel boat float?
prompt_hi: Kerala ki machhli pakadne wali naavein aksar lakdi ki hoti hain, par bade cargo jahaaz steel ke. Steel ki naav kaise tairti hai?
answer: It is shaped hollow like a bowl, so it pushes aside a lot of water and floats, just like the clay boat.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: People say it is easier to float in the sea than in a river or swimming pool. Why might that be?
prompt_hi: Log kehte hain ki samandar mein nadi ya swimming pool se zyada aasaani se tair-te hain. Aisa kyon ho sakta hai?
answer: Sea water is salty, and salty water pushes up harder, so we float more easily.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
