prompt: Look at this picture of two tubs with the same lump of clay: in tub A it is a ball at the bottom; in tub B it is a boat floating. In which tub has the water level risen more? Say it in words.
prompt_hi: Ye picture dekho, do tub mein ek jaisi clay: tub A mein goli neeche padi hai, tub B mein naav tair rahi hai. Kis tub mein paani ka level zyada upar aaya? Shabdon mein batao.
answer: Tub B: the floating boat pushes aside more water, so the water level rises more.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: When you push an empty, closed bottle under water, you feel it pushing back on your hand, and when you let go it jumps up. What is pushing it?
prompt_hi: Jab khaali band bottle ko paani mein neeche dabaate ho, toh woh haath ko wapas dhakelti hai, aur chhodte hi upar uchhal aati hai. Use kaun dhakel raha hai?
answer: The water is pushing up on the bottle; the bottle is very light for its size, so the water's upward push is bigger than its weight.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: Golu says: 'Heavy things sink and light things float. That's the rule!' Give one example that breaks Golu's rule.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Bhaari cheezein doobti hain aur halki tairti hain. Yahi rule hai!' Ek example do jo Golu ka rule tod de.
answer: A heavy log, watermelon or ship floats; a light coin, pin or pebble sinks. Weight alone doesn't decide.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu how a boat made of clay can float even though a ball of the same clay sinks.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki clay ki naav kaise tair sakti hai jabki usi clay ki goli doob jaati hai.
answer: It is the same clay with the same weight, but the hollow boat shape pushes aside much more water; water pushes up on it more, enough to hold it up.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
prompt: From last time: name one heavy thing that floats and one light thing that sinks.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek bhaari cheez batao jo tairti hai, aur ek halki jo doobti hai.
answer: Heavy that floats: a log, a watermelon, a ship, a coconut. Light that sinks: a coin, a pin, a pebble, a nail.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: What pushes or pulls each of these to make it move: a kite going up, a swing, a football?
prompt_hi: Inko kaun dhakelta ya kheenchta hai: upar jaati patang, jhoola, football?
answer: Kite: the wind pushes it up and the string pulls it. Swing: a push from someone or from your own legs. Football: a kick, which is a push.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: Make a paper helicopter: take a strip of paper, tear it halfway down the middle to make two wings, fold one wing forward and one back, and fold the bottom up a little. Stand on the floor and drop it from as high as you can reach. What does it do?
prompt_hi: Kaagaz ka helicopter banao: kaagaz ki ek patti lo, beech se aadhe tak phaado taaki do pankh banein, ek pankh aage aur ek peeche modo, aur neeche ka hissa thoda upar mod do. Zameen pe khade hokar jitna upar haath jaaye wahan se girao. Kya hota hai?
answer: It spins round and round as it falls slowly; the air pushes on its wings and turns it.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: Clip a paper clip to the bottom of your paper helicopter. Predict: will it fall faster or slower than before?
prompt_hi: Apne kaagaz ke helicopter ke neeche ek paper clip laga do. Guess karo: pehle se tez girega ya dheere?
answer: Faster: the extra weight pulls it down harder compared with the air pushing up on the wings.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: Make one helicopter with long wings and one with short wings from the same paper. Predict which one falls more slowly.
prompt_hi: Ek hi kaagaz se do helicopter banao, ek lambe pankh wala aur ek chhote pankh wala. Guess karo kaun dheere girega.
answer: The long-winged one: bigger wings catch more air, so it falls more slowly.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: Roll the same ball with the same push on a smooth floor and on a carpet or durrie. Predict where it will go farther.
prompt_hi: Ek hi ball ko ek jaise dhakke se chikne farsh pe aur carpet ya dari pe ludhkao. Guess karo kahan zyada door jayegi.
answer: On the smooth floor: the carpet rubs against the ball more (more friction) and slows it down sooner.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: You run with a phirki, first slowly and then fast. Predict: when will it spin faster?
prompt_hi: Tum phirki leke daudte ho, pehle dheere phir tez. Guess karo: kab zyada tez ghoomegi?
answer: When you run fast: more air pushes on the blades, so it spins faster.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: Why doesn't a phirki spin when you hold it still in a closed room?
prompt_hi: Band kamre mein phirki ko seedha pakad ke khade raho toh woh kyon nahi ghoomti?
answer: There is no moving air to push its blades; it needs a push from wind to turn.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: Drop a flat sheet of paper and a crumpled ball made from an identical sheet at the same time. Which lands first, and what is different about them?
prompt_hi: Ek seedhi kaagaz ki sheet aur usi jaisi sheet ko mod ke banayi goli, dono ek saath girao. Pehle kaun girta hai, aur dono mein kya farak hai?
answer: The crumpled ball lands first; both weigh the same, but the flat sheet has a big surface that the air pushes against, which slows it.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: Button spinner: pass a string through two holes of a big button, twist the string, then pull the ends in and out. What makes the button spin?
prompt_hi: Button spinner: bade button ke do chhedon mein dhaaga daalo, dhaage ko ghuma ke lapeto, phir dono sire kheencho aur dheela chhodo. Button ko kaun ghuma raha hai?
answer: Your pulls on the string: as the twisted string is pulled tight it unwinds and spins the button, and the button's spin winds it up again for the next pull.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: Windmills on hills in Tamil Nadu and Gujarat turn their huge blades. What pushes them, and why are they built in windy places?
prompt_hi: Tamil Nadu aur Gujarat ki pahaadiyon pe bade-bade windmill ke pankh ghoomte hain. Unhe kaun ghumata hai, aur unhe hawa wali jagah pe kyon lagaate hain?
answer: The wind pushes the blades, like a giant phirki; windy places give stronger, steadier pushes, so the blades turn more and make more electricity.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: Here is a table: Spinner A (short wings) took 1 second to fall; Spinner B (long wings) took 3 seconds. Tell me in words what this shows.
prompt_hi: Ye table dekho: Spinner A (chhote pankh) ko girne mein 1 second laga; Spinner B (lambe pankh) ko 3 second. Shabdon mein batao ye kya dikhata hai.
answer: The long-winged spinner fell more slowly (it took longer), because longer wings catch more air.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: Golu says: 'My lattu stopped because the push I gave it got used up inside it.' What's a better explanation?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Mera lattu isliye ruk gaya kyonki maine jo dhakka diya tha woh uske andar khatam ho gaya.' Isse behtar explanation kya hai?
answer: The floor and the air rub against the spinning lattu (friction), slowing it down until it stops.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu how a phirki works and how to make it spin faster.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki phirki kaise kaam karti hai aur use aur tez kaise ghuma sakte hain.
answer: Moving air pushes on the bent blades and turns them; more or faster air (running faster, stronger wind) means a faster spin; with no wind it doesn't spin.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
prompt: From last time: what must happen for anything to start moving?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kisi bhi cheez ko chalna shuru karne ke liye kya hona zaroori hai?
answer: It must be pushed or pulled.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: Name two plant materials that paper can be made from.
prompt_hi: Do paudhon wali cheezein batao jinse kaagaz banta hai.
answer: Any two: wood, bamboo, sugarcane waste (bagasse), cotton rags, straw.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: Put the paper-making steps in order: drying, making pulp, pressing out water, spreading the pulp thin.
prompt_hi: Kaagaz banane ke steps kram mein lagao: sukhaana, pulp banana, paani nichodna, pulp ko patla phailaana.
answer: making pulp → spreading the pulp thin → pressing out the water → drying

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: Slowly tear a piece of newspaper and look closely at the torn edge (with a magnifying glass if you have one). Predict first: will the edge be smooth or hairy?
prompt_hi: Akhbaar ka ek tukda dheere se phaado aur phati hui kinaari ko dhyaan se dekho (magnifying glass ho toh usse). Pehle guess karo: kinaari chikni hogi ya roeydaar?
answer: Hairy or fuzzy: you can see tiny fibres from plants, which is what paper is made of.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: We soak torn newspaper in a bucket of water overnight. Predict what it will be like in the morning.
prompt_hi: Phate hue akhbaar ko raat bhar paani ki baalti mein bhigo dete hain. Guess karo subah woh kaisa hoga?
answer: Soft, mushy and falling apart: the fibres loosen in water, so it can be mashed into pulp.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: Predict: which uses more trees and water, making 100 notebooks from fresh wood or making 100 notebooks from old paper?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: kismein zyada ped aur paani lagta hai, nayi lakdi se 100 copy banane mein ya purane kaagaz se 100 copy banane mein?
answer: From fresh wood: recycling old paper saves trees and uses less water and energy.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: Why do we press and dry the pulp when making paper?
prompt_hi: Kaagaz banate waqt pulp ko dabaate aur sukhaate kyon hain?
answer: To squeeze out the water so the fibres stick together tightly into a thin, flat, strong sheet.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: Compare a leaf and a sheet of paper. Both come from plants. How are they different?
prompt_hi: Ek patte aur ek kaagaz ki sheet ki tulna karo. Dono paudhon se aate hain. Farak kya hai?
answer: A leaf grows on a plant by itself; paper is made by people from plant fibres that are broken up, mixed with water, spread, pressed and dried.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: Your class uses a lot of paper. Name three ways to waste less paper at school.
prompt_hi: Tumhari class bahut kaagaz use karti hai. School mein kaagaz kam bekaar karne ke teen tareeke batao.
answer: Any three: use both sides, use old notebooks for rough work, put used paper in a recycling bin, practise on slates or whiteboards, don't tear pages out.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: In India some paper is made from bagasse, the dry leftover after sugarcane juice is squeezed out. Why is that a smart idea?
prompt_hi: India mein kuch kaagaz bagasse se banta hai, jo ganne ka ras nikaalne ke baad bacha hua sookha hissa hai. Ye samajhdaari kyon hai?
answer: It uses a waste material instead of cutting trees, so trees are saved and something that would be thrown away becomes useful.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: Four pictures are out of order: a sheet drying in the sun; torn newspaper in a bucket of water; mushy pulp spread on a net; a cloth pressing out water. Put them in order and say each step.
prompt_hi: Chaar picture ulte-seedhe hain: dhoop mein sookhti sheet; paani ki baalti mein phata akhbaar; jaali pe phaila hua gila pulp; kapde se paani nichodna. Inhe kram mein lagao aur har step bolo.
answer: Torn paper soaked in water → pulp spread on the net → pressed with a cloth to squeeze out water → dried in the sun.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: Golu says: 'Paper grows on paper trees, and people just pluck the sheets.' What's the mistake?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Kaagaz ke ped pe kaagaz ugte hain, log bas sheet tod lete hain.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Paper doesn't grow; people make it from plant fibres (like wood or bamboo) by making pulp, spreading it, pressing it and drying it.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu how to make recycled paper at home from old newspapers, step by step, using only safe things.
prompt_hi: Golu ko step-by-step samjhao ki ghar pe purane akhbaar se recycled kaagaz kaise banate hain, sirf safe cheezon se.
answer: Tear the paper into bits, soak it in water overnight, mash it with your hands into pulp, spread it thinly on a net or cloth, press out the water with another cloth, and dry it in the sun.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
prompt: From last time: give one reason why recycling paper helps nature.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek kaaran batao ki kaagaz recycle karna prakriti ke liye achha kyon hai.
answer: Fewer trees are cut, water and energy are saved, and there is less garbage.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: Sort into natural and human-made: wool, plastic bucket, stone, glass bottle, cotton, steel spoon.
prompt_hi: Inhe natural aur insaan ke banaye hue mein baanto: oon, plastic ki baalti, patthar, kaanch ki bottle, cotton, steel ka chammach.
answer: Natural: wool, stone, cotton. Human-made: plastic bucket, glass bottle, steel spoon.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: What natural material is each of these made from: glass, plastic, a steel plate?
prompt_hi: Ye kis natural cheez se bante hain: kaanch, plastic, steel ki plate?
answer: Glass: sand. Plastic: crude oil (petroleum). Steel: iron ore.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: Bury a strip of jute (from an old sack) and a strip of plastic bag in a pot of moist soil. Predict what you will find after two months.
prompt_hi: Ek gamle ki geeli mitti mein purani bori ka jute ka tukda aur plastic ki thaili ka tukda daba do. Guess karo, do mahine baad kya milega?
answer: The jute will be softening and starting to rot and fall apart; the plastic will look nearly the same.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: Spill a little water on a table. Put a cotton handkerchief on one drop and a piece of plastic sheet on another. Predict which one will soak up the water.
prompt_hi: Mez pe thoda paani gira do. Ek boond pe cotton ka rumaal rakho aur doosri pe plastic ki sheet. Guess karo kaun paani sokh lega.
answer: The cotton handkerchief soaks it up; plastic does not absorb water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: Crude oil is natural. Why do we still call plastic human-made?
prompt_hi: Crude oil toh natural hai. Phir bhi plastic ko insaan ka banaya hua kyon kehte hain?
answer: Because people change the oil completely in factories to make plastic; plastic is not found anywhere in nature.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: Compare a jute bag and a plastic bag: one good point and one problem of each.
prompt_hi: Jute ke thaile aur plastic ki thaili ki tulna karo: dono ki ek achhi baat aur ek pareshaani.
answer: Jute: strong, reusable and rots away naturally, but heavier and can get mouldy if left wet. Plastic: light and waterproof, but doesn't rot, pollutes soil and water and harms animals.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: Is silk natural or human-made? What about nylon?
prompt_hi: Resham (silk) natural hai ya insaan ka banaya hua? Aur nylon?
answer: Silk is natural (from silkworm cocoons); nylon is human-made (made from oil in factories).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: Cows on Indian streets sometimes eat plastic bags along with food scraps. Using what you know about plastic, explain why that is dangerous and what people can do.
prompt_hi: Sadkon pe gaayein kabhi-kabhi khaane ke saath plastic ki thaili bhi kha jaati hain. Plastic ke baare mein jo jaante ho, usse samjhao ki ye khatarnaak kyon hai aur log kya kar sakte hain.
answer: Plastic doesn't break down, so it stays in the cow's stomach and can make it very sick; people should not throw food in plastic bags, should use cloth or jute bags, and should put waste in bins.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: Draw arrows (or tell me) from each natural source to what is made from it. Sources: sand, iron ore, crude oil, cotton plant. Products: glass, steel, plastic, cloth.
prompt_hi: Har natural cheez se uski bani cheez tak teer banao (ya batao). Cheezein: ret, lohe ka ayask, crude oil, kapaas ka paudha. Bani cheezein: kaanch, steel, plastic, kapda.
answer: sand → glass; iron ore → steel; crude oil → plastic; cotton plant → cloth.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: Golu says: 'Glass comes from sand and plastic comes from oil, and sand and oil are natural, so glass and plastic are natural too!' Fix Golu.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Kaanch ret se aur plastic tel se banta hai, aur ret aur tel natural hain, toh kaanch aur plastic bhi natural hain!' Golu ko theek karo.
answer: They start from natural materials, but people change them a lot in factories (melting sand at very high heat, processing oil), so glass and plastic are human-made.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu how to tell whether a material is natural or human-made, with two examples of each.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki kaise pata karein koi material natural hai ya insaan ka banaya hua, dono ke do-do example dekar.
answer: Natural materials come from plants, animals or the earth and are used almost as they are (wood, cotton, wool, stone); human-made ones are made by people changing natural materials a lot (plastic, glass, steel, nylon).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
prompt: From last time: name two natural materials and two human-made materials in your kitchen.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: apne kitchen ki do natural aur do insaan ki banayi cheezein batao.
answer: e.g. Natural: a wooden belan, a clay pot, a stone sil-batta, a cotton cloth. Human-made: steel utensils, plastic boxes, a glass jar.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: Match each place to its description. Places: Ladakh, the Thar desert, the Kerala coast, the Punjab plains. Descriptions: cold desert, hot desert, near the sea, flat land with rivers.
prompt_hi: Jagah ko uske varnan se milao. Jagah: Ladakh, Thar registaan, Kerala ka samandar kinara, Punjab ke maidaan. Varnan: thanda registaan, garam registaan, samandar ke paas, nadiyon wali samtal zameen.
answer: Ladakh: cold desert. Thar: hot desert. Kerala coast: near the sea. Punjab plains: flat land with rivers.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: What clothes would people wear in Ladakh in winter, and in Rajasthan in summer?
prompt_hi: Ladakh mein sardiyon mein log kaise kapde pehente honge, aur Rajasthan mein garmiyon mein?
answer: Ladakh: thick woollen clothes in layers, with caps and long woollen robes. Rajasthan: loose, light cotton clothes, with a turban (safa) or dupatta to shade the head from the sun.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: In the Thar desert it is very hot in the afternoon. Predict: will it also be hot at midnight?
prompt_hi: Thar registaan mein dopahar mein bahut garmi hoti hai. Guess karo: kya aadhi raat ko bhi utni hi garmi hogi?
answer: No: desert nights can get quite cold, because the dry sand and clear skies let the heat escape quickly after sunset.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: A family moves from coastal Kerala to Ladakh. Predict two things they will have to change in their daily life.
prompt_hi: Ek family Kerala ke samandar kinare se Ladakh shift hoti hai. Guess karo, unhe rozmarra ki zindagi mein kaunsi do cheezein badalni padengi.
answer: Any two: wear heavy woollens instead of light cotton; eat more of what grows or keeps well there (barley, thukpa, butter tea) and less fresh coconut and sea fish; keep the house warm in winter; use water carefully because it is a dry place.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: Why is Ladakh called a desert even though it is cold and has snowy mountains?
prompt_hi: Ladakh thanda hai aur wahan barfeele pahaad hain, phir bhi use registaan kyon kehte hain?
answer: Because it gets very little rain and is very dry; a desert means a place with very little rain, not a hot place.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: Compare the Thar desert and Ladakh: one way they are alike and one way they are different.
prompt_hi: Thar registaan aur Ladakh ki tulna karo: ek baat jisme dono ek jaise hain, aur ek jisme alag.
answer: Alike: both get very little rain and have few plants. Different: the Thar is hot with sand dunes; Ladakh is cold, high and rocky with mountains.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: Fishing is a common job on the coast. What common jobs might people do in the plains, and in the mountains?
prompt_hi: Samandar kinare machhli pakadna ek aam kaam hai. Maidaanon mein aur pahaadon mein log kaun se aam kaam karte honge?
answer: Plains: farming (wheat, rice, sugarcane) and dairy. Mountains: herding sheep, goats or yaks, growing apples or barley, and guiding tourists.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: Antarctica is covered in ice, but scientists call it the world's biggest desert. Use what you learnt to explain why.
prompt_hi: Antarctica barf se dhaka hai, phir bhi scientist use duniya ka sabse bada registaan kehte hain. Jo seekha uske hisaab se samjhao kyon.
answer: It gets very little snow or rain each year, so it is extremely dry; a desert is defined by very little rain or snowfall, not by heat or sand.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: Read this clue card: 'Very little rain, freezing winters, snowy mountains, people wear thick wool, eat barley and drink butter tea.' Which region is this? Point to it on the map and tell me which clues gave it away.
prompt_hi: Ye clue card padho: 'Baarish bahut kam, kadaake ki sardi, barfeele pahaad, log mote oon ke kapde pehente hain, jau khaate hain aur butter wali chai peete hain.' Ye kaunsa ilaaka hai? Map pe dikhao aur batao kin clues se pata chala.
answer: Ladakh, a cold desert in the far north of India; the clues are very little rain plus freezing cold, mountains and thick wool.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: Golu says: 'All deserts are hot and full of sand dunes and camels.' Find the mistakes.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Saare registaan garam hote hain aur ret ke teelon aur oonton se bhare hote hain.' Galtiyan pakdo.
answer: Deserts are places with very little rain; some are cold, like Ladakh, and not all are sandy: some are rocky or icy.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu why people in the mountains and people on the coast eat and dress differently.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki pahaadon ke log aur samandar kinare ke log alag tarah ka khaana kyon khaate hain aur alag kapde kyon pehente hain.
answer: The weather and what grows are different: mountains are cold, so people wear wool and eat warming food and crops that grow there (barley, apples); coasts are warm and humid, so people wear light cotton and eat rice, fish and coconut.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
prompt: From last time: what is the one thing every desert has in common?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: har registaan mein kaunsi ek baat common hoti hai?
answer: Very little rain.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: Why are many houses in flood-prone parts of Assam built on bamboo stilts?
prompt_hi: Assam ke baadh wale ilaakon mein bahut se ghar baans ke khambhon (stilts) pe kyon bane hote hain?
answer: To stay above flood water and keep away from damp ground (and from crawling animals).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: Which roof suits each place: heavy rain in Kerala, very little rain in Rajasthan? Sloping or flat?
prompt_hi: Kis jagah ke liye kaunsi chhat theek hai: Kerala mein bahut baarish, Rajasthan mein bahut kam baarish? Dhalaan wali ya sapaat?
answer: Kerala: sloping roof. Rajasthan: flat roof.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: Pour a little water slowly onto a flat plate, and onto a plate tilted up on a book. Predict where the water will stay and where it will run off.
prompt_hi: Ek seedhi plate pe aur ek kitaab ke sahare tedhi rakhi plate pe dheere se thoda paani daalo. Guess karo, kahan paani rukega aur kahan beh jayega?
answer: It runs off the tilted plate and stays on the flat one, just as a sloping roof lets rain run off.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: Two small huts in the Thar desert: one with thick mud walls, one with thin tin sheets for its roof and walls. Predict which is cooler inside at 3 pm.
prompt_hi: Thar registaan mein do chhoti jhopdiyan: ek moti mitti ki deewaron wali, ek patli teen (tin) ki chhat aur deewaron wali. Guess karo, dopahar 3 baje andar se kaun zyada thandi hogi?
answer: The thick mud hut: thick mud lets heat in only slowly, while thin tin gets very hot very quickly.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: Why do many houses in Rajasthan have flat roofs that people use in the evenings?
prompt_hi: Rajasthan ke kai gharon ki chhat sapaat kyon hoti hai, aur log shaam ko uska use kyon karte hain?
answer: It rains very little, so water doesn't collect much on a flat roof; the roof is used to sleep on cool nights and to dry clothes, grain or chillies, and some houses even collect the little rain that falls.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: Compare a traditional Kerala house and a traditional Ladakh house. What do their roofs look like, and why?
prompt_hi: Kerala ke paaramparik ghar aur Ladakh ke paaramparik ghar ki tulna karo. Unki chhat kaisi hoti hai, aur kyon?
answer: Kerala: steep sloping roofs, because monsoon rain is very heavy. Ladakh: flat roofs, because very little rain or snow falls there; the roofs are used to dry apricots and store fodder.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: Lots of bamboo grows in the hills of Assam and Meghalaya. Why would people there build houses with bamboo?
prompt_hi: Assam aur Meghalaya ki pahaadiyon mein bahut baans ugta hai. Wahan log baans se ghar kyon banaate honge?
answer: Bamboo is found nearby, and it is strong, light and easy to work with, which is good for building raised houses.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: Imagine building a house on a very hot, sunny, dry street. Name two features you would add to keep it cool, using what you learnt.
prompt_hi: Socho tum ek bahut garam, dhoop wali, sookhi jagah pe ghar bana rahe ho. Jo seekha uske hisaab se, ghar thanda rakhne ke liye do cheezein batao.
answer: Any two: thick walls, small or shaded windows, light-coloured walls and roof, trees around the house, a verandah or deep shade, a high ceiling.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: Here is a description: 'A house on tall bamboo posts, with bamboo walls, a sloping thatch roof and a ladder to the door.' Draw it (or describe your drawing) and say what kind of place it suits.
prompt_hi: Ye varnan suno: 'Lambe baans ke khambhon pe ghar, baans ki deewarein, phoos ki dhalaan wali chhat, aur darwaze tak seedhi.' Iski drawing banao (ya batao kya banaoge) aur batao ye kis tarah ki jagah ke liye theek hai.
answer: A stilt house; it suits a place with heavy rain and floods, like parts of Assam.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: Golu says: 'Mud and bamboo houses are old-fashioned. Everyone everywhere should live in the same concrete flats.' What is Golu missing?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Mitti aur baans ke ghar purane zamaane ke hain. Har jagah sabko ek jaise concrete flat mein rehna chahiye.' Golu kya bhool raha hai?
answer: Houses suit their land and weather: stilts for floods, thick mud walls for heat, sloping roofs for rain and snow; local materials are close at hand and suit the place, so one design doesn't fit everywhere.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu why houses in Assam, Rajasthan and the snowy hills look different.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki Assam, Rajasthan aur barfeele pahaadon ke ghar alag-alag kyon dikhte hain.
answer: Each suits its weather: Assam's floods and heavy rain call for stilts and sloping roofs; Rajasthan's heat and little rain call for thick mud walls and flat roofs; snowy hills need sloping roofs so snow slides off.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
prompt: From last time: why do houses in places with heavy rain or snow have sloping roofs?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jahan bahut baarish ya barf hoti hai, wahan ke gharon ki chhat dhalaan wali kyon hoti hai?
answer: So the rain and snow slide off.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: What do you need to make a shadow?
prompt_hi: Parchhai banane ke liye kya-kya chahiye?
answer: A light source, an object that blocks the light, and a surface for the shadow to fall on.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: When is your shadow longest: morning, noon or evening? And when is it shortest?
prompt_hi: Tumhari parchhai sabse lambi kab hoti hai: subah, dopahar ya shaam? Aur sabse chhoti kab?
answer: Longest in the early morning and late evening; shortest around noon.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: At 8 in the morning the Sun is in the east. Predict: which direction will a stick's shadow point?
prompt_hi: Subah 8 baje Sooraj poorab (east) mein hota hai. Guess karo: dande ki parchhai kis disha mein padegi?
answer: West, on the opposite side from the Sun.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: Fix a stick upright in the ground in a sunny spot. Mark the tip of its shadow at 9 am, 12 noon and 3 pm (look at the shadow, never at the Sun). Predict: which mark will be closest to the stick?
prompt_hi: Dhoop wali jagah pe ek danda seedha gaad do. Subah 9 baje, dopahar 12 baje aur 3 baje parchhai ke sire pe nishaan lagao (parchhai dekho, Sooraj ko kabhi seedha mat dekhna). Guess karo: kaunsa nishaan dande ke sabse paas hoga?
answer: The 12 noon mark: the shadow is shortest around noon, when the Sun is high.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: Hold a red ball in sunlight. Predict: what colour will its shadow be?
prompt_hi: Dhoop mein ek laal ball pakdo. Guess karo: uski parchhai kis rang ki hogi?
answer: Dark grey, not red: a shadow is just where the light is blocked.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: Shine a torch on a toy so its shadow falls on a wall. Predict: if you move the torch closer to the toy, what happens to the shadow?
prompt_hi: Torch se ek khilone pe roshni daalo taaki deewar pe uski parchhai bane. Guess karo: torch ko khilone ke aur paas le jaoge toh parchhai ka kya hoga?
answer: The shadow gets bigger, because the toy blocks more of the torch's light.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: Why is a shadow always on the opposite side from the light?
prompt_hi: Parchhai hamesha roshni ki ulti taraf hi kyon banti hai?
answer: Light travels in straight lines; the object blocks it, so the area behind the object, away from the light, stays dark.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: Look at a toy in a mirror and at its shadow on the wall. Give two differences.
prompt_hi: Ek khilone ko sheeshe mein dekho aur deewar pe uski parchhai dekho. Do farak batao.
answer: The mirror shows the toy's colours and details; the shadow is just a dark outline with no colour or details. The mirror image comes from light bouncing back; the shadow is where light is blocked.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: At 5 pm the Sun is in the west. Which way does the shadow of a lamp post point?
prompt_hi: Shaam 5 baje Sooraj paschim mein hai. Bijli ke khambhe ki parchhai kis taraf padegi?
answer: East.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: In a village, people sit in a tree's shade. At noon the shade is right under the tree, but by evening it has moved and grown. Why does the shady spot move during the day?
prompt_hi: Gaon mein log ped ki chhaaya mein baithte hain. Dopahar mein chhaaya theek ped ke neeche hoti hai, par shaam tak woh khisak ke lambi ho jaati hai. Din bhar chhaaya kyon khisakti hai?
answer: The Sun's place in the sky changes as the Earth turns, so the tree's shadow changes direction and length: it moves to the side away from the Sun and gets longer as the Sun gets lower.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: In this picture the Sun is low on the left side of a house. Point to where the house's shadow will be, and say whether it is long or short.
prompt_hi: Is picture mein Sooraj ghar ke left side mein neeche hai. Batao ghar ki parchhai kahan hogi, aur lambi hogi ya chhoti?
answer: On the right side of the house, and long, because the Sun is low.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: Golu says: 'Every day the Sun walks across the sky from east to west, going around the Earth.' What is a better explanation?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Roz Sooraj aasmaan mein poorab se paschim tak chalta hai, Dharti ke chakkar lagaate hue.' Isse behtar explanation kya hai?
answer: The Earth spins once a day, so the Sun only seems to move across our sky.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu why his shadow is long in the morning, short at lunchtime and long again in the evening.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki uski parchhai subah lambi, dopahar mein chhoti, aur shaam ko phir lambi kyon hoti hai.
answer: In the morning and evening the Sun is low, so the shadow is long; at noon the Sun is high, so it is short; the shadow is always opposite the Sun, and the Sun's position changes because the Earth spins.

subject: evs
topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
prompt: From last time: what is a shadow, in one line?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek line mein batao, parchhai kya hoti hai?
answer: A dark area formed where an object blocks light.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: What do we call the night when we see the full round Moon, and the night when we can't see the Moon at all?
prompt_hi: Jis raat poora gol chaand dikhta hai use kya kehte hain, aur jis raat chaand bilkul nahi dikhta use kya?
answer: Full Moon: Purnima. No Moon visible: Amavasya (new moon).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: About how many days is it from one Purnima to the next Purnima?
prompt_hi: Ek Purnima se agli Purnima tak lagbhag kitne din hote hain?
answer: About 29 to 30 days, about a month.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: Tonight is Purnima. Predict: about one week from now, will the Moon look more lit, the same, or less lit?
prompt_hi: Aaj Purnima hai. Guess karo: lagbhag ek hafte baad chaand zyada roshan dikhega, waisa hi, ya kam?
answer: Less lit: about half of it (a half-moon), shrinking toward Amavasya.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: In a dark room, shine a torch on a white ball from one side. Walk slowly around the ball. Predict: will the lit part look the same from everywhere?
prompt_hi: Andhere kamre mein ek taraf se torch se safed ball pe roshni daalo. Ball ke chaaron taraf dheere-dheere ghoomo. Guess karo: kya roshan hissa har jagah se ek jaisa dikhega?
answer: No: from some spots you see it fully lit, from others half-lit or as a thin sliver, and from one spot almost dark, like the Moon's phases. The ball itself never changes.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: A few days after Amavasya you see a thin crescent Moon. Predict: over the next week, will it get thicker or thinner?
prompt_hi: Amavasya ke kuch din baad tumhe patla sa chaand dikhta hai. Guess karo: agle hafte woh mota hoga ya aur patla?
answer: Thicker: the lit part grows toward Purnima.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: Why does the Moon seem to change shape over a month?
prompt_hi: Mahine bhar mein chaand ka aakaar badalta hua kyon lagta hai?
answer: The Moon goes around the Earth; half of it is always lit by the Sun, and from Earth we see different amounts of that lit half on different days.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: Compare the Moon on Purnima and on Amavasya. What do we see, and is the Moon still there on Amavasya?
prompt_hi: Purnima aur Amavasya ke chaand ki tulna karo. Dono din kya dikhta hai, aur kya Amavasya ko chaand wahan hota hai?
answer: Purnima: we see the whole lit face, bright and round. Amavasya: we can't see it; it is still there, but its lit side faces away from us and it is close to the Sun in the sky.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: Diwali falls on Amavasya, a dark moonless night. About how many days later will the next Purnima come?
prompt_hi: Diwali Amavasya ki andheri raat ko hoti hai. Lagbhag kitne din baad agli Purnima aayegi?
answer: About 15 days later.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: Sometimes you can see the Moon in the morning sky while the Sun is also up. How is that possible if the Moon 'belongs to the night'?
prompt_hi: Kabhi-kabhi subah ke aasmaan mein Sooraj ke saath chaand bhi dikh jaata hai. Agar chaand 'raat ka' hai, toh ye kaise hota hai?
answer: The Moon is above the horizon during part of the day on many days; it shines by reflected sunlight, so it can be seen in daylight when it is up in the sky and bright enough.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: Here is Aman's moon diary with four drawings: thin crescent, half-moon, almost full, full. Put them in the order he would see them after Amavasya, and name the last one.
prompt_hi: Ye Aman ki moon diary hai jisme chaar drawings hain: patla chaand, aadha chaand, lagbhag poora, poora gol. Amavasya ke baad jis kram mein dikhenge us kram mein lagao, aur aakhri wale ka naam batao.
answer: thin crescent → half-moon → almost full → full Moon (Purnima)

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: Golu says: 'The Moon is a giant bulb that switches itself on at night.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Chaand ek bada sa bulb hai jo raat ko apne aap jal jaata hai.' Galat kya hai?
answer: The Moon makes no light of its own; it shines because sunlight falls on it and bounces to us.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: Explain to your little cousin Golu why the Moon looks like a thin slice on some nights and a full circle on others.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki chaand kuch raaton ko patli phaank jaisa aur kuch raaton ko poora gol kyon dikhta hai.
answer: The Sun always lights half of the Moon; as the Moon goes around the Earth over about a month, we see more or less of that lit half, from a thin slice to a full circle; the Moon itself stays round, and it is not the Earth's shadow.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
prompt: From last time: after Purnima, does the Moon's lit part grow or shrink?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Purnima ke baad chaand ka roshan hissa badhta hai ya ghatta hai?
answer: It shrinks, until Amavasya.

prompt: 1 cm stands for 10 m. What does 9 cm stand for?
prompt_hi: 1 cm, 10 m ke barabar hai. 9 cm kitne ke barabar hai?

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Each TV picture stands for 2 hours of screen time. Riya's row has 3 TV pictures. How many hours is that?
prompt_hi: Har TV tasveer 2 ghante screen time ke barabar hai. Riya ki row mein 3 TV tasveerein hain. Kitne ghante hue?
answer: 6 hours

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Each TV picture stands for 2 hours. Aman's row has 2 full TV pictures and a half one. How many hours?
prompt_hi: Har TV tasveer 2 ghante. Aman ki row mein 2 poori aur ek aadhi tasveer hai. Kitne ghante?
answer: 5 hours

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Each football picture stands for 10 students. The football row shows 4 pictures. How many students like football?
prompt_hi: Har football tasveer 10 bachchon ke barabar hai. Football ki row mein 4 tasveerein hain. Kitne bachchon ko football pasand hai?

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Each star stands for 10 students. How many stars should you draw for 35 students?
prompt_hi: Har star 10 bachchon ke barabar hai. 35 bachchon ke liye kitne star banaoge?
answer: 3 full stars and a half star

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Predict: if we change the key from '1 star = 10 students' to '1 star = 5 students', will the rows get longer or shorter?
prompt_hi: Andaaza lagao: agar key '1 star = 10 bachche' se badalkar '1 star = 5 bachche' kar dein, toh rows lambi hongi ya chhoti?
answer: Longer: each row needs twice as many stars

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Two pictographs both show 40 mangoes. One uses '1 mango picture = 10' and the other '1 mango picture = 5'. How many pictures in each row?
prompt_hi: Do pictograph dono 40 aam dikhaate hain. Ek mein '1 aam tasveer = 10' aur doosre mein '1 aam tasveer = 5'. Har row mein kitni tasveerein?
answer: 4 pictures and 8 pictures

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Why does half a picture stand for 5 when one full picture stands for 10?
prompt_hi: Ek poori tasveer 10 ke barabar ho toh aadhi tasveer 5 ke barabar kyun hoti hai?
answer: Half the picture means half of its value, and half of 10 is 5

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Each TV picture stands for 2 hours. Neel read 3 full TV pictures and a half one as 8 hours. Check him.
prompt_hi: Har TV tasveer 2 ghante. Neel ne 3 poori aur ek aadhi TV tasveer ko 8 ghante padha. Check karo.
answer: Wrong: the half picture is 1 hour, so it is 6 + 1 = 7 hours

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: In a pictograph of runs, each bat picture stands for 20 runs. Rohit's row shows 4 bats and a half bat. How many runs?
prompt_hi: Runs ke pictograph mein har bat ki tasveer 20 runs ke barabar hai. Rohit ki row mein 4 bat aur ek aadha bat hai. Kitne runs?
answer: 90 runs

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Your family drank 28, 42 and 35 glasses of water on three days. Choose a picture value so the rows are not too long, and say how many pictures each day needs.
prompt_hi: Tumhare parivaar ne teen dinon mein 28, 42 aur 35 glass paani piya. Ek tasveer ki aisi value chuno ki rows zyada lambi na hon, aur batao har din kitni tasveerein.
answer: 1 picture = 7 glasses: 4, 6 and 5 pictures

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Turn this table into pictograph rows using '1 bus picture = 4 children': Bus 12, Walk 6.
prompt_hi: Is table ko pictograph rows mein badlo, '1 bus tasveer = 4 bachche': Bus 12, Paidal 6.
answer: Bus: 3 pictures; Walk: 1 and a half pictures

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Teach Chintu how to read a pictograph that has a key.
prompt_hi: Chintu ko sikhao ki key wala pictograph kaise padhte hain.
answer: Read the key first; multiply the whole pictures by the key value; add half the key value for each half picture

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
prompt: Each apple picture stands for 5 apples. How many apples do 6 apple pictures show?
prompt_hi: Har seb ki tasveer 5 seb. 6 tasveerein kitne seb dikhaati hain?

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: Each line on the scale stands for 10 children. The mango bar reaches the 4th line. How many children like mango?
prompt_hi: Scale ki har line 10 bachchon ke barabar hai. Aam wala bar chauthi line tak hai. Kitne bachchon ko aam pasand hai?

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: The scale goes 0, 50, 100, 150. A bar stops exactly halfway between 100 and 150. What value does it show?
prompt_hi: Scale 0, 50, 100, 150 hai. Ek bar 100 aur 150 ke theek beech mein rukta hai. Woh kya value dikhata hai?

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: A bar graph shows runs: Anil 80, Raju 65, Sunny 45. How many more runs did Anil score than Sunny?
prompt_hi: Bar graph mein runs hain: Anil 80, Raju 65, Sunny 45. Anil ne Sunny se kitne zyada runs banaaye?

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: You need bars for 12, 18, 25 and 30 cups of chai sold. Which scale step is sensible: 1, 5 or 50?
prompt_hi: Tumhe 12, 18, 25 aur 30 cup chai ke bars banane hain. Kaunsa scale step theek hai: 1, 5 ya 50?

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: Predict: if the scale started at 40 instead of 0, how would a 45-run bar look next to a 65-run bar?
prompt_hi: Andaaza lagao: agar scale 0 ki jagah 40 se shuru ho, toh 45 runs wala bar 65 runs wale ke saamne kaisa dikhega?
answer: Much shorter than it should: the gap would look far bigger than it is

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: Two graphs show the same rainfall, 100 mm and 95 mm. Graph A starts at 0 and Graph B starts at 90. In which graph do the bars look nearly equal, and which tells the truth better?
prompt_hi: Do graph ek hi baarish dikhaate hain, 100 mm aur 95 mm. Graph A 0 se aur Graph B 90 se shuru hota hai. Kismein bars lagbhag barabar dikhte hain, aur kaun sach behtar batata hai?
answer: In Graph A they look nearly equal, and Graph A tells the truth better

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: Why should the steps on a bar graph's scale be equal?
prompt_hi: Bar graph ke scale ke steps barabar kyun hone chahiye?
answer: So that equal heights mean equal amounts; uneven steps make the bars mislead

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: A town's rainfall bar reaches the 8th line and each line is 100 mm. Tanu says the rainfall is 8 mm. Check.
prompt_hi: Ek shehar ka baarish wala bar 8vi line tak hai aur har line 100 mm hai. Tanu kehti hai baarish 8 mm hui. Check karo.
answer: Wrong: 8 × 100 = 800 mm

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: A bar graph of monthly rainfall shows June 300 mm, July 450 mm and August 400 mm. Which month was the wettest, and how much more rain did it get than June?
prompt_hi: Mahine ki baarish ke bar graph mein June 300 mm, July 450 mm aur August 400 mm hai. Sabse geela mahina kaunsa tha, aur June se kitni zyada baarish hui?
answer: July, 150 mm more than June

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: An advertisement shows Brand X's bar twice as tall as Brand Y's. The scale starts at 80; X is 90 and Y is 85. What would you tell your friend?
prompt_hi: Ek vigyaapan mein Brand X ka bar Brand Y se do guna lamba dikhta hai. Scale 80 se shuru hai; X 90 hai aur Y 85. Tum dost ko kya bataoge?
answer: The difference is only 5; the graph exaggerates because its scale does not start at 0

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: Plan a bar graph for: Cycle 15, Bus 25, Walk 10 children. What scale would you use, and how tall is each bar?
prompt_hi: In ke liye bar graph plan karo: Cycle 15, Bus 25, Paidal 10 bachche. Kaunsa scale loge, aur har bar kitna lamba hoga?
answer: Steps of 5: Cycle 3 steps, Bus 5 steps, Walk 2 steps

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: Teach Chintu how to read a bar graph.
prompt_hi: Chintu ko sikhao ki bar graph kaise padhte hain.
answer: Read the title and labels, check the scale steps and that it starts at 0, follow the top of each bar across to the scale, then compare

subject: maths
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
prompt: On a scale of 0, 20, 40, 60, one bar reaches 60 and another reaches 20. How many times taller is the first?
prompt_hi: 0, 20, 40, 60 wale scale par ek bar 60 tak aur doosra 20 tak hai. Pehla kitne guna lamba hai?
answer: 3 times

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Name the three forms of water and give one place where you can find each.
prompt_hi: Paani ke teen roop batao, aur har roop ke liye ek jagah batao jahaan woh milta hai.
answer: Liquid: rivers, seas, ponds, tap water. Solid: ice in the freezer, snow and glaciers on the Himalayas. Gas: invisible water vapour in the air.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Where is most of Earth's water found: in rivers, in seas and oceans, or in ponds and lakes?
prompt_hi: Earth ka sabse zyada paani kahaan hai: nadiyon mein, samudra aur mahasagar mein, ya taalab aur jheelon mein?
answer: In the seas and oceans; about 97 out of every 100 parts of Earth's water is salty sea water.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Take a steel glass of ice-cold water from the fridge and wipe its outside dry. Predict first: after five minutes, will the outside stay dry or get wet? If it gets wet, where will that water come from?
prompt_hi: Fridge se barf jaise thande paani ka steel glass nikalo aur bahar se poochh ke sukha kar do. Pehle guess karo: paanch minute baad glass bahar se sukha rahega ya geela ho jayega? Agar geela hua, toh woh paani kahaan se aayega?
answer: The outside gets covered with tiny drops. They come from invisible water vapour in the air that turns back into liquid when it touches the cold glass (condensation); the water inside does not leak out.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Two equally wet handkerchiefs: one spread open in the sun, one folded up in a shady corner. Predict which one dries first, and where its water goes.
prompt_hi: Do barabar geele rumaal: ek dhoop mein khol ke phailaya, ek chhaanv wale kone mein tah karke rakha. Guess karo kaunsa pehle sookhega, aur uska paani kahaan jayega?
answer: The one spread open in the sun dries first; warmth and a bigger open surface make the water evaporate faster. The water goes into the air as invisible water vapour; it is not destroyed.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Stir two spoons of salt into half a cup of water, pour it into a plate and leave it in the sun for two or three days. Predict: what will be left on the plate?
prompt_hi: Aadhe cup paani mein do chammach namak ghol do, plate mein daal ke do-teen din dhoop mein rakh do. Guess karo: plate mein kya bachega?
answer: The water evaporates and white salt is left behind on the plate. This is how salt is made from sea water in salt pans, for example in Gujarat.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: There is so much water on Earth, yet many towns in India run short of drinking water every summer. Why?
prompt_hi: Earth pe itna saara paani hai, phir bhi har garmi mein India ke kai shehron mein peene ka paani kam pad jaata hai. Aisa kyon?
answer: Most of Earth's water is salty sea water, and most of the fresh water is frozen ice or deep under the ground; only a tiny part is in rivers, lakes and wells we can reach, and very many people share it.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Rain clouds get much of their water from the salty sea. So why is rain water not salty?
prompt_hi: Baarish ke baadal apna kaafi paani khaare samudra se lete hain. Phir baarish ka paani khaara kyon nahi hota?
answer: When sea water evaporates, only the water rises as vapour; the salt stays behind in the sea. So clouds and rain are fresh water.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Compare the water in a glacier high in the Himalayas with the water in the Arabian Sea. How are they different, and which one is fresh water?
prompt_hi: Himalaya ke glacier ke paani aur Arabian Sea ke paani ki tulna karo. Dono mein kya farak hai, aur kaunsa meetha (fresh) paani hai?
answer: Glacier water is solid ice and fresh, not salty; sea water is liquid and salty. Glacier ice melts slowly and feeds rivers like the Ganga.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Where does the water in your home's tap or handpump come from? Trace it back as far as you can.
prompt_hi: Tumhare ghar ke nal ya handpump ka paani kahaan se aata hai? Jitna peeche tak jaa sako, utna batao.
answer: From fresh water: a river, lake or dam reservoir through pipes and a tank, or from water under the ground through a borewell, well or handpump. All of it first came from rain or melting snow.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Chennai is right next to the sea, yet it sometimes faces water shortage. The city has built big plants that remove salt from sea water. Why can't every city just do this instead of saving water?
prompt_hi: Chennai bilkul samudra ke paas hai, phir bhi wahaan kabhi-kabhi paani ki kami hoti hai. Shehar ne bade plant banaye hain jo samudra ke paani se namak nikaalte hain. Har shehar bas yahi kyon nahi kar leta, paani bachane ki jagah?
answer: Removing salt from sea water needs big machines and a lot of electricity, so it is costly; it cannot replace saving water and keeping rivers, lakes and ground water clean.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Draw 100 small boxes to stand for all of Earth's water. Colour how many are salty sea water, how many are frozen ice, and how many are fresh water we can use. Then tell me what your drawing shows.
prompt_hi: 100 chhote dabbe banao jo Earth ke saare paani ko dikhayein. Rang bharo: kitne dabbe khaara samudra, kitne jami hui barf, aur kitne woh meetha paani jo hum use kar sakte hain. Phir batao tumhari drawing kya dikhati hai.
answer: About 97 boxes for salty sea water, about 2 boxes for ice and glaciers, and less than 1 box shared by ground water, rivers and lakes; usable fresh water is a tiny part.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Pinky says: 'When a puddle dries in the sun, the water is finished forever. The sun destroys it.' What is wrong with Pinky's idea?
prompt_hi: Pinky kehti hai: 'Jab dhoop mein gaddhe ka paani sookh jaata hai, toh paani hamesha ke liye khatam ho jaata hai. Suraj use mita deta hai.' Pinky ki baat mein galti kya hai?
answer: The water is not destroyed. It evaporates into the air as invisible water vapour, which later cools into clouds and comes back down as rain.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Your little cousin thinks steam, ice and rain are three totally different things. Explain to him how they are all water, and why we must not waste fresh water.
prompt_hi: Tumhara chhota cousin sochta hai ki bhaap, barf aur baarish teen bilkul alag cheezein hain. Use samjhao ki ye sab paani hi hain, aur hume meetha paani barbaad kyon nahi karna chahiye.
answer: Ice (solid), liquid water and water vapour (gas) are the same water in different forms; cooling and warming change the form. Very little of Earth's water is fresh and usable, so saving it matters.

subject: evs
topic: Water in different forms and places
outcomes: Learner can describe where water is found on Earth (oceans, rivers, ice, vapour) and why fresh water is scarce
prompt: Quick one from last time: out of every 100 buckets of Earth's water, about how many are salty?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se ek jaldi wala sawaal: Earth ke har 100 baalti paani mein se lagbhag kitni baaltiyaan khaari hain?
answer: About 97.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: Through which part does a plant mostly take in water: its flowers, its leaves or its roots?
prompt_hi: Paudha zyaadatar paani kis hisse se leta hai: phoolon se, pattiyon se ya jadon se?
answer: Through its roots.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: Name three ways your body loses water in a day.
prompt_hi: Teen tareeke batao jinse tumhare shareer se din bhar mein paani nikalta hai.
answer: Sweating, breathing out water vapour, and passing urine (tears too).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: Put a white flower (like a white rose or guldaudi) or a leafy stem in a glass of water with a few drops of food colour. Ask an adult to cut the stem fresh. Predict: what will you see on the petals or leaves after a day?
prompt_hi: Ek safed phool (jaise safed gulab ya guldaudi) ya patton wali tehni ko paani ke glass mein rakho jismein khaane ka rang ki kuch boondein daali hon. Tehni kisi bade se taaza katwa lo. Guess karo: ek din baad pankhudiyon ya pattiyon pe kya dikhega?
answer: The colour shows up in the petals or in the veins of the leaves, because water travels up the stem from the bottom to the top.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: In the morning, tie a clear plastic bag around one leafy branch of a plant standing in the sun (only the branch, not the whole plant). Predict: what will you see inside the bag by evening?
prompt_hi: Subah dhoop mein khade paudhe ki ek patton wali daal pe saaf plastic ki thaili baandh do (sirf daal pe, poore paudhe pe nahi). Guess karo: shaam tak thaili ke andar kya dikhega?
answer: Water drops and mist inside the bag. The leaves give out water vapour through tiny openings, and it turns into drops on the bag; this water came up from the roots.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: Two drooping potted plants: for one you spray water only on the leaves; for the other you pour water into the soil. Predict which one will stand up straight first.
prompt_hi: Do murjhaye hue gamle ke paudhe: ek ki sirf pattiyon pe paani chhidko, doosre ki mitti mein paani daalo. Guess karo kaunsa paudha pehle seedha khada hoga.
answer: The one watered in the soil, because its roots take up the water and send it up the stem to the leaves.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: Why does a plant droop (wilt) if it gets no water for a few days?
prompt_hi: Agar paudhe ko kuch din paani na mile, toh woh murjha kyon jaata hai?
answer: Water keeps the stem and leaves firm and is needed to make food. Without water coming up from the roots, the leaves lose more water than they get, go soft and droop.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: Farmers add manure to the soil. So does a plant eat soil and manure as its food? Explain.
prompt_hi: Kisaan mitti mein khaad daalte hain. Toh kya paudha mitti aur khaad ko apna khaana bana ke khaata hai? Samjhao.
answer: No. A plant makes its own food in its leaves using sunlight, water and air. Its roots take water and small amounts of minerals from the soil and manure, which keep it healthy, but soil is not its food.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: Compare a camel in the Thar desert with a buffalo near a village pond. How does each manage its water?
prompt_hi: Thar registan ke oont aur gaon ke taalab ke paas wali bhains ki tulna karo. Dono apne paani ka intezaam kaise karte hain?
answer: The buffalo drinks often and lies in the pond to stay cool. The camel can go many days without drinking because its body loses very little water, and it drinks a lot at once when it finds water. Its hump stores fat, not water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: On a hot summer day you play cricket for two hours. What happens to the water in your body, and what should you do?
prompt_hi: Garmi ke din tum do ghante cricket khelte ho. Tumhare shareer ke paani ka kya hota hai, aur tumhe kya karna chahiye?
answer: You lose a lot of water as sweat and through breathing, so you feel thirsty and tired. Drink water often and rest in the shade.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: Many farmers in Rajasthan use drip irrigation: thin pipes drip water right at the base of each plant. Why is this smarter than flooding the whole field with water?
prompt_hi: Rajasthan ke kai kisaan drip irrigation use karte hain: patli pipe se paani boond-boond har paudhe ki jad ke paas girta hai. Ye poore khet mein paani bhar dene se zyada samajhdaari kyon hai?
answer: The water goes straight to the roots, where the plant takes it in, so less water is lost to evaporation or to soil where there are no roots. It saves scarce water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: Draw a plant and use arrows to show the path water takes from the soil to the air. Label each part the water passes.
prompt_hi: Ek paudha banao aur teer (arrows) se dikhao ki paani mitti se hawa tak kaunsa raasta leta hai. Har hissa label karo jahaan se paani guzarta hai.
answer: Soil, then roots, then stem, then leaves, then out as water vapour through tiny openings into the air.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: Rohan says: 'A camel's hump is its water tank. That's why it can live in the desert.' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Rohan kehta hai: 'Oont ka kubad uski paani ki tanki hai. Isiliye woh registan mein reh paata hai.' Galti kya hai?
answer: The hump stores fat, not water. Camels survive because their bodies lose water very slowly and they can drink a lot at once when they find water.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: Your friend's younger sister waters only the leaves of her plant and thinks plants eat mud. Explain to her how a plant really gets its water and its food.
prompt_hi: Tumhare dost ki chhoti behen apne paudhe ki sirf pattiyon pe paani daalti hai aur sochti hai ki paudhe mitti khaate hain. Use samjhao ki paudha asal mein paani aur khaana kaise paata hai.
answer: Roots take water from the soil and it travels up the stem to the leaves; the leaves make the plant's food using sunlight, water and air. Soil gives water and minerals but is not the plant's food.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain how plants and animals depend on water
prompt: From last time: say the path water takes inside a plant, from the bottom to the top.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: paudhe ke andar paani neeche se upar kaunsa raasta leta hai?
answer: Roots, then stem, then leaves.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: Name two places where a river can begin its journey.
prompt_hi: Do jagah batao jahaan se koi nadi apna safar shuru kar sakti hai.
answer: A melting glacier, a spring coming out of the ground, a lake, or rain water collecting on hills and mountains.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: What do we call a smaller river that joins a bigger river?
prompt_hi: Jo chhoti nadi kisi badi nadi mein aakar milti hai, use kya kehte hain?
answer: A tributary.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: Outdoors, make a small hill of sand or soil in a tray or on the ground and slowly pour a mug of water on its top. Predict: which way will the water go, and what will it carry with it?
prompt_hi: Bahar ek tray mein ya zameen pe ret ya mitti ka chhota pahad banao, aur uski choti pe dheere-dheere ek mug paani daalo. Guess karo: paani kis taraf jayega, aur apne saath kya le jayega?
answer: The water runs down the slopes from the top to the bottom, making little channels, and carries some sand or soil down with it, which collects at the bottom.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: A river rushes down a steep mountain and then reaches flat plains. Predict: in the plains, will it flow faster or slower, and what will happen to the mud it is carrying?
prompt_hi: Ek nadi oonche pahad se tezi se neeche aati hai aur phir samatal maidaan mein pahunchti hai. Guess karo: maidaan mein woh tez bahegi ya dheere, aur jo mitti woh saath laa rahi hai uska kya hoga?
answer: Slower. As it slows down, it drops the fine mud and sand (silt) it was carrying, which makes the land in the plains fertile.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: The Narmada starts at Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and ends in the Arabian Sea in Gujarat. Using what you know about where the Arabian Sea is, predict: does it flow towards the east or the west? Then check on a map.
prompt_hi: Narmada Madhya Pradesh ke Amarkantak se shuru hoti hai aur Gujarat mein Arabian Sea mein milti hai. Arabian Sea kahaan hai, ye yaad karke guess karo: woh east ki taraf behti hai ya west ki taraf? Phir map pe check karo.
answer: Towards the west, because the Arabian Sea is on India's west side and the river flows from higher land down to that sea.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: The Ganga flows into the sea every day. Why does it not run out of water?
prompt_hi: Ganga roz samudra mein behti hai. Phir uska paani khatam kyon nahi hota?
answer: Rain and melting snow and glacier ice in the Himalayas keep feeding it, and tributaries add more. Water from the sea evaporates and comes back as rain, so it is a cycle.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: Why have so many big towns and cities, like Varanasi, Patna and Rajahmundry, grown up on river banks?
prompt_hi: Varanasi, Patna aur Rajahmundry jaise kai bade shehar nadi ke kinaare hi kyon base hain?
answer: Rivers give water for drinking and farming, fertile soil, fish, and a way to travel and trade.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: Compare a river high in the mountains with the same river near the sea. Think about its speed, its width and the land around it.
prompt_hi: Pahadon mein behti nadi aur samudra ke paas wahi nadi, dono ki tulna karo. Uski raftaar, chaudai aur aas-paas ki zameen ke baare mein socho.
answer: In the mountains it is narrow, fast and rocky and cuts deep valleys. Near the sea it is wide and slow, flows over flat land, drops silt and may split into many channels (a delta).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: Is there a river, nala or stream near your town? Ask an elder where it begins and where it ends. Is the start higher or lower than the end?
prompt_hi: Tumhare shehar ke paas koi nadi, naala ya dhaara hai? Kisi bade se poochho ki woh kahaan se shuru hoti hai aur kahaan khatam. Shuru wali jagah oonchi hai ya khatam wali?
answer: The start is always higher than the end: it begins at a higher place such as hills, a spring or a lake, and ends in a lower place such as a bigger river, a lake or the sea.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: After heavy rain, water flows along the road outside your school and into a drain. How is this like a river's journey?
prompt_hi: Tez baarish ke baad school ke bahar sadak pe paani behta hai aur naali mein chala jaata hai. Ye kisi nadi ke safar jaisa kaise hai?
answer: The water flows downhill from higher to lower places; small streams join into bigger ones like tributaries; it carries mud and leaves; and it ends in a bigger drain or river, like a river reaching the sea.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: Draw a river's journey from a mountain to the sea. Label the source, a tributary, the plains with farms, and the mouth where it meets the sea.
prompt_hi: Pahad se samudra tak ek nadi ka safar banao. Label karo: source (udgam), ek tributary, kheton wale maidaan, aur mouth jahaan woh samudra se milti hai.
answer: Source at the top of the mountains; a tributary joining on the way; plains with farms and towns where the river is wide and slow; the mouth or delta at the sea; arrows pointing downhill towards the sea.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: Golu says: 'The sea is full of water, so it fills the rivers. Rivers start at the sea and flow up to the mountains.' Spot the mistake.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Samudra paani se bhara hai, isliye wahi nadiyon ko bharta hai. Nadiyaan samudra se shuru hokar pahadon tak jaati hain.' Galti pakdo.
answer: Water flows downhill, not uphill. Rivers start high in the hills or mountains and flow down into the sea; also, river water is fresh while sea water is salty.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: Explain to a friend from another country the journey of the Godavari: where it starts, which way it goes, and where it ends.
prompt_hi: Kisi doosre desh ke dost ko Godavari ka safar samjhao: kahaan se shuru hoti hai, kis taraf jaati hai, aur kahaan khatam hoti hai.
answer: It starts in the hills near Trimbakeshwar in Nashik, Maharashtra; flows east across Maharashtra, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, joined by tributaries; slows down in the plains; and ends in the Bay of Bengal.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can trace the path of a river and how it changes the land and lives along it
prompt: From last time: does a river flow from high land to low land, or from low land to high land?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: nadi oonchi zameen se neechi zameen ki taraf behti hai, ya neechi se oonchi ki taraf?
answer: From high land to low land, downhill.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: Name two things that can cause a flood.
prompt_hi: Do cheezein batao jinse baadh aa sakti hai.
answer: Any two: very heavy rain, a river overflowing its banks, drains blocked with garbage, cutting forests, building on low land beside a river, sudden release of water from a dam.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: Name three things that make river water dirty.
prompt_hi: Teen cheezein batao jo nadi ke paani ko ganda karti hain.
answer: Any three: sewage or dirty drain water, factory waste, garbage and plastic, soap from washing clothes or animals, idols made of plaster of Paris with paint.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: Find a small slope in a park or garden with one grassy patch and one bare patch of soil. Pour one mug of water at the top of each. Predict: which patch will send down more muddy water, and faster?
prompt_hi: Park ya bageeche mein ek chhoti dhalaan dhoondho jahaan ek jagah ghaas ho aur ek jagah khaali mitti. Dono ke upar ek-ek mug paani daalo. Guess karo: kahaan se zyada aur jaldi matmaila paani neeche aayega?
