answer: The bare patch: water runs off quickly and carries mud. On the grassy patch, roots hold the soil and more water soaks in, so less muddy water comes down, and more slowly.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: Bury a banana peel and a plastic wrapper in a pot of damp soil. After three weeks, dig them up with a stick or spoon (and wash your hands after). Predict what each will look like.
prompt_hi: Geeli mitti wale gamle mein ek kele ka chhilka aur ek plastic ka wrapper daba do. Teen hafte baad lakdi ya chammach se nikaalo (aur baad mein haath dhona). Guess karo dono kaise dikhenge.
answer: The banana peel will be soft, dark and partly broken down by tiny living things (microbes); the plastic wrapper will look almost the same, because plastic does not rot.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: Put a lump of unbaked mitti (clay) and a small plastic toy in two buckets of water for two days. Predict: which one will soften and mix back into mud, and which one will stay as it is?
prompt_hi: Kachchi mitti ka ek dhela aur ek chhota plastic ka khilona do alag baaltiyon ke paani mein do din ke liye rakh do. Guess karo: kaun naram hokar mitti mein ghul jayega, aur kaun waisa hi rahega?
answer: The clay softens, crumbles and settles as mud, going back to nature; the plastic toy stays the same. This is why towns ask for idols made of natural clay.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: Why do hills that have lost their forests get floods and landslides more often in the monsoon?
prompt_hi: Jin pahadon ke jungle kat gaye hain, wahaan monsoon mein baadh aur landslide zyada kyon hote hain?
answer: Without tree roots to hold the soil and leaves to slow the rain, water rushes down quickly carrying soil, so rivers fill up fast and slopes slide.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: During heavy rain, muddy water is flowing fast across the road on your way home. What is the safe thing to do?
prompt_hi: Tez baarish mein ghar jaate waqt sadak pe matmaila paani tezi se beh raha hai. Sabse surakshit kya karna chahiye?
answer: Do not walk or wade into the flowing water; wait at a safe, higher place, tell or call an adult, and follow official warnings. Fast water can knock you over and hide open drains.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: Compare two families after a festival: Family A throws its flowers and plastic bags into the river; Family B puts the flowers in a compost pit and the plastic in the dry-waste bin. What happens to the river in each case?
prompt_hi: Tyohaar ke baad do families ki tulna karo: Family A apne phool aur plastic ki thailiyaan nadi mein phenk deti hai; Family B phoolon ko compost pit mein aur plastic ko sukhe kachre ke dibbe mein daalti hai. Dono baar nadi ka kya hota hai?
answer: With Family A, the plastic stays in the river and harms fish and animals, and large heaps of rotting flowers dirty the water. With Family B, the flowers become manure, the plastic can be recycled, and the river stays cleaner.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: Your colony is celebrating a festival in which idols are immersed. Suggest two ways to do it without harming the nearby lake.
prompt_hi: Tumhari colony mein ek tyohaar mein murtiyon ka visarjan hota hai. Paas ki jheel ko nuksaan pahunchaye bina ye karne ke do tareeke batao.
answer: Any two: use idols made of natural clay without harmful paints; immerse them in an artificial tank or a bucket at home; remove decorations, plastic and cloth before immersion.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: A town is built on low land right next to a river, and it floods every few years. If you were planning a new school there, what would you choose, and why?
prompt_hi: Ek shehar nadi ke bilkul paas neechi zameen pe basa hai aur har kuch saal mein wahaan baadh aati hai. Agar tumhe wahaan naya school banana ho, toh kya chunoge, aur kyon?
answer: Build it on higher ground away from the river's flood land, raise the floor, keep drains clear and plant trees around it, so flood water does not reach the classrooms.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: Draw a river passing a village, a factory and a town. Mark with arrows where dirt could enter the river, and draw one fix next to each place.
prompt_hi: Ek nadi banao jo ek gaon, ek factory aur ek shehar ke paas se guzarti hai. Teer se dikhao ki ganda kahaan se nadi mein ja sakta hai, aur har jagah ke paas ek ilaaj banao.
answer: Village: washing and garbage, fixed with dustbins and compost; factory: waste pipe, fixed by cleaning the waste before it is released; town: sewage drain, fixed with a sewage treatment plant, and plastic, fixed with bins and recycling.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: On a picnic, Chintu sees a stream and says, 'This water is so clear, it must be safe to drink!' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Picnic pe Chintu ek dhaara dekh ke kehta hai, 'Ye paani kitna saaf hai, ise toh seedha pee sakte hain!' Galti kya hai?
answer: Clear water can still have germs and harmful dissolved things we cannot see. Drink only water that is known to be safe, such as water your family has boiled or filtered.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: Explain to a younger child why cutting trees on hills can bring floods to towns far below.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki pahadon pe ped kaatne se door neeche ke shehron mein baadh kyon aa sakti hai.
answer: Tree roots hold the soil and help rain soak in. Without trees, rain rushes down fast with mud, rivers fill up and overflow downstream in the towns.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe causes of floods and river pollution and ways to reduce them
prompt: From last time: name one way your family can help keep a river or lake clean.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek tareeka batao jisse tumhari family kisi nadi ya jheel ko saaf rakhne mein madad kar sakti hai.
answer: Any one: no garbage or plastic in the water, clay idols or immersion tanks, composting festival flowers, not washing with soap in the river, using dustbins.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: What are microbes, and where can we find them?
prompt_hi: Microbes kya hote hain, aur ye kahaan-kahaan milte hain?
answer: Tiny living things too small to see with our eyes alone; we need a microscope. They are everywhere: in air, water and soil, on food and on our hands.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Name three signs that tell you food has spoiled, without tasting it.
prompt_hi: Bina chakhe, teen nishaaniyaan batao jinse pata chale ki khaana kharaab ho gaya hai.
answer: Any three: a bad or sour smell, slime, a change of colour, fuzzy mould spots, froth or bubbles.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Put a slice of bread into each of two zip bags. Sprinkle a few drops of water on one slice and leave the other dry. Seal both and keep them in a warm place for five days. Predict: which gets mould first? (Keep the bags sealed and throw them away sealed at the end.)
prompt_hi: Do zip wali thailiyon mein ek-ek bread slice rakho. Ek slice pe paani ki kuch boondein chhidko, doosri sukhi rehne do. Dono band karke paanch din garam jagah rakho. Guess karo: kis pe pehle phaphoond lagegi? (Thailiyaan band hi rakhna, aur aakhir mein band hi phenk dena.)
answer: The damp slice, because microbes such as mould grow faster where there is moisture and warmth.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Your family sets curd every evening. Predict: will it set faster on a hot May night or on a cold January night?
prompt_hi: Tumhare ghar mein roz shaam ko dahi jamaya jaata hai. Guess karo: garam May ki raat mein dahi jaldi jamega ya thandi January ki raat mein?
answer: On the hot May night. The helpful bacteria that turn milk into curd grow and work faster in warmth; in the cold they work slowly, so curd takes longer.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Imagine the same cooked dal left out on the kitchen counter, once on a hot summer afternoon and once on a cool winter day. Predict which one will smell sour first.
prompt_hi: Socho, wahi pakki hui daal kitchen ke counter pe chhod di gayi: ek baar garmi ki dopahar mein, ek baar thandi sardi ke din. Guess karo kaunsi daal pehle khatti badboo degi.
answer: The summer one; microbes grow much faster in warmth, so the dal spoils sooner, even though both are the same age.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Why does adding one spoon of old curd to lukewarm milk turn the whole bowl into curd overnight?
prompt_hi: Halke garam doodh mein ek chammach purana dahi daalne se poora katora raat bhar mein dahi kyon ban jaata hai?
answer: The spoon of curd contains helpful bacteria. In the warm milk they multiply and change the milk into curd.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Why do we cover food and wash our hands before eating?
prompt_hi: Hum khaana dhak ke kyon rakhte hain, aur khaane se pehle haath kyon dhote hain?
answer: To stop microbes from the air, from flies and from our hands getting onto the food; fewer microbes means the food stays fresh longer and we do not fall sick.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Idli batter rising overnight and milk going bad and smelly both happen because of microbes. So what is the difference?
prompt_hi: Raat bhar mein idli ka ghol phoolna aur doodh ka kharaab hokar badboo dena, dono microbes ki wajah se hote hain. Toh dono mein farak kya hai?
answer: In idli batter, helpful microbes ferment it the way we want: it rises and tastes good. In spoiled milk, unwanted microbes grow and make it smelly and unsafe. Some microbes help us and some harm us.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Your tiffin has rice and sabzi. On a hot day it sits in a closed bag until 4 pm. What could happen, and how could you prevent it?
prompt_hi: Tumhare tiffin mein chawal aur sabzi hai. Garmi ke din woh band bag mein shaam 4 baje tak pada rehta hai. Kya ho sakta hai, aur ise kaise roka ja sakta hai?
answer: Microbes could grow in the warmth and spoil the food. Eat it at lunch time, keep the bag in a cool, shady place, use a clean, dry box, and do not eat it if it smells sour.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Gardeners make compost from vegetable peels and leaves. What do microbes have to do with it?
prompt_hi: Maali sabzi ke chhilkon aur patton se compost banate hain. Ismein microbes ka kya kaam hai?
answer: Microbes such as bacteria and fungi, along with earthworms and insects, break the peels and leaves down into compost, a rich soil that feeds plants. Here microbes are helpful.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Draw what a damp slice of bread kept in a warm place might look like on day 1, day 3 and day 6. Write one line under each drawing.
prompt_hi: Garam jagah rakhi geeli bread slice din 1, din 3 aur din 6 pe kaisi dikhegi, uski drawing banao. Har drawing ke neeche ek line likho.
answer: Day 1: fresh, no spots. Day 3: a few small mould spots. Day 6: many fuzzy green, black or white patches spread over the slice, because the microbes keep growing and multiplying.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Bunty finds a fuzzy spot on a slice of bread. He says, 'I'll just pull off that bit and eat the rest.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Bunty ko bread ki slice pe ek roodaar dhabba milta hai. Woh kehta hai, 'Bas woh hissa tod ke baaki kha leta hoon.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Mould spreads tiny threads deep inside soft bread that we cannot see, so the whole slice, and maybe the rest of the packet, can be spoiled. Throw it away.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: Your little brother says, 'Germs are all bad. I wish there were no microbes at all!' Explain to him what microbes are, how they spoil food, and why some of them are our friends.
prompt_hi: Tumhara chhota bhai kehta hai, 'Saare germs bure hote hain. Kaash koi microbe hota hi nahi!' Use samjhao ki microbes kya hote hain, khaana kaise kharaab karte hain, aur kuch microbes hamare dost kyon hain.
answer: Microbes are tiny living things everywhere; some grow on warm, moist food and spoil it, but others are helpful: they make curd and idli batter and turn waste into compost.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain that tiny living things called microbes spoil food
prompt: From last time: name two things that help microbes grow fast on food.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: do cheezein batao jinse khaane pe microbes jaldi badhte hain.
answer: Warmth and moisture; leaving food open and touching it with dirty hands also help.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Name three ways families in India keep food from spoiling for a long time.
prompt_hi: Teen tareeke batao jinse India ki families khaane ko lambe samay tak kharaab hone se bachaati hain.
answer: Any three: sun-drying (papad, vadi, mango slices), pickling with salt and oil (achaar), sugar (murabba, jam), keeping it in a fridge or freezer, boiling milk, storing in airtight containers.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Match each method to its reason. Methods: drying, salting, fridge. Reasons: (a) slows microbes down with cold, (b) removes the water microbes need, (c) pulls water out and makes the food too salty for microbes.
prompt_hi: Har tareeke ko uski wajah se milao. Tareeke: sukhana, namak lagana, fridge. Wajah: (a) thand se microbes ko dheema karta hai, (b) woh paani hata deta hai jo microbes ko chahiye, (c) paani kheench leta hai aur khaane ko microbes ke liye bahut namkeen bana deta hai.
answer: Drying goes with (b), salting with (c), the fridge with (a).

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Ask an adult to cut two slices of cucumber. Sprinkle salt on one and leave the other plain. Predict: what will you see on the salted slice after 20 minutes?
prompt_hi: Kisi bade se kheere ki do slice katwao. Ek pe namak chhidko, doosri saadi rehne do. Guess karo: 20 minute baad namak wali slice pe kya dikhega?
answer: Water droplets come out on the salted slice and it turns soft and limp. Salt pulls water out of food, which is why salty food like achaar is hard for microbes to grow on.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Imagine two bowls of the same boiled milk: one kept in the fridge, one left out on a hot day. Predict which goes sour first, and whether the fridge one will last forever.
prompt_hi: Socho, ek hi ubale hue doodh ki do katoriyaan hain: ek fridge mein, ek garam din mein bahar. Guess karo kaunsi pehle khatti hogi, aur kya fridge wali hamesha theek rahegi?
answer: The one left out goes sour first, often within a day in summer. The fridge one lasts a few days but will also spoil in the end, because cold only slows microbes.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Fresh grapes and raisins (kishmish) are kept in two open bowls for a week. Predict which one spoils first, and why.
prompt_hi: Taaze angoor aur kishmish ko do khuli katoriyon mein ek hafte ke liye rakha. Guess karo kaun pehle kharaab hoga, aur kyon.
answer: The fresh grapes, because they have lots of water; raisins are dried grapes with little water, so microbes cannot grow easily on them.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Why is there a layer of oil on top of achaar in the jar?
prompt_hi: Achaar ke martaban mein upar tel ki parat kyon hoti hai?
answer: The oil covers the food and keeps air and moisture away, so microbes, especially mould, cannot easily grow on it; together with the salt it keeps the achaar good for months.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Why are papads and vadis dried in hot sun before they are stored?
prompt_hi: Papad aur vadiyaan rakhne se pehle tez dhoop mein kyon sukhaayi jaati hain?
answer: The sun dries the water out of them; without water microbes cannot grow, so the papads and vadis last for months.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Compare how your grandparents might have kept mangoes for the whole year with how a shop keeps mango juice in packets. What is the same idea behind both?
prompt_hi: Tumhare dada-dadi aam ko saal bhar kaise rakhte the, aur dukaan mango juice ko packet mein kaise rakhti hai, dono ki tulna karo. Dono ke peeche ek jaisa idea kya hai?
answer: Grandparents made achaar with salt and oil or aam papad dried in the sun; the shop's juice is heated and sealed in airtight packets, often with sugar. The same idea: stop microbes by removing water, adding salt or sugar, killing them with heat, or keeping air out.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Nani says, 'Always take achaar out with a dry spoon.' Why does this matter?
prompt_hi: Nani kehti hain, 'Achaar hamesha sukhe chammach se nikaalna.' Ye kyon zaroori hai?
answer: A wet or dirty spoon puts water and microbes into the jar, and the achaar can then grow mould.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Your family is going on a two-day train journey from Delhi to Chennai. Which foods would you pack so they do not spoil, and why?
prompt_hi: Tumhari family Delhi se Chennai do din ki train yatra pe ja rahi hai. Kaunsa khaana pack karoge jo kharaab na ho, aur kyon?
answer: Dry or low-water foods like thepla, mathri, laddoo, khakhra, roasted chana, dry fruits, achaar, and fruits with peels like bananas. Avoid curd rice, cut fruit, milk sweets and gravy dishes, which spoil quickly in warmth.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Make a table with three columns, food, method and why it works, for papad, mango achaar, milk and frozen peas.
prompt_hi: Teen column wali table banao: khaana, tareeka aur kyon kaam karta hai. Isme papad, aam ka achaar, doodh aur frozen matar bharo.
answer: Papad: sun-drying, removes water. Mango achaar: salt and oil, salt pulls water out and oil keeps air out. Milk: boiling and then the fridge, heat kills many microbes and cold slows the rest. Frozen peas: freezing, very cold stops microbes from growing.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Riya says, 'This paneer has been in the fridge for two weeks, so it's still fine. Fridge food never goes bad.' What would you tell her?
prompt_hi: Riya kehti hai, 'Ye paneer do hafte se fridge mein hai, toh abhi bhi theek hoga. Fridge ka khaana kabhi kharaab nahi hota.' Tum use kya bologe?
answer: The fridge only slows microbes, so after two weeks paneer can spoil. Check its smell, look and date; if in doubt, throw it out, and never taste it to check.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: Explain to a friend how three different methods, drying, salting and keeping in a fridge, all stop food from spoiling.
prompt_hi: Ek dost ko samjhao ki teen alag tareeke, sukhana, namak lagana aur fridge mein rakhna, kaise khaane ko kharaab hone se rokte hain.
answer: Microbes need water and warmth to grow. Drying removes water; salting pulls water out and makes food too salty; the fridge's cold slows microbes down.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe traditional and modern ways of preserving food
prompt: From last time: name one traditional and one modern way of preserving food.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: khaana bachaane ka ek purana aur ek naya tareeka batao.
answer: Traditional: sun-drying, salting, achaar, sugar or murabba. Modern: fridge, freezer, sealed packets or cans, packaged boiled milk.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: Sort these into wet and dry waste: banana peel, chips packet, used notebook paper, leftover rice, plastic bottle, used tea leaves.
prompt_hi: Inhe geela aur sukha kachra mein baanto: kele ka chhilka, chips ka packet, purane copy ke panne, bacha hua chawal, plastic ki bottle, use ki hui chai patti.
answer: Wet: banana peel, leftover rice, used tea leaves. Dry: chips packet, notebook paper, plastic bottle.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: Name three things students can do every day to keep their classroom clean.
prompt_hi: Teen kaam batao jo bachche roz apni class ko saaf rakhne ke liye kar sakte hain.
answer: Any three: put litter in the right bin, not scribble on walls or desks, keep their own place tidy, take turns on cleaning duty, not waste food.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: The school puts vegetable peels, dry leaves and one plastic spoon into a compost pit and covers it with soil. Predict what you will find when you dig it up after two months.
prompt_hi: School ne compost pit mein sabzi ke chhilke, sukhe patte aur ek plastic ka chammach daal ke mitti se dhak diya. Guess karo do mahine baad khodne pe kya milega.
answer: The peels and leaves will have broken down into dark, crumbly compost, helped by microbes and earthworms; the plastic spoon will still be there, unchanged.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: Put a small cup under a dripping school tap for ten minutes. Before you start, predict: will it collect just a few drops, a few spoonfuls, or a full cup? Then think: how much in a whole day, and in a whole week?
prompt_hi: School ke tapakte nal ke neeche das minute ke liye ek chhota cup rakho. Shuru karne se pehle guess karo: sirf kuch boondein jama hongi, kuch chammach bhar paani, ya poora cup? Phir socho: poore din mein kitna, aur poore hafte mein kitna?
answer: It depends on how fast the tap drips. At about one drop a second, ten minutes gives roughly 30 mL, a few spoonfuls, which is more than a few drops but less than a cup. Over a day that adds up to about 4 litres, and over a week to around 30 litres, a few buckets, so leaks must be reported and fixed.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: On a hot afternoon, predict: will the spot under a big neem tree or the open, sunny corner of the playground feel cooler? Go and stand in each for a minute to check.
prompt_hi: Garam dopahar mein guess karo: bade neem ke ped ke neeche wali jagah thandi lagegi ya playground ka khula dhoop wala kona? Dono jagah ek-ek minute khade hoke check karo.
answer: Under the tree. The tree gives shade, and its leaves give out water vapour, which cools the air around it.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: Why is it useful to keep wet and dry waste in separate bins?
prompt_hi: Geela aur sukha kachra alag-alag dibbon mein rakhna kyon faydemand hai?
answer: Wet waste can be turned into compost and dry waste like paper and plastic can be recycled. Mixed waste gets dirty and smelly, cannot easily be composted or recycled, and ends up in a dump.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: There are cleaning staff in your school. Why should students also help keep the school clean?
prompt_hi: School mein safai karne wale staff hain. Phir bhi bachchon ko school saaf rakhne mein madad kyon karni chahiye?
answer: The school belongs to all of us and we make most of the mess. If everyone avoids littering and tidies up after themselves, the school stays clean and healthy, and the staff's work becomes possible.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: Compare two school canteens: in one, all waste goes into one big drum; in the other, there are green and blue bins and a compost pit. What happens to the waste in each?
prompt_hi: Do school canteen ki tulna karo: ek mein saara kachra ek bade drum mein jaata hai; doosre mein hare aur neele dibbe aur ek compost pit hai. Dono jagah kachre ka kya hota hai?
answer: In the one-drum canteen, mixed waste smells, attracts flies and goes to a dump. In the other, wet waste becomes compost for the school garden and dry waste goes for recycling, so much less is thrown away.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: At home, which bin should these go in: potato peels, a broken plastic toy, old newspaper, leftover dal?
prompt_hi: Ghar pe ye kis dibbe mein jaayenge: aloo ke chhilke, toota hua plastic ka khilona, purana akhbaar, bachi hui daal?
answer: Green (wet): potato peels and leftover dal. Blue (dry): the broken plastic toy and the old newspaper.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: Your school has a big roof and runs short of water every summer. Suggest a plan to use the monsoon rain.
prompt_hi: Tumhare school ki chhat badi hai aur har garmi mein paani kam pad jaata hai. Monsoon ki baarish ka faayda uthane ka plan batao.
answer: Rainwater harvesting: collect roof rain through pipes into a covered tank, or lead it into a recharge pit so it soaks into the ground; use it for plants, cleaning and toilets. Keep tanks covered so mosquitoes cannot breed.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: Draw a map of your school. Mark where you would put green and blue bins, a compost pit, a garden, and any tap that leaks. Explain your choices.
prompt_hi: Apne school ka map banao. Dikhao ki hare aur neele dibbe, compost pit, bageecha, aur koi tapakta nal kahaan hai ya kahaan hona chahiye. Apni pasand ki wajah batao.
answer: Bins near the canteen and classrooms; the compost pit in a corner near the garden, away from classrooms and the drinking water tank; the garden in a sunny spot; leaking taps marked for repair.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: Pinky's poster says: 'Put plastic, peels and leaves into the compost pit. It turns everything into soil!' What should she fix?
prompt_hi: Pinky ke poster pe likha hai: 'Plastic, chhilke aur patte sab compost pit mein daalo. Woh sab kuch mitti bana deta hai!' Use kya theek karna chahiye?
answer: Only wet waste such as peels, food scraps and leaves breaks down into compost. Plastic does not rot; it must go into the dry-waste bin for recycling.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: Explain to a new student how your school stays clean, green and safe, and what they should do to help.
prompt_hi: Ek naye bachche ko samjhao ki tumhara school saaf, hara-bhara aur surakshit kaise rehta hai, aur use madad ke liye kya karna chahiye.
answer: It is everyone's job; sort waste into green (wet) and blue (dry) bins; wet waste becomes compost; close taps and report leaks; care for the plants; follow safety rules such as no running on stairs.

subject: evs
topic: A clean, green and safe school
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to keep the school clean, green and safe and manage its water and waste
prompt: From last time: which colour bin is for wet waste, and what can happen to that waste?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: geele kachre ke liye kis rang ka dibba hota hai, aur us kachre ka kya ho sakta hai?
answer: The green bin; the wet waste can become compost.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: What does each traffic light colour tell drivers: red, yellow and green?
prompt_hi: Traffic light ka har rang driver ko kya batata hai: laal, peela aur hara?
answer: Red: stop. Yellow (amber): slow down and get ready, the light is about to change. Green: go, if the way is clear.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: What is a zebra crossing, and why is it painted with white stripes?
prompt_hi: Zebra crossing kya hota hai, aur us pe safed dhaariyaan kyon bani hoti hain?
answer: It is the striped part of the road where people should cross; the bright stripes are easy for drivers to see, so they slow down and stop for people walking across.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: On a foggy winter morning, one child wears a dark jacket and another wears a light jacket with shiny reflective strips. Predict: which child will a driver see first?
prompt_hi: Kohre wali sardi ki subah ek bachche ne gehre rang ki jacket pehni hai aur doosre ne halke rang ki jacket jis pe chamakdaar reflective patti hai. Guess karo: driver ko pehle kaun dikhega?
answer: The child in the light jacket with reflective strips; dark clothes are hard to see in fog or darkness, while reflective strips shine in headlights.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: Imagine a big school bus parked at the roadside, and a child standing right behind it. Predict: can a car driver coming along the road see the child? Can the child see the car? (You can test it with a big box as the bus and a toy car, looking from the toy car's height.)
prompt_hi: Socho, sadak kinaare ek badi school bus khadi hai aur ek bachcha uske theek peeche khada hai. Guess karo: sadak pe aate car driver ko bachcha dikhega? Kya bachche ko car dikhegi? (Bade dabbe ko bus aur khilona car ko car maan ke, car ki oonchai se dekh ke check kar sakte ho.)
answer: No and no: the bus blocks the view both ways, so stepping out from behind it is very dangerous.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: In India, why do we look to the right first before crossing a road?
prompt_hi: India mein sadak paar karne se pehle hum pehle daayein (right) kyon dekhte hain?
answer: Vehicles drive on the left side of the road, so the traffic in the lane nearest to you comes from your right. We look right, then left, then right again because new traffic may have come.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: Why should you never put your hand or head out of the window of a moving school bus?
prompt_hi: Chalti school bus ki khidki se haath ya sir bahar kyon nahi nikaalna chahiye?
answer: Passing vehicles, poles, trees or walls can hit you, and the bus can move close to them suddenly.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: Two children at a signal: Aman crosses when the cars' light turns red and the green walking figure lights up. Bela crosses when the cars' light turns green. Who is right, and why?
prompt_hi: Signal pe do bachche: Aman tab paar karta hai jab gaadiyon ki batti laal hoti hai aur hara chalta hua aadmi jalta hai. Bela tab paar karti hai jab gaadiyon ki batti hari hoti hai. Kaun sahi hai, aur kyon?
answer: Aman. When the cars' light is red the cars stop, and the green walking figure shows it is safe for people. Bela is crossing just as the cars start moving, which is dangerous.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: There is no footpath on the road to your tuition class. Which side of the road should you walk on, and why?
prompt_hi: Tumhari tuition class ke raaste mein footpath nahi hai. Sadak ke kis taraf chalna chahiye, aur kyon?
answer: On the right edge of the road, facing the oncoming traffic, so you can see vehicles coming towards you and step aside; walk in single file.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: Your family visits a crowded mela with many roads around it, and you are holding your little cousin's hand. Make a safety plan for crossing roads and staying together.
prompt_hi: Tumhari family ek bheed wale mele mein jaati hai jiske aas-paas kai sadakein hain, aur tumne apne chhote cousin ka haath pakda hai. Sadak paar karne aur saath rehne ka safety plan banao.
answer: Hold hands all the time; agree on a meeting point if anyone gets separated; cross only at crossings or with an adult; stop and look right, left and right again; walk, don't run; know a parent's phone number; if lost, go to a police person or a uniformed helper.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: Draw a road near a school with a zebra crossing, a traffic signal and a footpath. Draw a child crossing safely, and mark with arrows where the child looks first, second and third.
prompt_hi: School ke paas ki ek sadak banao jismein zebra crossing, traffic signal aur footpath ho. Ek bachche ko surakshit sadak paar karte hue banao, aur teer se dikhao ki woh pehle, doosre aur teesre kahaan dekhta hai.
answer: The child stands at the footpath edge at the zebra crossing; arrow 1 points right, arrow 2 left, arrow 3 right again; the walking figure is green and the child crosses in a straight line.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: Rahul says, 'The safest way to cross a busy road is to run really fast, zig-zagging between the cars.' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Rahul kehta hai, 'Bheed wali sadak paar karne ka sabse surakshit tareeka hai bahut tez bhaagna, gaadiyon ke beech zig-zag karte hue.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Running and zig-zagging can make you trip or pop up suddenly in front of a driver who cannot stop in time. Cross at a zebra crossing, walk briskly in a straight line and keep looking.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: Teach your younger sibling the steps to cross a road safely on the way to school.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote bhai ya behen ko school jaate waqt surakshit sadak paar karne ke steps sikhao.
answer: Find a zebra crossing, overbridge or signal; stop at the edge; look right, left and right again and listen; cross when it is clear or the walking figure is green; walk straight without running and keep looking; never cross from behind a parked vehicle.

subject: evs
topic: Safety on the way to school
outcomes: Learner can follow road safety rules near the school
prompt: From last time: in which order do we look before crossing a road in India?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: India mein sadak paar karne se pehle kis kram mein dekhte hain?
answer: Right, then left, then right again.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: How do you say 'water' in your home language? Find out how to say it in two other Indian languages.
prompt_hi: Tumhari ghar ki bhaasha mein 'paani' ko kya kehte hain? Do aur Indian bhaashaon mein ise kya kehte hain, pata karo.
answer: Answers vary. Examples: Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi and Odia paani; Bengali jol; Assamese paani; Tamil thanneer; Telugu and Kannada neeru; Malayalam vellam.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: Match each dance to its state. Dances: Bharatanatyam, Bhangra, Bihu, Garba. States: Assam, Gujarat, Punjab, Tamil Nadu.
prompt_hi: Har nritya ko uske rajya se milao. Nritya: Bharatanatyam, Bhangra, Bihu, Garba. Rajya: Assam, Gujarat, Punjab, Tamil Nadu.
answer: Bharatanatyam: Tamil Nadu. Bhangra: Punjab. Bihu: Assam. Garba: Gujarat.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: Name the classical music tradition of north India and the one of south India.
prompt_hi: Uttar Bharat ki shastriya sangeet parampara aur Dakshin Bharat ki parampara ka naam batao.
answer: Hindustani music in the north and Carnatic music in the south.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: Guess first: out of every 10 people in India, how many have Hindi as their mother tongue: all 10, about 8, or about 4?
prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: India ke har 10 logon mein se kitno ki maatrubhaasha Hindi hai: saare 10, lagbhag 8, ya lagbhag 4?
answer: About 4 out of 10, a little less than half. Most Indians have another language as their mother tongue, although many also understand Hindi.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: Predict: does a rupee note show its value in just one or two languages, or in many? Then look at the back of a note and count the languages in the small panel.
prompt_hi: Guess karo: rupaye ke note pe uski keemat sirf ek-do bhaashaon mein likhi hoti hai, ya bahut saari bhaashaon mein? Phir note ke peeche ki chhoti patti dekh ke bhaashayein gino.
answer: Many. The language panel on the back shows the amount in 15 Indian languages, and Hindi and English appear on the note as well.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: Why do many Indians speak two or three languages?
prompt_hi: Bahut saare Indians do ya teen bhaashayein kyon bolte hain?
answer: They speak their home language, use the state's language or Hindi with neighbours, and learn English or Hindi at school or work; people moving between states and living together makes this useful.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: Compare Kathakali from Kerala with Bhangra from Punjab. How are they different, and what do they share?
prompt_hi: Kerala ke Kathakali aur Punjab ke Bhangra ki tulna karo. Dono mein kya farak hai, aur kya ek jaisa hai?
answer: Kathakali is a classical dance-drama with elaborate face make-up and costumes that tells stories through expressions and hand gestures, with drums. Bhangra is an energetic folk dance often linked with the harvest, danced to the dhol. Both use music and rhythm, celebrate or tell something, and are part of India's culture.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: Think of your class or colony. Ask three friends what language they speak at home. How many different languages did you find?
prompt_hi: Apni class ya colony ke baare mein socho. Teen doston se poochho ki woh ghar pe kaunsi bhaasha bolte hain. Kitni alag bhaashayein mili?
answer: Answers vary; usually more than one language turns up even in one class or colony, which shows India's variety close to home.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: A family from Assam moves to Pune. Name two ways they and their new neighbours could share and enjoy each other's culture.
prompt_hi: Assam ki ek family Pune shift hoti hai. Do tareeke batao jinse woh aur unke naye padosi ek doosre ki sanskriti baant aur enjoy kar sakein.
answer: Any two: share food such as Assamese pitha and Maharashtrian puran poli, invite each other to their festivals, learn a few words of Assamese and Marathi, teach each other dances like Bihu or Lavani, or songs.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: On an outline map of India, place these dances: Bihu, Garba, Bharatanatyam, Bhangra, Kathakali, Odissi. Tell me which part of India each is from.
prompt_hi: India ke khaali map pe ye nritya lagao: Bihu, Garba, Bharatanatyam, Bhangra, Kathakali, Odissi. Batao har ek India ke kis hisse se hai.
answer: Bihu: Assam, north-east. Garba: Gujarat, west. Bharatanatyam: Tamil Nadu, south. Bhangra: Punjab, north. Kathakali: Kerala, south-west. Odissi: Odisha, east.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: Golu says, 'Hindi is India's only language; everyone everywhere speaks it at home.' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai, 'Hindi India ki ikloti bhaasha hai; har jagah sab log ghar pe yahi bolte hain.' Galti kya hai?
answer: India has many languages: the Constitution lists 22 and hundreds more are spoken. Most Indians speak a different language at home, such as Tamil, Bengali, Marathi or Telugu, though many also understand Hindi.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: A child from another country asks you, 'What is India like?' Tell her about India's languages, music and dances in a way that shows how varied it is.
prompt_hi: Doosre desh ka ek bachcha tumse poochhta hai, 'India kaisa hai?' Use India ki bhaashaon, sangeet aur nrityon ke baare mein aise batao ki pata chale India kitna rang-birangi hai.
answer: Many languages (22 in the Constitution, hundreds spoken; Hindi is the most spoken but most people have another mother tongue); dances such as Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, Odissi, Bihu, Garba and Bhangra; Hindustani and Carnatic music; food changes by region; people share and respect each other's cultures.

subject: evs
topic: Languages, music and dances of India
outcomes: Learner can describe the diversity of languages, food and art across states
prompt: From last time: Garba is a dance from which state?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Garba kis rajya ka nritya hai?
answer: Gujarat.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: Name India's national animal, national bird and national flower.
prompt_hi: India ka rashtriya pashu, rashtriya pakshi aur rashtriya phool batao.
answer: The tiger, the peacock (Indian peafowl) and the lotus.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: What are the three colours of our national flag from top to bottom, and what is in the middle?
prompt_hi: Hamare rashtriya dhwaj ke teen rang upar se neeche kaunse hain, aur beech mein kya hai?
answer: Saffron at the top, white in the middle with a navy-blue Ashoka Chakra, and green at the bottom.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: Who wrote our national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana', and who wrote our national song 'Vande Mataram'?
prompt_hi: Hamara rashtriya gaan 'Jana Gana Mana' kisne likha, aur rashtriya geet 'Vande Mataram' kisne likha?
answer: Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana'; Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote 'Vande Mataram'.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: Before counting, guess: how many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra on our flag have: 12, 24 or 32? Then look closely at a flag or a picture and count.
prompt_hi: Ginne se pehle guess karo: hamare jhande ke Ashoka Chakra mein kitni teeliyaan hain: 12, 24 ya 32? Phir jhande ya photo ko dhyaan se dekh ke gino.
answer: 24 spokes.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: Look at the emblem on a coin or a rupee note and count the lions you can see. Now predict: how many lions were carved on the real Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath?
prompt_hi: Kisi sikke ya note pe bane emblem mein dikhne waale sher gino. Ab guess karo: Sarnath ke asli Ashoka stambh (Lion Capital) pe kitne sher bane the?
answer: Four lions sitting back to back. A flat picture shows only three because the fourth is hidden behind.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: What do the saffron, white and green bands and the Ashoka Chakra on our flag stand for?
prompt_hi: Hamare jhande ki kesariya, safed aur hari patti aur Ashoka Chakra kis baat ke prateek hain?
answer: Saffron: courage and strength. White: peace and truth. Green: growth and the fertile land. The Ashoka Chakra: the wheel of law and moving forward.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: How is Independence Day (15 August) different from Republic Day (26 January)?
prompt_hi: Swatantrata Diwas (15 August) aur Ganatantra Diwas (26 January) mein kya farak hai?
answer: On 15 August 1947 India became free from British rule. On 26 January 1950 India's Constitution came into force and India became a republic that chooses its own leaders.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: Find the national emblem on something at home: a coin, a rupee note or a government letter. What words are written under the emblem, and what do they mean? (If you can't find them, look at a picture of the emblem.)
prompt_hi: Ghar pe kisi cheez pe rashtriya emblem dhoondho: sikka, note ya sarkari chitthi. Emblem ke neeche kya likha hai, aur uska matlab kya hai? (Na mile toh emblem ki photo dekho.)
answer: 'Satyameva Jayate', written in Devanagari script; it means 'Truth alone triumphs'.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: Your class needs a class monitor. Should the teacher pick the child whose elder sibling was monitor last year, or should the class vote? How is this like India being a republic?
prompt_hi: Class ko monitor chahiye. Kya teacher us bachche ko chune jiska bada bhai ya behen pichhle saal monitor tha, ya class vote kare? Ye India ke ganrajya hone jaisa kaise hai?
answer: The class should vote. In a republic, the people choose their leaders by voting; the job does not pass down in a family the way a king's throne does.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: Draw and colour the national flag correctly, and label what each colour and the chakra stand for.
prompt_hi: Rashtriya dhwaj sahi tareeke se banao aur rang bharo, aur label karo ki har rang aur chakra kis baat ka prateek hai.
answer: Three equal horizontal bands: saffron on top, white in the middle with a navy-blue 24-spoke chakra, green at the bottom; labels: courage and strength, peace and truth, growth and fertile land, wheel of law.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: Chintu says, 'Our national animal is the lion; that's why there are lions on the emblem!' What's the mix-up?
prompt_hi: Chintu kehta hai, 'Hamara rashtriya pashu sher (lion) hai, isliye emblem pe sher bane hain!' Gadbad kahaan hai?
answer: The national animal is the tiger. The lions on the emblem come from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath; they are part of the emblem, not the national animal.

subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify national symbols and explain what they stand for
prompt: Explain to a younger child what we celebrate on Republic Day, and name three national symbols with what they mean.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki Republic Day pe hum kya manaate hain, aur teen rashtriya prateek unke matlab ke saath batao.
answer: On 26 January 1950 India's Constitution came into force and India became a republic where people choose their leaders. Symbols: the flag (courage, peace, growth, wheel of law), the emblem (Satyameva Jayate, truth alone triumphs), the tiger, the peacock, the lotus, the anthem.

subject: evs

prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: India ka rashtriya vriksh kaunsa hai, aur rashtriya jaliya jeev kaunsa hai?
answer: The banyan tree and the Ganges river dolphin.

subject: evs

subject: evs
