prompt: Weigh a glass of water on a kitchen scale, then stir in two spoons of sugar until you cannot see it. Predict: will the weight go up, stay the same or go down?
prompt_hi: Kitchen ke taraazu pe paani ka glass tolo, phir do chammach cheeni ghol do jab tak dikhe nahi. Guess karo: wazan badhega, utna hi rahega ya ghatega?
answer: It goes up by the weight of the sugar; the sugar has dissolved but it is still in the water.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
prompt: Ask an adult to cut an apple into two pieces. Leave one piece open on a plate and dip the other in lemon water. Predict which one turns brown faster. Is browning a physical or a chemical change?
prompt_hi: Kisi bade se seb ke do tukde katwao. Ek tukda plate pe khula chhod do aur doosre ko nimbu-paani mein dubo do. Guess karo kaunsa jaldi bhoora hoga. Bhoora hona physical badlav hai ya chemical?
answer: The open piece turns brown faster. Browning is a chemical change: substances in the apple react with oxygen in the air to make new brown substances; lemon juice slows this.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
prompt: Tearing a sheet of paper cannot be undone, yet it is a physical change. Why?
prompt_hi: Kaagaz phaadna ulta nahi kiya ja sakta, phir bhi ye physical badlav hai. Kyon?
answer: No new substance is formed: the torn pieces are still paper. Whether a change can be reversed is only a clue; the real test is whether a new substance forms.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
prompt: Compare the melting of a candle's wax with the burning of its wick. Which is physical and which is chemical? Give evidence for each.
prompt_hi: Mombatti ke wax ke pighalne aur uski baati ke jalne ki tulna karo. Kaunsa physical hai aur kaunsa chemical? Dono ke liye saboot do.
answer: Melting wax is physical: the liquid wax cools back into solid wax. Burning is chemical: heat and light are given out, and new substances such as carbon dioxide, water vapour and soot form.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
prompt: Milk left out on a hot day turns sour and forms lumps. Is this a physical or a chemical change? What is your evidence?
prompt_hi: Garmi ke din bahar chhoda doodh khatta ho ke phat jaata hai. Ye physical badlav hai ya chemical? Tumhara saboot kya hai?
answer: Chemical: there is a new sour smell and taste and lumps form, and it cannot be turned back into fresh milk.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
prompt: Think of a festival kitchen while sweets are being made. Name one physical change and one chemical change that happen there.
prompt_hi: Socho tyohaar ke din kitchen mein mithai ban rahi hai. Wahaan hone wala ek physical badlav aur ek chemical badlav batao.
answer: Physical: sugar dissolving in water for the syrup, ghee melting, dough being rolled. Chemical: dough or besan turning golden-brown when fried or roasted, or milk being made into chenna or paneer with lemon juice.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
prompt: Kunal says, 'When I stir salt into water, the salt melts.' Which word should he use, and how is it different from melting?
prompt_hi: Kunal kehta hai, 'Jab main namak paani mein hilaata hoon, toh namak pighal jaata hai.' Use kaunsa shabd use karna chahiye, aur wo pighalne se alag kaise hai?
answer: Dissolves. Dissolving is the salt spreading into the water to form a solution; melting is a solid turning into a liquid by heating, and salt needs a temperature of about 800 °C to melt.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
prompt: Sort these into a two-circle chart, 'physical' and 'chemical': freezing water into ice, cooking rice, folding a paper boat, a banana ripening, dissolving salt, toasting bread, blowing up a balloon.
prompt_hi: Inhe do gole wale chart mein baanto, 'physical' aur 'chemical': paani ka barf banna, chawal pakaana, kaagaz ki naav banana, kele ka pakna, namak gholna, bread toast karna, gubbara phulaana.
answer: Physical: freezing water, folding a paper boat, dissolving salt, blowing up a balloon. Chemical: cooking rice, a banana ripening, toasting bread.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
prompt: Explain to a younger child how to tell a physical change from a chemical change, using two examples from the kitchen.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko kitchen ke do examples se samjhao ki physical aur chemical badlav mein farak kaise pehchaanein.
answer: Ask: has a new substance formed? If not, it is physical, like ice melting or sugar dissolving. If yes, with signs like a new colour, smell, gas, heat or light, it is chemical, like a roti browning or milk turning into curd.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
prompt: From last time: when water freezes in the freezer, is it a physical or a chemical change?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jab freezer mein paani jamta hai, toh ye physical badlav hai ya chemical?
answer: Physical: it is still water, only in the solid state.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Which gas from the air is needed for burning?
prompt_hi: Jalne ke liye hawa ki kaunsi gas zaroori hai?
answer: Oxygen.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Name the three things needed for a fire to burn.
prompt_hi: Aag jalne ke liye teen zaroori cheezein batao.
answer: Fuel, oxygen (air) and enough heat to reach the ignition temperature.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Think-only question; never try this yourself. In class, your teacher lights two identical candles and covers one with a small glass jar and the other with a big glass jar. Predict which flame goes out first, and why.
prompt_hi: Sirf sochne wala sawaal hai, ise khud kabhi try mat karna. Class mein teacher do ek jaisi mombattiyan jalaate hain aur ek ko chhote kaanch ke jar se aur doosri ko bade jar se dhak dete hain. Guess karo kaunsi lau pehle bujhegi, aur kyon?
answer: The one under the small jar goes out first, because it has less air, so its oxygen gets used up sooner.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Think-only question. A piece of wood is burnt completely inside a strong sealed box from which nothing can escape, and the whole box is weighed before and after. Predict: will the total mass go down, stay the same or go up?
prompt_hi: Sirf sochne wala sawaal. Lakdi ka ek tukda ek mazboot band dibbe mein poora jala diya jaata hai jahaan se kuch bhi bahar nahi nikal sakta, aur poore dibbe ko pehle aur baad mein tola jaata hai. Guess karo: kul wazan ghatega, utna hi rahega ya badhega?
answer: It stays the same: the wood and the oxygen it used turn into ash, smoke and gases that are all still inside the box; nothing is destroyed. In an open fire the gases escape, which is why the ash left behind is lighter.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Think-only question. In a science video, a paper cup full of water is held over a steady flame. Predict: will the paper cup catch fire before the water boils?
prompt_hi: Sirf sochne wala sawaal. Ek science video mein paani se bhara kaagaz ka cup ek sthir lau ke upar pakda jaata hai. Guess karo: kya paani ubalne se pehle kaagaz ka cup jal jaayega?
answer: No. The water keeps taking heat away from the paper, so the paper stays below its ignition temperature while there is water in it.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Why does fanning a sigri or a chulha make it burn more strongly?
prompt_hi: Sigri ya chulhe ko pankha jhalne se wo zyada tez kyon jalta hai?
answer: Fanning pushes more fresh, oxygen-rich air to the fuel, so it burns faster and gives more heat and light.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Why must water never be thrown on burning oil in a kadhai, or on an electrical fire?
prompt_hi: Kadhai ke jalte tel pe ya bijli ki aag pe kabhi paani kyon nahi daalna chahiye?
answer: Oil floats on water and the water turns to steam explosively, splashing burning oil and spreading the fire; water also conducts electricity and could give a shock. Adults should turn off the gas or power and cover the fire to cut off air.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Compare the rusting of an iron nail with the burning of a matchstick. Give one way they are the same and two ways they are different.
prompt_hi: Lohe ki keel ke jung lagne aur maachis ki teeli ke jalne ki tulna karo. Ek samaanta aur do farak batao.
answer: Same: both are chemical changes in which a substance combines with oxygen. Different: rusting is slow (days to weeks) and needs water, with no flame or light; burning is fast and gives out heat and light.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Why do petrol pumps keep buckets of sand, and why do firefighters cover some fires with foam?
prompt_hi: Petrol pump pe ret ki baaltiyan kyon rakhi jaati hain, aur fire-fighters kuch aag ko foam se kyon dhakte hain?
answer: Sand and foam cover the burning fuel and cut off its oxygen, so the fire goes out; water is not safe on burning petrol because petrol floats on water.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: In some states, farmers burn leftover crop straw (parali) in the fields. Using what you know about combustion, explain where the straw's matter goes and why cities far away get smoky air.
prompt_hi: Kuch rajyon mein kisaan khet mein bachi parali jalaate hain. Combustion ke baare mein jo jaante ho uske hisaab se samjhao ki parali ka padarth kahaan jaata hai aur door ke shehron ki hawa dhuaan-dhuaan kyon ho jaati hai.
answer: Burning turns the straw into carbon dioxide, water vapour, smoke particles and ash; the gases and smoke rise into the air and winds carry them to cities, where the smoke pollutes the air.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Pinky says, 'After a bonfire, the ash is so light, so most of the wood was destroyed into nothing.' What is the mistake?
prompt_hi: Pinky kehti hai, 'Alaav ke baad raakh itni halki hoti hai, matlab zyadatar lakdi khatam ho ke kuch nahi bachi.' Galti kya hai?
answer: The wood's matter was not destroyed; most of it turned into gases (carbon dioxide and water vapour) and smoke that went into the air. Only a small part was left as ash.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Draw a fire triangle and label its three sides. Next to each side, draw one way of removing it to put a fire out.
prompt_hi: Ek fire triangle banao aur uski teeno bhujaon pe label lagao. Har bhuja ke paas aag bujhaane ke liye use hataane ka ek tareeka banao.
answer: Fuel: remove the fuel, for example turn off the gas. Oxygen: cut off air with a lid, sand or a fire blanket. Heat: cool it with water (only for wood, paper or cloth fires).

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: Explain to a younger child what a fire needs to burn, why a fire goes out when it is covered, and why children must never play with fire.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki aag ko jalne ke liye kya chahiye, dhakne pe aag kyon bujh jaati hai, aur bachchon ko aag se kabhi kyon nahi khelna chahiye.
answer: A fire needs fuel, oxygen from the air and enough heat; covering it cuts off the oxygen so it goes out. Fire spreads fast and burns skin, so only adults should handle it.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
prompt: From last time: is burning a physical or a chemical change, and what does it give out?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jalna physical badlav hai ya chemical, aur isse kya nikalta hai?
answer: A chemical change; it gives out heat and light, and makes new substances such as carbon dioxide.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: What is weathering? Give one cause of it.
prompt_hi: Weathering kya hai? Iska ek kaaran batao.
answer: Weathering is the slow breaking down of rocks where they are; causes include heating and cooling, water freezing in cracks, plant roots growing into cracks, and rainwater.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: Name three things that can carry away broken rock and soil.
prompt_hi: Teen cheezein batao jo tooti chattan aur mitti ko bahaa ke le ja sakti hain.
answer: Any three of: flowing water (rivers and rain), wind, moving ice (glaciers), sea waves.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: Put a few small pieces of chalk, or a few sugar cubes, into a closed steel tiffin box or plastic bottle and shake it hard for three minutes. Predict what the pieces will look like and what you will find at the bottom.
prompt_hi: Chalk ke kuch chhote tukde, ya kuch sugar cubes, ek band steel ke tiffin ya plastic ki bottle mein daalo aur teen minute zor se hilaao. Guess karo tukde kaise dikhenge aur neeche kya milega.
answer: Their corners become rounded and they get smaller, and fine powder collects at the bottom, just as rocks become rounded pebbles and sand in a stream.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: Outdoors, make two small slopes of soil in trays: one bare, one covered with grass or a layer of leaves. Pour one mug of water slowly on each from the same height. Predict which slope loses more soil.
prompt_hi: Bahar do tray mein mitti ki do chhoti dhalaan banao: ek khaali, ek ghaas ya patton ki parat se dhaki. Har ek pe ek hi oonchai se dheere dheere ek mug paani daalo. Guess karo kaunsi dhalaan se zyada mitti bahegi.
answer: The bare slope loses more soil; the grass or leaves hold the soil and slow the water down.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: Fill a small plastic bottle completely with water, close it tightly, put it in a plastic bag and leave it in the freezer overnight. Predict what will happen to the bottle, and how this explains cracks in rocks on cold mountains.
prompt_hi: Ek chhoti plastic ki bottle ko poora paani se bharo, kas ke band karo, plastic ki thaili mein rakho aur raat bhar freezer mein chhod do. Guess karo bottle ka kya hoga, aur isse thande pahadon ki chattanon mein daraar kaise samajh aati hai.
answer: The bottle bulges or even splits, because water expands when it freezes. In rocks, water in cracks freezes and expands, pushing the cracks wider until pieces break off.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: Why are the pebbles in a mountain stream round and smooth, while rocks freshly broken from a cliff are sharp?
prompt_hi: Pahaadi nadi ke kankar gol aur chikne kyon hote hain, jabki chattan se abhi toote tukde nukile hote hain?
answer: As the stream carries the pebbles, they knock and rub against each other and the riverbed for a long time, wearing away their sharp edges; fresh pieces have not been rubbed yet.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: Compare: (A) in Rajasthan, hot days and cold nights make rock surfaces crack and peel; (B) wind blows sand across the Thar desert and piles it into dunes. Which is weathering and which is erosion?
prompt_hi: Tulna karo: (A) Rajasthan mein garam din aur thandi raatein chattanon ki sataha mein daraar daal ke chhilka utaar deti hain; (B) hawa Thar registaan mein ret uda ke tibbe bana deti hai. Kaunsa weathering hai aur kaunsa erosion?
answer: A is weathering (rock breaking where it is); B is erosion, with the wind carrying sand and dropping it in dunes.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: A peepal tree is growing out of a crack in an old wall. What will happen to the wall over many years, and what is this an example of?
prompt_hi: Ek purani deewar ki daraar se peepal ka ped ug raha hai. Kai saalon mein deewar ka kya hoga, aur ye kiska example hai?
answer: The roots grow thicker and push the crack wider until the wall breaks apart; this is weathering by plants.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: After forests on a hill are cut down, villages below see muddier rivers and more landslides. Explain this using erosion.
prompt_hi: Pahadi ke jungle kaatne ke baad neeche ke gaon mein nadiyaan zyada matmaili ho jaati hain aur zyada landslide hote hain. Erosion se ise samjhao.
answer: Tree roots hold the soil together and leaves slow the rain; without trees, rain erodes the soil quickly, rivers carry the mud downhill, and loosened slopes slide.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: Tushar says, 'Soil is easy to replace; if rain washes it away, new soil will form by next year.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Tushar kehta hai, 'Mitti ko badalna aasaan hai; agar baarish use bahaa le jaaye, toh agle saal tak nayi mitti ban jaayegi.' Kya galat hai?
answer: Soil forms very slowly from weathered rock and humus; a few centimetres can take hundreds of years, so lost soil cannot be replaced in a year.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: Draw a river's journey from the mountains to the sea in three parts. Label where you would find big sharp rocks, rounded pebbles, and fine sand and mud. Explain the pattern.
prompt_hi: Pahadon se samudra tak nadi ka safar teen hisson mein banao. Label karo ki bade nukile patthar, gol kankar, aur baarik ret aur keechad kahaan milenge. Pattern samjhao.
answer: Mountains: big sharp rocks, freshly broken. Middle: rounded pebbles, rubbed while being carried. Near the sea, on the plains and in the delta: fine sand and mud, dropped where the river slows (for example the Sundarbans delta).

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: Using the chalk-in-a-box experiment, explain to a friend how a mountain stream turns rocks into pebbles and sand.
prompt_hi: Chalk-in-a-box experiment ki madad se apne dost ko samjhao ki pahaadi nadi chattanon ko kankar aur ret mein kaise badal deti hai.
answer: Like the shaken chalk, rocks carried by a stream knock and rub against each other and the riverbed; over a long time their edges wear off, they get rounder and smaller, and finally break into sand.

subject: science
chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
prompt: From last time: name one thing that can break rocks without any people being involved.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek aisi cheez batao jo bina kisi insaan ke chattanon ko tod sakti hai.
answer: Any one of: water freezing in cracks, plant roots, heating and cooling, rainwater.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: What is the stage of life between childhood and adulthood called, and roughly what ages does it cover?
prompt_hi: Bachpan aur badappan ke beech ke jeevan ke daur ko kya kehte hain, aur ye lagbhag kis umar tak hota hai?
answer: Adolescence; roughly from 10 to 19 years of age.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: Name three physical changes that happen during adolescence.
prompt_hi: Adolescence ke dauraan hone wale teen shaaririk badlav batao.
answer: Any three of: a growth spurt in height, the voice getting deeper, new hair growth (for example in the underarms), more sweat and oil (body odour, pimples), changes in body shape, and periods starting in girls.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: On screen is a height chart of five friends from age 9 to 16, with the later years hidden. Before you see them, predict: will all five have their biggest growth jump in the same year?
prompt_hi: Screen pe paanch doston ka 9 se 16 saal tak ka height chart hai, aage ke saal chhupe hue hain. Dekhne se pehle guess karo: kya paanchon ki sabse badi lambai ki chhalaang ek hi saal mein hogi?
answer: No. Each friend has a growth spurt at a different age; girls often have it a little earlier than boys. Different timing is normal.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: Your height mark on the wall was 135 cm at age 10 and 137 cm at 11. Predict: will you keep growing only 2 cm a year until you are 18?
prompt_hi: Deewar pe tumhari lambai ka nishaan 10 saal pe 135 cm aur 11 saal pe 137 cm tha. Guess karo: kya tum 18 saal tak har saal sirf 2 cm hi badhoge?
answer: Probably not. During the adolescent growth spurt many people grow much faster, sometimes several centimetres in a year; afterwards growth slows and usually stops by the late teens.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: What causes the body to change during adolescence?
prompt_hi: Adolescence ke dauraan shareer mein badlav kis wajah se hote hain?
answer: Hormones: chemical messengers released into the blood that signal the body to grow and mature.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: Why do many adolescents notice more sweat and body odour, and what helps?
prompt_hi: Bahut se adolescents ko zyada paseena aur shareer ki gandh kyon mehsoos hoti hai, aur isme kya madad karta hai?
answer: Sweat glands become more active; bacteria on the skin act on sweat and cause the smell. A daily bath, washing the underarms, and clean clothes and socks help.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: Compare how the voice changes in boys and in girls during adolescence.
prompt_hi: Adolescence mein ladkon aur ladkiyon ki aawaaz kaise badalti hai, tulna karo.
answer: Both voices get deeper. In boys the voice box grows more, so the voice becomes much deeper, may crack for a while, and an Adam's apple may show; in girls the change is smaller and less noticeable.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: Two cousins, Priya and Arjun, are both 12. At a family wedding, Priya is taller than Arjun this year, though last year Arjun was taller. Is this normal? Why?
prompt_hi: Do cousins, Priya aur Arjun, dono 12 saal ke hain. Ek shaadi mein Priya is saal Arjun se lambi hai, jabki pichhle saal Arjun lamba tha. Kya ye normal hai? Kyon?
answer: Yes. Girls often begin their growth spurt earlier than boys, so they can be taller for a while; boys often catch up and grow later.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: A sports coach picks 12-year-olds for a team only by their height. Using what you know about adolescence, why might this be unfair?
prompt_hi: Ek sports coach 12 saal ke bachchon ko sirf unki lambai dekh ke team mein chunta hai. Adolescence ke baare mein jo jaante ho, uske hisaab se ye unfair kyon ho sakta hai?
answer: Children grow at different ages; a child who is short at 12 may grow a lot later. Height at 12 does not show final height or ability, so skill should be judged instead.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: Mohit says, 'Pimples come only from eating samosas, so if I stop eating them I'll never get pimples.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Mohit kehta hai, 'Pimples sirf samose khaane se hote hain, toh agar main samose band kar doon toh kabhi pimples nahi honge.' Kya galat hai?
answer: Pimples in adolescence happen mainly because hormones make the skin's oil glands more active and pores get blocked. Gentle face washing and a balanced diet can help, but no single food is the only cause.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: Draw a simple timeline from age 8 to 20. Mark roughly when the growth spurt often happens for many girls and for many boys, and when growth usually stops.
prompt_hi: 8 se 20 saal tak ki ek simple timeline banao. Lagbhag mark karo ki kai ladkiyon aur kai ladkon ki growth spurt aksar kab hoti hai, aur lambai badhna aam taur pe kab rukta hai.
answer: Many girls: roughly 10 to 13; many boys: roughly 12 to 15; growth usually stops in the late teens. These are rough ranges, and each person is different.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: Your younger cousin is worried because her friends have started growing faster than her. Explain to her why this is normal.
prompt_hi: Tumhari chhoti cousin pareshaan hai kyonki uske dost usse jaldi lambe hone lage hain. Use samjhao ki ye normal kyon hai.
answer: Everyone's body changes when its own hormones start the changes, which can be at different ages over several years; starting later is normal, and her growth spurt will come. She can ask a parent or doctor anything she wants to know.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
prompt: From last time: what are the chemical messengers that bring about the changes of adolescence called?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: adolescence ke badlav laane wale chemical messengers ko kya kehte hain?
answer: Hormones.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: Name two emotional changes that many people notice during adolescence.
prompt_hi: Do aise bhaavnaatmak badlav batao jo bahut log adolescence mein mehsoos karte hain.
answer: Any two of: quick mood changes, wanting more independence, caring more about looks, caring more about what friends think, feeling more sensitive or worried.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: Name three trusted people a student could talk to about worries while growing up.
prompt_hi: Teen aise bharosemand logon ke naam batao jinse ek student badhte waqt apni chintaon ke baare mein baat kar sakta hai.
answer: For example: a parent, a class teacher, a school counsellor, a doctor, an elder sibling or another trusted adult in the family.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: A class puts up an anonymous question box about growing up. Predict: will most questions be very different from each other, or will many students ask similar things? What does that tell you?
prompt_hi: Ek class mein badhne ke baare mein bina naam ka question box rakha gaya. Guess karo: zyadatar sawaal ek doosre se bilkul alag honge, ya bahut se students milte-julte sawaal poochhenge? Isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer: Many students will ask similar questions. Most people share the same worries, so nobody is alone and asking is normal.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: Predict: if someone keeps a worry completely to themselves for weeks, will it usually feel bigger or smaller over time? And what usually happens after they share it with a trusted adult?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar koi apni chinta hafton tak bilkul apne tak rakhe, toh samay ke saath wo aksar badi lagegi ya chhoti? Aur bharosemand bade se share karne ke baad aksar kya hota hai?
answer: Kept inside, a worry often feels bigger; after sharing it with a trusted adult it usually feels lighter, and together they can find a way to deal with it.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: Why is it normal to have strong or changing feelings during adolescence?
prompt_hi: Adolescence ke dauraan tez ya badalti bhaavnaayein hona normal kyon hai?
answer: Hormones and many big changes in the body, school and friendships all happen at once, and the brain is still developing; everyone goes through this.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: Why is it better to check information about growing up with a trusted adult, a doctor or a textbook rather than only with a friend or a random online video?
prompt_hi: Badhne ke baare mein jaankari kisi dost ya random online video ki bajaye bharosemand bade, doctor ya textbook se check karna kyon behtar hai?
answer: Friends and random videos can spread myths and wrong information; trusted adults, doctors and textbooks give correct and safe information.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: Compare two ways Kabir handles stress before exams: (A) staying up all night on his phone and skipping meals; (B) sleeping on time, playing for half an hour and talking to his elder sister. Which helps more, and why?
prompt_hi: Exam se pehle tension sambhaalne ke Kabir ke do tareekon ki tulna karo: (A) poori raat phone pe jaagna aur khaana chhodna; (B) time pe sona, aadha ghanta khelna aur badi behen se baat karna. Kaunsa zyada madad karta hai, aur kyon?
answer: B, because sleep, physical activity and talking reduce stress and help the brain focus and remember; A makes tiredness, mood and concentration worse.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: Some friends dare Ishaan to try tobacco 'just once'. What is a healthy way for him to respond?
prompt_hi: Kuch dost Ishaan ko 'bas ek baar' tobacco try karne ki challenge dete hain. Uske liye accha jawaab kya hoga?
answer: Say no firmly, walk away or suggest doing something else, and tell a trusted adult if the pressure continues. Tobacco is harmful and addictive, and real friends respect a no.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: A friend tells you they have felt very sad for weeks and don't want to do anything. What could you do to help?
prompt_hi: Ek dost tumhe batata hai ki wo hafton se bahut udaas hai aur kuch karne ka mann nahi karta. Uski madad ke liye tum kya kar sakte ho?
answer: Listen kindly without making fun, encourage them to tell a trusted adult such as a parent, teacher or counsellor, and offer to go with them; if they seem unsafe, tell an adult straight away. Tele-MANAS (14416) and Childline (1098) are free helplines.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: Neel says, 'Talking about body changes is shameful; grown-up people never ask questions.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Neel kehta hai, 'Body changes ke baare mein baat karna sharm ki baat hai; samajhdaar log sawaal nahi poochhte.' Kya galat hai?
answer: These changes are natural and happen to everyone; asking trusted adults or doctors is a sensible, grown-up thing to do, and it prevents myths and worry.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: Draw a 'circle of trust' with yourself in the centre and at least four trusted people or places around you. Next to each, write one thing you could talk to them about.
prompt_hi: Ek 'circle of trust' banao jismein beech mein tum ho aur charon taraf kam se kam chaar bharosemand log ya jagah. Har ek ke paas likho ki unse kis baare mein baat kar sakte ho.
answer: For example: parent (body changes, worries); class teacher or school counsellor (school stress, bullying); doctor (health questions); elder sibling or cousin (friendships); Childline 1098 (if ever unsafe).

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: Explain to a younger cousin who is about to start Class 7 what kinds of feelings might change and who they can talk to.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko, jo Class 7 shuru karne wala hai, samjhao ki kaunsi bhaavnaayein badal sakti hain aur wo kisse baat kar sakta hai.
answer: Moods can change quickly, you may want more independence and care more about looks and friends; this is normal. Talk to parents, teachers, a counsellor or a doctor, and use sleep, play and hobbies to feel better.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
prompt: From last time: what number can a child in India call for free if they are in trouble or unsafe?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Bharat mein agar koi bachcha musibat mein ho ya surakshit na ho, toh wo kaunsa number free mein call kar sakta hai?
answer: Childline 1098 (and Tele-MANAS 14416 for emotional and mental health support).

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: Why do adolescents need more protein and calcium in their diet?
prompt_hi: Adolescents ko apne khaane mein zyada protein aur calcium ki zaroorat kyon hoti hai?
answer: For fast growth: protein builds muscles and other body parts, and calcium builds strong bones and teeth.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: Name three iron-rich foods that are common in Indian homes.
prompt_hi: Teen aise iron se bharpoor khaane batao jo Indian gharon mein aam hain.
answer: For example: spinach (palak), methi and other green leafy vegetables, jaggery (gur), chana, rajma, dates, bajra, and eggs for those who eat them.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: Two lunches have the same palak dal. One is eaten with a glass of lemon water, the other with a cup of tea. Predict which helps the body take in more iron.
prompt_hi: Do lunch mein ek jaisi palak dal hai. Ek ke saath nimbu-paani piya jaata hai, doosre ke saath ek cup chai. Guess karo kaunsa shareer ko zyada iron lene mein madad karega.
answer: The one with lemon water: vitamin C helps the body absorb iron, while substances in tea reduce iron absorption.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: Count your pulse while sitting quietly: count the beats at your wrist for 30 seconds and double it. Predict: after one minute of skipping or jumping on the spot, will it go up, go down or stay the same? Why?
prompt_hi: Shaanti se baith ke apni nabz gino: kalaai pe 30 second tak dhadkan gino aur do se guna karo. Guess karo: ek minute rassi koodne ya jagah pe uchhalne ke baad nabz badhegi, ghategi ya utni hi rahegi? Kyon?
answer: It goes up, because working muscles need more oxygen and food energy, so the heart pumps faster to deliver them.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: Predict which breakfast will keep you full and active longer until lunch: a packet of chips with a cola, or poha with peanuts and a glass of milk.
prompt_hi: Guess karo kaunsa nashta tumhe lunch tak zyada der bhara aur active rakhega: chips ka packet aur cola, ya moongfali wala poha aur ek glass doodh.
answer: Poha with peanuts and milk: it gives carbohydrates, protein and some fat that release energy steadily; chips and cola give a quick sugar rush, little nutrition, and hunger again soon.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: Why are adolescent girls in India at greater risk of anaemia, and what helps?
prompt_hi: Bharat mein kishor ladkiyon ko anaemia ka khatra zyada kyon hota hai, aur kya madad karta hai?
answer: They are growing fast and lose some blood during periods each month, so they need more iron. Iron-rich foods eaten with vitamin C, and iron tablets when a doctor or a school health programme gives them, help.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: Compare two routines: Raju bathes daily and changes his socks every day; Manu bathes every three days and wears the same socks. Who is more likely to have body odour and skin problems, and why?
prompt_hi: Do routine ki tulna karo: Raju roz nahaata hai aur roz moze badalta hai; Manu teen din mein ek baar nahaata hai aur wahi moze pehenta hai. Kisko shareer ki gandh aur skin ki pareshaani hone ki zyada sambhavna hai, aur kyon?
answer: Manu, because sweat builds up on his skin and socks and bacteria grow on it, causing odour and skin infections; Raju's daily washing removes the sweat and bacteria.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: Simran says, 'I'll skip lunch and dinner so I become fit fast.' What is the problem with her plan?
prompt_hi: Simran kehti hai, 'Main lunch aur dinner chhod doongi taaki jaldi fit ho jaaun.' Uske plan mein kya gadbad hai?
answer: Her growing body needs regular, balanced meals; skipping them makes her tired and weak, harms growth and concentration, and is not fitness. Fitness comes from balanced food, daily activity and good sleep.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: A vegetarian hostel serves rice, aloo sabzi and tea every day. Suggest two changes that would give the students more iron and protein.
prompt_hi: Ek shaakahari hostel mein roz chawal, aloo ki sabzi aur chai milti hai. Do aise badlav sujhao jisse students ko zyada iron aur protein mile.
answer: For example: add dal, chana or rajma for protein and iron; add green leafy vegetables like palak or methi with lemon; give milk, curd or paneer; serve tea away from meals; include millets like bajra or ragi.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: Design a one-day plan for a Class 7 student that fits in school, homework, play and sleep, and meets the needs of a growing body.
prompt_hi: Class 7 ke ek student ke liye ek din ka plan banao jismein school, homework, khelna aur sona sab ho, aur badhte shareer ki zaroorat poori ho.
answer: It should include three balanced meals and healthy snacks (with dal, vegetables, milk or curd, fruit), about an hour of active play, around 9 or more hours of sleep, a daily bath and brushing twice, and limited screen time.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: Draw a thali divided into parts showing what a growing adolescent's lunch should include. Label one food in each part and what it gives the body.
prompt_hi: Ek thaali banao jo hisson mein bati ho aur dikhaaye ki badhte adolescent ke lunch mein kya hona chahiye. Har hisse mein ek khaana aur wo shareer ko kya deta hai, label karo.
answer: For example: roti or rice (energy), dal, chana, paneer or egg (protein), green leafy sabzi (iron and vitamins), curd (calcium), salad or fruit (vitamins and fibre), and a glass of water.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: Explain to a younger cousin why personal hygiene becomes more important during adolescence, and give two habits to follow.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko samjhao ki adolescence mein saaf-safaai zyada zaroori kyon ho jaati hai, aur do aadatein batao.
answer: Sweat and oil glands become more active, so bacteria on sweaty skin cause body odour and skin problems. Habits: bathe daily, wear clean clothes and socks, wash the face gently, brush twice a day, and for girls change pads regularly during periods.

subject: science
chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
prompt: From last time: which fruits or vegetables help your body absorb iron from palak?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kaunse phal ya sabziyan palak ka iron shareer mein lene mein madad karte hain?
answer: Foods rich in vitamin C, such as lemon, amla, guava, orange or tomato.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: In which direction does heat always flow between two objects?
prompt_hi: Do cheezon ke beech garmi hamesha kis disha mein behti hai?
answer: From the hotter object to the colder one.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: Sort these into good and poor conductors of heat: steel spoon, wooden ladle, aluminium pan, plastic handle, woollen cloth, copper wire.
prompt_hi: Inhe garmi ke acche aur kharaab conductor mein baanto: steel ka chammach, lakdi ki karchhi, aluminium ka pan, plastic ka handle, oon ka kapda, copper ka taar.
answer: Good conductors: steel spoon, aluminium pan, copper wire. Poor conductors: wooden ladle, plastic handle, woollen cloth.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: Wrap one ice cube in a woollen sweater and leave another unwrapped on a plate in the same room. Predict which one will melt first.
prompt_hi: Ek barf ke tukde ko oon ke sweater mein lapeto aur doosre ko usi kamre mein plate pe khula chhodo. Guess karo kaunsa pehle pighlega.
answer: The unwrapped one melts first. The sweater does not make heat; the air trapped in it slows the room's heat from reaching the ice, so the wrapped one melts more slowly.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: Ask an adult to pour warm water (not boiling) into a mug. Stand a steel spoon, a plastic spoon and a wooden spoon in it. Predict: after two minutes, which handle will feel warmest?
prompt_hi: Kisi bade se mug mein garam (ubalta hua nahi) paani daalne ko kaho. Usme steel ka, plastic ka aur lakdi ka chammach khada karo. Guess karo: do minute baad kiska handle sabse garam lagega?
answer: The steel spoon's handle, because steel is a good conductor and passes heat up from the water quickly; plastic and wood are poor conductors.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: Place two equal ice cubes at the same moment: one on a steel plate and one on a wooden chopping board, both at room temperature. Predict which melts faster.
prompt_hi: Do barabar barf ke tukde ek hi samay rakho: ek steel ki plate pe aur ek lakdi ke chopping board pe, dono kamre ke taapmaan pe. Guess karo kaun jaldi pighlega.
answer: The one on the steel plate melts faster: steel conducts heat from the plate and the room into the ice much faster than wood does, even though steel feels colder to touch.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: Why are a kadhai and a tawa made of iron or aluminium, but their handles made of wood or plastic?
prompt_hi: Kadhai aur tawa lohe ya aluminium ke kyon hote hain, par unke handle lakdi ya plastic ke kyon?
answer: The metal conducts heat quickly from the flame to the food; wood and plastic are poor conductors, so the handle stays cool enough to hold.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: On a winter morning, the steel railing on the school stairs feels much colder than the wooden bench next to it. Why, if both are at the same temperature?
prompt_hi: Sardi ki subah school ki seedhiyon ki steel railing paas ki lakdi ki bench se bahut zyada thandi lagti hai. Agar dono ka taapmaan same hai, toh aisa kyon?
answer: Steel conducts heat away from your hand much faster than wood does, so your hand loses heat quickly and feels cold, even though both are at the same temperature.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: Compare a cotton shirt and a woollen sweater on a cold day. Why does the sweater keep you warmer, even though neither makes any heat?
prompt_hi: Thande din pe cotton ki shirt aur oon ke sweater ki tulna karo. Sweater zyada garam kyon rakhta hai, jabki dono mein se koi garmi nahi banata?
answer: The sweater's fluffy fibres trap much more air, and air is a poor conductor, so body heat escapes slowly; the thin cotton shirt traps little air.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: When you hold an ice-cream cone, your hand gets cold and the ice-cream starts melting. Describe which way heat is flowing.
prompt_hi: Jab tum ice-cream cone pakadte ho, haath thanda hota hai aur ice-cream pighalne lagti hai. Batao garmi kis taraf beh rahi hai.
answer: Heat flows from your warm hand (and the air) into the ice-cream; your hand loses heat and feels cold, and the ice-cream gains heat and melts.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: In winter, birds often fluff up their feathers. Using the idea of conduction, why does this help them stay warm?
prompt_hi: Sardi mein pakshi aksar apne pankh phula lete hain. Conduction ke idea se samjhao ki isse unhe garam rehne mein madad kyon milti hai.
answer: Fluffing up traps more air between the feathers; air is a poor conductor, so less body heat escapes.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: Ananya writes: 'The fridge puts cold into the food.' Correct the science.
prompt_hi: Ananya likhti hai: 'Fridge khaane mein thand daal deta hai.' Science ko sahi karo.
answer: The fridge takes heat out of the food: heat flows from the warmer food into the colder inside of the fridge, and the fridge pumps that heat outside, so the food cools.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: Draw a steel rod with one end dipped in a pot of hot water and three markers stuck along its length. Show with arrows how heat moves, and number the markers in the order they would warm up.
prompt_hi: Ek steel ki rod banao jiska ek sira garam paani ke bartan mein dooba ho aur uski lambaai pe teen marker lage hon. Teer se dikhao ki garmi kaise chalti hai, aur markers ko us kram mein number do jis kram mein wo garam honge.
answer: Arrows go from the end in the hot water along the rod towards the dry end. The marker nearest the hot water warms first (1), then the middle one (2), then the farthest one (3).

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: Explain to your grandfather why his steel tumbler of hot chai is hard to hold, but a kulhad (clay cup) is easy to hold.
prompt_hi: Apne daada ya naana ko samjhao ki garam chai wala steel ka gilaas pakadna mushkil kyon hota hai, par kulhad pakadna aasaan kyon.
answer: Steel is a good conductor, so heat flows quickly from the chai through the tumbler into his fingers; clay is a poor conductor, so the outside of the kulhad stays cooler.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
prompt: From last time: name one good conductor of heat and one poor conductor of heat.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: garmi ka ek accha conductor aur ek kharaab conductor batao.
answer: Good: a metal such as steel, copper, iron or aluminium. Poor: wood, plastic, wool, clay, cloth or air.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: What is the transfer of heat by the movement of a heated liquid or gas called?
prompt_hi: Garam liquid ya gas ke chalne se garmi ke pahunchne ko kya kehte hain?
answer: Convection.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: When does a sea breeze blow, in the day or at night, and in which direction?
prompt_hi: Sea breeze kab chalti hai, din mein ya raat mein, aur kis disha mein?
answer: During the day, from the sea towards the land.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: Freeze water with a few drops of food colour to make a coloured ice cube. Gently drop it into a clear glass of warm water. Predict where the coloured water will go as the ice melts.
prompt_hi: Paani mein khaane ka rang daal ke rangeen barf ka tukda jamaao. Use dheere se garam paani ke saaf glass mein daalo. Guess karo barf pighalne pe rangeen paani kahaan jaayega.
answer: The cold coloured water sinks to the bottom, because cold water is heavier (denser) than warm water; the warm water stays above. This sinking and rising is convection.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: A room has a window near the floor and a ventilator near the ceiling. On a hot day, predict which way air will move through each opening.
prompt_hi: Ek kamre mein zameen ke paas ek khidki hai aur chhat ke paas ek ventilator. Garam din pe guess karo har khule hisse se hawa kis taraf chalegi.
answer: Warm air rises and leaves through the ventilator near the ceiling; cooler air from outside comes in through the lower window.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: Predict: at 10 at night on a beach in Chennai, which way will the breeze near the ground blow, and why?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: Chennai ke beach pe raat 10 baje zameen ke paas hawa kis taraf chalegi, aur kyon?
answer: From the land towards the sea (a land breeze): at night the land cools faster than the sea, so the air over the warmer sea rises and cooler air from the land moves out to replace it.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: Why does all the water in a pot on the stove get hot, even though only the bottom of the pot touches the flame?
prompt_hi: Chulhe pe rakhe bartan ka saara paani garam kyon ho jaata hai, jabki sirf bartan ki tali aag ko chhooti hai?
answer: Water at the bottom warms, expands, becomes lighter and rises, while cooler water from the top sinks to be heated; these convection currents mix the heat through all the water.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: Why is an AC fitted high on the wall, while a room heater works best placed on the floor?
prompt_hi: AC deewar pe oonchaai pe kyon lagta hai, jabki room heater zameen pe rakhne pe sabse accha kaam karta hai?
answer: Cool air from the AC is heavier and sinks, spreading through the room; warm air from a heater on the floor rises and spreads upward, so both set up convection currents that mix the room's air.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: Compare how heat reaches your hand when (a) you hold it above a cup of hot tea, and (b) you touch the top of a steel spoon resting in hot tea. Name the way of heat transfer in each.
prompt_hi: Tulna karo ki garmi tumhare haath tak kaise pahunchti hai jab (a) tum haath garam chai ke cup ke upar rakhte ho, aur (b) garam chai mein rakhe steel ke chammach ka upar wala hissa chhoote ho. Har ek mein garmi pahunchne ka tareeka batao.
answer: (a) Mostly convection: warm air and steam rise up to your hand. (b) Conduction: heat travels through the metal of the spoon to your fingers.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: Fishermen in coastal Kerala often sail out to sea early in the morning and return in the afternoon. How could land and sea breezes help their sailboats?
prompt_hi: Kerala ke tatiya ilaakon ke machhuaare aksar subah jaldi samudra mein jaate hain aur dopahar ko laut-te hain. Land breeze aur sea breeze unki naav ki kaise madad kar sakti hai?
answer: The land breeze that blows from land to sea through the night and early morning helps push boats out; the afternoon sea breeze blowing from sea to land helps bring them back.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: Kitchen exhaust fans are fixed high on the wall, and many old houses had openings near the roof of the kitchen. Explain why.
prompt_hi: Kitchen ke exhaust fan deewar pe oonchaai pe lagte hain, aur kai purane gharon mein kitchen ki chhat ke paas khule hisse hote the. Kyon?
answer: Hot air, steam and smoke from cooking rise; openings high up let them escape, while cooler fresh air comes in lower down, keeping the kitchen cooler and less smoky.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: Dev says, 'Heat only moves up, so the floor next to a heater can't get warm.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Dev kehta hai, 'Garmi sirf upar jaati hai, isliye heater ke bagal ka farsh garam nahi ho sakta.' Kya galat hai?
answer: Heat flows from hot to cold in all directions; the heater warms things beside it and below it by radiation and conduction. Only the warm air rises by convection.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: Draw two pictures of a beach, one for the afternoon and one for the night. Use arrows to show air rising, sinking and moving across, and label which is the sea breeze and which is the land breeze.
prompt_hi: Beach ki do picture banao, ek dopahar ki aur ek raat ki. Teer se dikhao hawa kahaan upar uth rahi hai, kahaan neeche aa rahi hai aur kahaan aar-paar chal rahi hai, aur label karo kaunsi sea breeze hai aur kaunsi land breeze.
answer: Afternoon: air rises over the hot land, sinks over the cooler sea, and near the ground moves from sea to land (sea breeze). Night: air rises over the warmer sea, sinks over the cooler land, and near the ground moves from land to sea (land breeze).

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: Explain convection to a younger child using the coloured ice cube experiment.
prompt_hi: Rangeen barf wale experiment se ek chhote bachche ko convection samjhao.
answer: When the coloured ice melts, the cold coloured water sinks because it is heavier, and warmer water stays on top or rises; liquids and gases carry heat by moving like this, and that is convection.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
prompt: From last time: why does land heat up faster than the sea during the day?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: din mein zameen samudra se jaldi garam kyon hoti hai?
answer: Land (soil and rock) heats up and cools down faster than water, which needs much more heat to warm up and also mixes the heat deep down.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: How does heat from the Sun reach the Earth?
prompt_hi: Sun ki garmi Earth tak kaise pahunchti hai?
answer: By radiation.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: Which colour of clothes is better to wear on a hot summer afternoon, and why?
prompt_hi: Garmi ki dopahar mein kis rang ke kapde pehenna behtar hai, aur kyon?
answer: Light colours such as white, because they reflect more sunlight and absorb less heat.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: Take two identical steel tumblers with the same amount of water. Wrap one in black cloth and one in white cloth, and keep both in the sun for 30 minutes. Predict which water will be warmer.
prompt_hi: Barabar paani wale do ek jaise steel ke gilaas lo. Ek ko kaale kapde mein aur ek ko safed kapde mein lapeto, aur dono ko 30 minute dhoop mein rakho. Guess karo kiska paani zyada garam hoga.
answer: The water in the black-wrapped tumbler, because black cloth absorbs more of the Sun's radiation.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: Put one ice cube on a sheet of black paper and another on a sheet of white paper in the sun. Predict which melts first.
prompt_hi: Ek barf ka tukda kaale kaagaz pe aur doosra safed kaagaz pe dhoop mein rakho. Guess karo kaunsa pehle pighlega.
answer: The one on black paper, because the black paper absorbs more sunlight, warms up and passes heat into the ice.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: On a spacewalk, an astronaut's suit faces the Sun on one side. There is no air in space. Predict: will the side of the suit facing the Sun get hot?
prompt_hi: Spacewalk ke dauraan astronaut ke suit ka ek hissa Sun ki taraf hai. Space mein hawa nahi hai. Guess karo: kya suit ka Sun wala hissa garam hoga?
answer: Yes, very hot, because radiation travels through empty space; that is why spacesuits are white and reflective, to reflect much of it.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: Why is the inside of a solar cooker painted black, and why does it have a glass lid and a shiny reflector?
prompt_hi: Solar cooker ka andar ka hissa kaala kyon rang kiya jaata hai, aur usme kaanch ka dhakkan aur chamakdaar reflector kyon hota hai?
answer: Black absorbs as much sunlight as possible; the shiny reflector sends extra sunlight into the box; the glass lid lets sunlight in but traps the warm air so heat is not carried away.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: Compare two identical houses in Rajasthan, one with a white-painted roof and one with a dark roof. Which stays cooler inside, and why?
prompt_hi: Rajasthan ke do ek jaise gharon ki tulna karo, ek ki chhat safed rang ki aur ek ki gehre rang ki. Kaunsa andar se zyada thanda rahega, aur kyon?
answer: The house with the white roof, because the white surface reflects more sunlight and absorbs less heat.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: In Ladakh's cold but sunny winters, many people like dark-coloured woollens. Why?
prompt_hi: Ladakh ki thandi par dhoop wali sardiyon mein bahut log gehre rang ke oonee kapde pasand karte hain. Kyon?
answer: Dark colours absorb more sunlight and warm the wearer, and wool traps air that keeps the body's heat in.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: Why are petrol and oil storage tanks often painted white or silver?
prompt_hi: Petrol aur tel ke bade storage tank aksar safed ya silver rang ke kyon hote hain?
answer: To reflect sunlight and stay cooler, so the fuel inside does not heat up too much and evaporate or build up pressure.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: Lata writes: 'The Sun heats the air near it, and that hot air travels all the way to Earth.' What is the mistake?
prompt_hi: Lata likhti hai: 'Sun apne paas ki hawa ko garam karta hai, aur wo garam hawa Earth tak aati hai.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Space between the Sun and the Earth is almost empty, with no air to carry heat; the Sun's heat reaches us by radiation, which needs no material.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: Draw one kitchen scene that shows conduction, convection and radiation, and label each.
prompt_hi: Ek hi kitchen ka scene banao jismein conduction, convection aur radiation teeno dikhen, aur har ek pe label lagao.
answer: Conduction: heat passing through a tawa to a roti, or up a steel spoon in hot dal. Convection: hot water or steam rising in a pot. Radiation: warmth felt on your face standing beside (not over) the stove, or sunlight through the window.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: Explain to your younger sibling why her white school shirt feels cooler in the sun than her black jacket.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote bhai ya behen ko samjhao ki dhoop mein uski safed school shirt kaali jacket se thandi kyon lagti hai.
answer: The Sun's heat comes as radiation; white cloth reflects most of it while black cloth absorbs most of it and heats up, so the white shirt stays cooler.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: From last time: which way of heat transfer can work through empty space?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: garmi pahunchne ka kaunsa tareeka khaali space mein bhi kaam karta hai?
answer: Radiation.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
prompt: On a summer evening just after sunset, you stand close to a brick wall that was in the Sun all day. The air is still, yet your face feels warm from the wall. How is heat reaching you?
prompt_hi: Garmi ki shaam, sooraj doobne ke theek baad, tum ek eent ki deewar ke paas khade ho jo din bhar dhoop mein thi. Hawa ruki hui hai, phir bhi deewar se chehre pe garmi lagti hai. Garmi tum tak kaise pahunch rahi hai?
answer: Mostly by radiation: the warm wall, like every warm object (not just the Sun), gives out heat radiation, which travels straight to your face.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: Name the main steps of the water cycle.
prompt_hi: Jal chakra ke mukhya kadam batao.
answer: Evaporation (and transpiration from plants), condensation into clouds, precipitation as rain, snow or hail, and collection in rivers, seas and groundwater.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: What is groundwater, and what is the water table?
prompt_hi: Groundwater kya hota hai, aur water table kya hai?
answer: Groundwater is water stored in the tiny gaps in soil, sand, gravel and rock under the ground; the water table is the top level of the layer in which all those gaps are filled with water.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: Ask an adult to make a few small holes in the bottoms of three plastic cups. Fill one with gravel (small stones), one with sand and one with clay soil. Pour the same amount of water into each. Predict which lets the water through fastest and which slowest.
prompt_hi: Kisi bade se teen plastic ke cup ki tali mein kuch chhote chhed karwao. Ek mein bajri (chhote patthar), ek mein ret aur ek mein chikni mitti bharo. Har ek mein barabar paani daalo. Guess karo kaun paani sabse jaldi aur kaun sabse dheere nikaalega.
answer: Gravel fastest, then sand, and clay slowest, because bigger gaps between the pieces let water seep through faster.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: In a clear plastic bottle with its top cut off by an adult, make layers: gravel at the bottom, then sand, then soil. Pour water slowly on top. Predict where the water will collect and what it will look like.
prompt_hi: Ek saaf plastic ki bottle lo jiska upar ka hissa kisi bade ne kaat diya ho, aur usme parat banao: neeche bajri, phir ret, phir mitti. Upar se dheere dheere paani daalo. Guess karo paani kahaan ikattha hoga aur kaisa dikhega.
answer: It seeps down through the soil and sand and collects in the gaps between the stones at the bottom, filling the spaces, like an aquifer; no open lake forms.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: Two neighbourhoods get the same rain. One has open soil, gardens and trees; the other is fully covered with concrete and roads. Predict where groundwater will be refilled more, and where more water will flood the streets.
prompt_hi: Do mohallon mein ek jaisi baarish hoti hai. Ek mein khuli mitti, bageeche aur ped hain; doosra poora concrete aur sadkon se dhaka hai. Guess karo kahaan groundwater zyada bharega, aur kahaan sadkon pe zyada paani bharega.
answer: The open-soil neighbourhood refills more groundwater because rain soaks in; in the concrete one, rain runs off, floods the streets and very little reaches the groundwater.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: Why do many borewells go dry in summer?
prompt_hi: Kai borewell garmi mein kyon sookh jaate hain?
answer: There is no rain for months to recharge the groundwater, while people pump out more water for drinking and farming; the water table falls below the bottom of the borewell.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: Only with an adult beside you, and standing well back (never put your hand or face near the steam): look at a boiling kettle on the stove. Compare the clear gap right at the spout with the white mist a little above it. Which one is like a cloud, and why?
prompt_hi: Sirf kisi bade ke saath, aur door khade hokar (bhaap ke paas haath ya chehra bilkul mat le jaana): stove pe ubalti ketli ko dekho. Tonti ke theek paas ke saaf hisse aur thoda upar wali safed dhundh ki tulna karo. Inmein se baadal jaisa kaun hai, aur kyon?
answer: The white mist is like a cloud: it is made of tiny water droplets that formed when the invisible water vapour cooled and condensed. The clear part right at the spout is water vapour gas, which we cannot see.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: A school collects rainwater from its roof through pipes into a recharge pit filled with stones and sand. How does this help the school's borewell?
prompt_hi: Ek school apni chhat ka baarish ka paani pipe se patthar aur ret bhare recharge pit mein ikattha karta hai. Isse school ke borewell ko kaise madad milti hai?
answer: Instead of running off, the rainwater seeps through the pit into the ground, adding to the groundwater and raising the water table near the borewell.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: In parts of Punjab and Rajasthan, farmers now have to drill borewells much deeper than their grandparents' wells. Why might this be?
prompt_hi: Punjab aur Rajasthan ke kuch hisson mein kisaanon ko ab apne daada-pardaada ke kuon se kahin zyada gehre borewell khodne padte hain. Aisa kyon ho sakta hai?
answer: For years more groundwater has been pumped out, for example to irrigate thirsty crops, than rain has put back, so the water table has fallen deeper.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: Meenu's drawing shows a big blue lake in a cave under her village, labelled 'groundwater'. What would you change?
prompt_hi: Meenu ki drawing mein gaon ke neeche ek gufa mein bada neela taalab dikhaya gaya hai jis pe 'groundwater' likha hai. Tum kya badloge?
answer: Groundwater is mostly water filling the tiny gaps between grains of soil, sand and gravel and the cracks in rocks; she should draw layers of soil and rock with water in their spaces, with the water table as the top of the wet layer.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: Draw the water cycle as a loop with arrows linking the sea, the Sun, clouds, rain, a river, the soil, groundwater and a tree. Label each arrow with the right process.
prompt_hi: Jal chakra ko ek loop ke roop mein banao jismein teer samudra, Sun, baadal, baarish, nadi, mitti, groundwater aur ek ped ko jodein. Har teer pe sahi prakriya likho.
answer: Evaporation (sea to air), transpiration (tree to air), condensation (vapour to clouds), precipitation (clouds to land), runoff (land to river to sea), infiltration (soil to groundwater), and groundwater seeping into wells and rivers.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: Explain to your grandmother where the water in her village well comes from, and why the level rises after the monsoon.
prompt_hi: Apni daadi ya naani ko samjhao ki unke gaon ke kuen ka paani kahaan se aata hai, aur monsoon ke baad paani ka level kyon badh jaata hai.
answer: Rain seeps into the soil and fills the gaps in sand and rock underground; the well is dug below the water table, so groundwater seeps into it. The monsoon rain recharges the groundwater and raises the water table, so the well's level rises.

subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
prompt: From last time: what is it called when rainwater seeps down into the ground?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jab baarish ka paani zameen mein ris ke neeche jaata hai, use kya kehte hain?
answer: Infiltration.

subject: science
topic: Measuring time and the simple pendulum
outcomes: Learner can measure the time period of a pendulum and state the SI unit of time
prompt: What is the SI unit of time?
prompt_hi: Samay ki SI unit kya hai?
answer: The second (s).

subject: science
topic: Measuring time and the simple pendulum
outcomes: Learner can measure the time period of a pendulum and state the SI unit of time
prompt: A pendulum completes 20 oscillations in 30 seconds. What is its time period?
prompt_hi: Ek pendulum 30 second mein 20 oscillations poore karta hai. Uska time period kitna hai?
answer: 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5 seconds.

subject: science
topic: Measuring time and the simple pendulum
outcomes: Learner can measure the time period of a pendulum and state the SI unit of time
prompt: Tie a key to a 50 cm thread, hang it from a table edge and time 10 swings. Now tie two keys together on the same length of thread. Predict: will the time for 10 swings be shorter, longer or about the same?
prompt_hi: Ek chaabi ko 50 cm ke dhaage se baandho, mez ke kinaare se latkaao aur 10 jhoolon ka samay naapo. Ab do chaabiyan saath baandh ke wahi lambaai ka dhaaga rakho. Guess karo: 10 jhoolon ka samay kam hoga, zyada hoga ya lagbhag utna hi?
answer: About the same (around 14 seconds for 10 swings), because the bob's mass does not change the time period.

subject: science
topic: Measuring time and the simple pendulum
outcomes: Learner can measure the time period of a pendulum and state the SI unit of time
prompt: Now shorten the thread from 50 cm to 25 cm. Predict: will the pendulum swing faster or slower than before?
prompt_hi: Ab dhaage ko 50 cm se chhota karke 25 cm kar do. Guess karo: pendulum pehle se tez jhoolega ya dheere?
answer: Faster: a shorter pendulum has a shorter time period (about 1 second instead of about 1.4 seconds).

subject: science
topic: Measuring time and the simple pendulum
outcomes: Learner can measure the time period of a pendulum and state the SI unit of time
prompt: Predict: if you start the pendulum with a small pull versus a slightly bigger pull (still a small swing), will the time period change much?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar pendulum ko thoda sa kheench ke chhodo ya thoda zyada kheench ke (par abhi bhi chhota jhoola), toh kya time period mein zyada farak aayega?
answer: Hardly at all: for small swings the time period stays nearly the same, because on a bigger swing the bob also moves faster.

subject: science
topic: Measuring time and the simple pendulum
outcomes: Learner can measure the time period of a pendulum and state the SI unit of time
prompt: Why do we time 20 oscillations and divide by 20, instead of timing just one?
prompt_hi: Hum sirf ek oscillation ki jagah 20 oscillations ka samay naap ke 20 se bhaag kyon dete hain?
answer: One swing is too quick to time accurately because of our reaction time in starting and stopping the stopwatch; timing many swings spreads that error over all of them and gives a more accurate result.

subject: science
topic: Measuring time and the simple pendulum
outcomes: Learner can measure the time period of a pendulum and state the SI unit of time
prompt: Compare a sundial and a pendulum clock. What does each depend on, and when would each fail?
prompt_hi: Sundial aur pendulum ghadi ki tulna karo. Har ek kis cheez pe nirbhar hai, aur kab kaam nahi karega?
